News.title: Bournemouth thrash Milan to seal greatest win in club’s history
News.content:
Milan could not even point to being down to 10 men for the last hour as mitigation; long before, Bournemouth had treated the Rossoneri with contempt. When Ruben Amorim’s side trudged off, soaked and silenced, they had not mustered a single shot on target.

Few nights have better encapsulated the Premier League’s power. Bournemouth have never finished higher than last season’s sixth in the top flight of English football; AC Milan have won seven European Cups. But the Premier League’s financial clout is such that, each season, the bottom club earns more than the champions of Serie A.

The Premier League’s shared riches, allied to years of astute recruitment and management, have underpinned the Bournemouth’s ascent. Even Andoni Iraola’s departure has not stalled the progress at the Vitality Stadium; Marco Rose has relished the new European adventure.

Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz had already been toppled in Bournemouth’s first two European games. Now, Bournemouth have won their first three matches in Europe. Despite middling Premier League form, Rose’s ambitions will extend far beyond securing a berth in the knockout stages of the Europa League. On this evidence, Bournemouth are legitimate contenders to win the competition, and earn a berth in next season’s Champions League.

“It’s a special night for the club,” Ryan Christie, Bournemouth captain, said. “It’s mega – in terms of the story of the club, it’s ridiculous.”

Evanilson, perhaps, was Bournemouth’s standout player against AC Milan, combining intricate linkup play with a constant threat in front of goal. Centre-back Antonio Silva, controlling play from deep while marauding forward, also possessed a calmness that any of Milan’s beleaguered team lacked.

His side’s fate swiftly sealed, Amorim did not bother to summon Luka Modric or Christian Pulisic. Bournemouth’s own bench showed the depth that the club now possesses. Rayan showed off his trickery and directness; Adli – a substitute for substitute Alex Toth, who suffered a hamstring injury – then ensured that Bournemouth secured the margin of victory that their dominance deserved.

News.title: Harry Brook hits historic double century – but England still lose to Sri Lanka
News.content:
Good morning and welcome to the fourth match of the autumn tri-series in Pakistan. After two wins for the hosts, the two touring sides face each other for the first time in Rawalpindi, the last match here before the circus leaves for Lahore. England and Sri Lanka played each other only last month in this format, England winning at Chester-le-Street and the Oval by a distance, those victories sandwiching a narrow defeat at Headingley where, if you remember, Harry Brook’s side were cruising until Jos Buttler ripped his left hamstring. He did eventually come back out to bat on one leg as his rattled team-mates flapped and fell to Asitha Fernando, Dilshan Madushanka and Eshan Malinga.

On Tuesday against Pakistan, England again were flying with both ball and bat but they let the middle-order rebuild, losing control of the rate. Their two most experienced white-ball bowlers, Adil Rashid, who looked rusty after breaking his hand in August, and Sam Curran, who missed the end of August and all of September following groin surgery, went for 6.87 and eight runs an over respectively. Then, after a promising opening partnership, Ben Duckett top-edged a pull, Tom Banton flicked straight to midwicket and Will Jacks later fell in identical fashion when well-set to marshal the chase. Arafat Minhas ended up with six for 40, bowling Harry Brook with a beauty, and there will be more trial by spin today.

Although there was some talk of England failing in end-of-days Bazball fashion, it most reminded me of the teething troubles of Eoin Morgan’s side in 2015 and 2016 when they were experimenting with players, viz this Rose Bowl collapse. We have to acknowledge that Joe Root, the best player of spin, was undone by one that kept low from Naseem Shah and both Brook and Jordan Cox lost their wickets to very good deliveries from Arafat, a bowler, on a feast day. Dunith Welllalage will return to try to replicate his line of attack today but he is a bowler that England know well. He has had his days against them but they have also given him some tap in the past.

Sports.title: Record-breaking defender and former Leeds coach Barry Murphy dies aged 86 as tributes pour in for ‘true legend’
Sports.content:
Next

TRIBUTES have poured in for Barry Murphy after he died at the age of 86.

The defender was a record-breaker during his career, in which he spent 16 years at Barnsley.



Murphy became the club’s record appearance holder during his time with the Reds.

The full-back played a staggering 569 times for the club after joining from South Shields in 1962.



Murphy played his last game for the club against Torquay United at the age of 38 in April 1978.

After retiring from football, he went into coaching and worked with Barnsley until 1980.

That is when he made the move across Yorkshire to continue working with manager Allan Clarke at Leeds.

Murphy’s death was announced on social media by Barnsley with a touching statement.

It read: “We are heartbroken to announce the passing of Barry Murphy, aged 86.

“An iconic full-back who was our record-appearance holder with 569 games for the Reds.



“Barry was a true Barnsley legend. We will truly miss you, Barry. Once a Red, Always a Red.”

Fans have also paid tribute for the club legend as they flooded social media.

One posted: “What a true legend. To have to best away end in the EFL named after you still didn’t do him justice…. Rest easy Barry.”



A second commented: “RIP Barry. A true Barnsley legend.”

A third wrote: “RIP Barry, a true gent and legend at Barnsley FC, adored by the fans.”

A fourth said: “Sorry to hear, a true Barnsley legend a wonderful man.. RIP Barry.”

Another added: “The record will stand for a lifetime, it will never be surpassed. A true Barnsley Football Club legend. RIP Barry.”

Murphy left Leeds’ coaching staff in 1984 and after retiring he became a regular guest at Barnsley.



He was often a host for the club’s charitable events.

The 29-year-old has shared her excitement for “party season” as partner Ugarte prepares to spend Christmas on the United sidelines.



Georgia has shared a stunning video of herself modelling a series of dresses from Oh Polly.

She captioned the Instagram post: “Party season pending…”





The content creator first appeared standing in front of a bathroom mirror wearing a low-cut turquoise dress.

Her video then cut to the social media star showcasing her sideboob in a textured red dress, featuring a single thick strap over her right shoulder.

This was followed by Georgia posing in another red dress, this time featuring a silk skirt and a halterneck.

Finally, Georgia displayed a sparkling long-sleeve black dress, with lace detailing and a notable leg slit.



Georgia has built a strong social media fanbase, with more than 200,000 Instagram followers and counting after being previously linked with France’s Kylian Mbappe.

But Ugarte is yet to feature for United this season after suffering a serious knee injury while on duty for Uruguay during the 2026 World Cup.



Now Georgia is set to enjoy more time with her partner over the festive period as her fans share their love for her outfit choices.

Sports.title: Vincent Kompany to be out ‘for weeks’ after collapsing at training ground as Bayern Munich give update on boss
Sports.content:
Next

VINCENT KOMPANY could be out for weeks after collapsing at Bayern Munich’s training ground.

The manager is stable after his horrifying incident and has spoken to Bayern executive Max Eberl.



Kompany, 40, was rushed to hospital after collapsing at the Bundesliga giants’ training ground on Friday.

The incident occurred during the team’s second training session of the day.



The boss was airlifted to hospital after a helicopter had landed at Bayern’s Sabener Strasse base.

Eberl has confirmed that Kompany is “stable” but did admit that Kompany’s recovery may not be a swift one.

READ MORE ON FOOTBALL fame of two halves West Ham ace scores TWO from halfway in same game as fans left in shock



He said: “The good news is: He’s stable. I spoke with him last night, as well as with his wife.

“That was no pleasant moment for any of us; he collapsed on the pitch yesterday and will have to stay in the hospital for a few more days until everything has been checked and verified.

“This once again shows that health is the most important thing in life—not football.

“Therefore, the best wishes for a speedy recovery from all of us go out to him; we at FC Bayern stand together.



“The most important thing is that the cause is found and that he gets fit again. That he only comes back once he’s fit.

“Vinnie will be given all the time he needs. We’re not starting to build any timeframes.

“We need to figure out what it is, and then we’ll discuss what recovery time means.

“We won’t be talking about days, but weeks. We all understand that. And we have such a fantastic coaching staff, with Vinnie at its head.

“But the success is based on an outstanding team behind the scenes. There’s absolutely no thought of changing anything.



“All the guys who are here are outstanding – and therefore we can all approach the next few weeks in the spirit of Vinnie, which everyone has within them.”

Kompany had only been in the dugout just days earlier as Bayern drew 2-2 with Arsenal in the Champions League.

Assistant manager Aaron Danks has stated that Kompany will be kept away from football talk as much as possible.



He insisted that the manager will be left to focus on his “family and his recovery”.

Danks added: “We’re going to try and avoid as many football communication with him as possible.

“I’ll exchange messages with him on a care-friendly basis, but not so much a football basis.

“In terms of the game plan, in terms of the players and the team we’ll do all that together as a staff, we’ve got René Marić with me as one of the assistants.

“René’s tactical detail; his opposition analysis is really, really high level. And that’s the way him and Vince work together, so we’ll be using that and continuing that work moving forward.



“I promise you we’re going to do our best to avoid as many football conversations with Vince as possible, just allowing him his time to recover, be with the family, get himself better, get himself healthy.

“We’ll take care of the football for as long as we can, and we’ll use the players to help us, use all the staff to help us.

“And we’ll let Vince just focus on his family and his recovery.”

Sports.title: Man Utd manager contenders ‘have two major fears about dressing room’ after Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martinez rants

MANCHESTER UNITED’s dressing room is reportedly causing major fears among future managerial candidates.

Manager Michael Carrick is under huge pressure at Old Trafford after a shocking start to the season.



United have won just two games this season and are sitting in 13th place in the Premier League.

Europe has offered little comfort with a 4-1 hammering at the hands of Como in midweek, leaving the club 20th in the table.



This has sparked speculation that Carrick could be set for the sack at the club.

The likes of Antonio Conte, Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe have all been linked with the seat in the Old Trafford dugout.

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler has insisted he is focused on his work on the South Coast despite being a top target of United.

United could have an issue attracting managers to the job following outbursts by Lisandro Martinez and Bruno Fernandes.

“I always stayed fit since I came back from my injury, but people didn’t know that.

“They were like, ‘Why is he not playing?'”

Malacia was one of the marquee signings of Erik ten Hag‘s ill-fated reign at Old Trafford.



But his stay at the Theatre of Dreams was blighted by injury and he left the club this summer following the expiration of his contract, although he claims current United boss Michael Carrick prevented him from leaving sooner due to “the numbers in the squad”.

He explained: “I had a good conversation with Michael when he came. Obviously, I wanted to leave, then some injuries came so I couldn’t leave because of the numbers in the squad.

“That was difficult to accept. I was like ‘I’m not going to play but I’m not allowed to leave so what’s the point of me staying here’. Then he explained to me.

“At the end of the day everybody is there for themselves. I’m there for myself obviously in the first place and then obviously the team but also the manager is there for himself, he needs to save his job or do his job well.

The 27-year-old reckons Amorim didn’t give him a fair shake, saying: “Ruben came in when I just got back from my injury.



“He gave me a couple of games, but I had come back after a year and a half.

“Imagine not playing for a year and a half and adapting to everything, especially in the best league in the world and playing for such a big club. It takes time.

“As a player you need to understand if you play for a big club like Manchester United, sometimes you don’t get the time.”



Malacia left Old Trafford with only 50 appearances to his name, but insists: “I wouldn’t regret anything, not one bit.

“Even if I could do it over, I would do the same thing because otherwise I wouldn’t be the man I am now.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He added: “I don’t regret anything. I had a great time in my first season.

“And the people who worked there and the players I met there were amazing, so, nah, I really enjoyed my time.”

PRESTON FEARON stole the show with TWO goals from inside his own half in West Ham’s U21s clash against Burnley

The Hammers ran out 3-1 winners at Rush Green on Friday night thanks largely to the stunning efforts from the midfielder.



Fearon, 19, netted his first goal from range in the 35th minute after winning the ball off former Hammer Josh Cullen.

The starlet ran a couple of yards with the ball before unleashing his shot from the halfway line.



The ball flew over Burnley goalkeeper Lewis Forshaw and into the back of the net.

For most, one goal from halfway would be enough in a game, but Fearon went for it again in first-half injury time.

And he was successful as Cullen gave the ball away for a second time, and Fearon spotted Forshaw off his line again.

The midfielder went for the audacious effort yet again and yet again he was successful and left the stopper floored with the surprise effort.

Fearon had only just returned to West Ham after his three-month loan at Forest Green Rovers was cut short.

Sports.title: England crush France to remain in hunt for World Cup semi-final spot
Sports.content:
Herbie Farnworth scored a first-half hat-trick as England demolished France

England kept alive their faint hopes of reaching the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals with an 82-0 trouncing of France.

Herbie Farnworth and Dom Young scored hat-tricks as England overcame a nervy start in Perth to boost their scoring difference and remain in the hunt for a last-four spot heading into the final round of pool matches.

England entered the game staring at a 150-point deficit following Samoa's landslide win in Papua New Guinea earlier on Saturday. They took a sizeable chunk out of that with a 14-try victory but require another big win when they face the Kumuls in Wollongong on Friday, and will also need a favour from Tonga against Samoa on November 1.

Mikey Lewis came off the bench to score twice with Matty Ashton, George Williams, Victor Radley, Jez Litten, Jack Welsby and AJ Brimson also crossing for England while Hugo Savala kicked 26 points.

Brimson was the architect for many of those tries, the full-back shredding France in an awesome attacking display, with Junior Nsemba and Kai Pearce-Paul producing a number of eye-catching carries and offloads in contact.

Dom Young also bagged a hat-trick

England were met with stiff resistance during the opening quarter as some superb France defending kept them scoreless, but the dam burst on 23 minutes and those early efforts took its toll as they faded badly towards the end of the first half.

Brian McDermott's side scored six tries in the final 17 minutes of the first period, Farnworth grabbing three of those to help England into a 36-0 half-time lead.

The rout continued in the second half and France's persistence with going short from kick-offs led to a hat-trick try for Young on 62 minutes, while Brimson bagged the try his performance deserved with three minutes remaining.

Brimson shines for England

AJ Brimson starred at full-back

England full-back Brimson was deservedly named man of the match after a brilliant display that included a try, three assists and five line breaks.

He told Premier Sports: "It's my first win for England. Disappointing last week [against Tonga]. We had a tough assignment today, we needed a good performance to give ourselves a chance. It's not always easy having that mindset.

"The first 20 was a grind but credit to our spine and halves, keeping us calm and we knew we'd get them in the end."

McDermott hails 'enormous' effort

England head coach Brian McDermott:

"What we've done today, given the context, is just enormous. We had to win big but, as any coach will tell you, nobody thinks like that. You think, 'we've got to win'.

"We had some real good, candid conversations this week about what that actually means and we've been able to do that without getting distracted in chasing points.

"Everything was measured, everything was inside the game model, everything was what we planned to do - well, most of it at least.

"Whatever the results are next week, we want to finish strong against PNG [Papua New Guinea] as well, and if that means we're going home next Sunday night, that will be a big disappointment to us.

"But I'm not sure what more we could have done."

What's next?

England need another big win when they face Papua New Guinea in their final pool match in Wollongong on Friday (9.05am). Attention will then turn to Tonga vs Samoa on Sunday (9.05am), where they require a favour from the former.

Sports.title: England suffer 15-try defeat against rampant Australia
Sports.content:
Jocelyn Kelleher scored two tries and kicked nine goals against England

England were outclassed in a 78-0 defeat to defending champions Australia but remain in with a chance of reaching the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals.

Stuart Barrow's side shipped 15 tries on a unforgiving evening in Perth and must quickly regroup ahead of Friday's final pool match against Samoa, where the winner will advance to the last four.

England had no answer to a rampant Jillaroos, who dominated from the first whistle and kept a clean sheet for the second successive game. But they will be frustrated by the manner in which they gifted Australia territory and scoring opportunities during an error-strewn and ill-disciplined first half.

England's start was disastrous. They were caught offside from the kick-off and duly punished as Jaime Chapman opened the scoring, and another botched restart followed as Jenna Foubister kicked the ball straight into touch.

Australia aren't a side who require such easy access into the opposition half and they cut loose, scoring seven tries in a one-sided first half where their one negative was a suspected broken wrist suffered by Julia Robinson.

England also lost Eva Hunter to injury - the second rower could only watch on with ankle on ice as her team-mates fell to a heavy loss.

Jaime Chapman celebrates scoring the first of Australia's 15 tries

After conceding two early Chapman tries, England thought they had hit back when Anna Davies crossed in the corner. However, replays showed her knee was in touch before she grounded the ball.

That was as good as it got. With the excellent Tamika Upton returning kicks with interest and Jocelyn Kelleher combining with half-back partner Tarryn Aiken to devastating effect, Australia kept the scoreboard ticking over with regularity.

Kelleher scored twice with Isabelle Kelly and Abbi Church also dotting down to make it 36-0 at half-time.

The onslaught continued with Aiken, Olivia Kernick, Quincy Dodd all scoring within 10 minutes of the restart, before Church scored one of the tries of the game after Kelleher regathered her own grubber and combined with Upton to put the winger over.

Makenzie Weale, Tiani Penitani Gray, Kelly and Shayley Bent added further tries as Australia threatened to better the 90-4 victory over England in Las Vegas last year, but England refused to throw in the towel and popped up with some big defensive moments despite being under constant pressure.

Focus must quickly shift to Samoa but Barrow faces a challenge to lift his players.

What's next?

England play Samoa in their final pool fixture on Friday (6.05am), where victory in Wollongong will secure a semi-final place.

Sports.title: 'Like a mini World Cup' - Jacks sees positives in England's tri-series troubles
Sports.content:
Will Jacks intends to treat England's next two tri-series matches as a mini World Cup after defeats by Pakistan and Sri Lanka in their opening two matches boxed them into must-win territory.

England had looked set to bounce back from an 87-run hammering by Pakistan as Harry Brook's record-breaking 202 saw Sri Lanka set a massive 430 to win their match on Thursday, only for them to pull off a remarkable run chase on the penultimate ball.

The two-wicket defeat means England arrive in Lahore knowing they must beat both Pakistan on Sunday and then Sri Lanka on Thursday to give themselves a chance of of reaching the final on Saturday, October 31.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nasser Hussain and Mark Butcher describe Harry Brook as 'box office' after his record ODI innings against Sri Lanka.

Jacks pointed out that England were faced with a similar predicament en route to winning the 2019 World Cup and, looking ahead to 2027 edition in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, he views this next week as important preparation.

"It's my first tri-series and it replicates World Cup-style pressure." Jacks told the Press Association on Friday. "You can't replicate that in training or a bilateral series.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Brook reacts to his record-breaking double century in England's defeat to Sri Lanka, but insists the milestone means little after ending up on the losing side.

"In World Cups you have to bounce back, I remember in 2019 when England lost a couple of games in the group and they had to win their last two [against India and New Zealand] and they were able to do that to take the momentum forward [into the semi-finals].

"I'm not saying it's the same thing but it's a mini version of that and hopefully we can win on Sunday and move on. We have the opportunity to play in two must-win fixtures.

"Every game that we play is a stepping stone towards South Africa in 12 months' time. Sometimes you learn more in losses than you do in wins. There's always going to be bumps."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from England against Sri Lanka during their ODI tri-series game.

Jacks was part of a six-strong bowling group that was pummelled to all parts by Sri Lanka in Rawalpindi on Thursday.

Sam Curran, in his second match back after groin surgery, was the most experienced of the attack but ended up being the most expensive, conceding an eye-watering 103 from nine overs - the worst ever ODI figures by an England bowler.

Jacks said of Curran: "I've been through operations and it's always a bit tense playing your first few games and keeping your fingers crossed that your body holds up and you get into the game.

"They were incredibly hard conditions to bowl in for any bowler and he bowls a lot of pressure overs - that's his role in the team. He's been so successful with that for England over a number of years.

"There are some days where it doesn't quite work. If they're going to chase 430 then someone's going to have to get some tap, but it's more of a bowling unit problem that we lost that game."

While the bowling came under scrutiny, Jacks believes they found the "perfect batting template", with his close friend Brook recording the all-time fastest ODI double-hundred and the first by an England batter.

Image: The records broken by Harry Brook during his stunning ODI double hundred for England

Jacks, who was at the other end when Brook reached the milestone, added: "From when I went in, he was on 90, so to see him get to a hundred and then a double hundred - which we didn't even really think about until the last two overs - was amazing.

"He's someone I've played a lot of cricket with and to be at the other end and have the best seat was really special, I loved it."

Sports.title: Newey responds to Horner's 'abandon ship' criticism
Sports.content:
Adrian Newey suspects Christian Horner did not "fully understand" his "pain and frustration" during Red Bull's fallow years with Renault engines after criticism of him in the former team principal's new book.

Horner as team principal and Newey as technical chief worked together with huge success across 19 years at Red Bull, enjoying two periods of sustained title-winning form with first Sebastian Vettel in 2010-2013 and then Max Verstappen in 2021-2024.

But between those periods Red Bull took a back seat to Mercedes' dominance of the sport following the arrival of turbo-hybrid engines in 2014.

Red Bull initially continued to be powered by Renault, as in their four title-winning years under the previous rules era, but the French manufacturer struggled with the new regulations, which compromised the performance of the team's Newey-designed car.

Writing in his newly-released autobiography, Drive, Horner recounted a period mid-way through 2014 when he became disappointed in Newey after the legendary designer had received an offer to join Ferrari and was mulling whether to leave.

Horner wrote: "I stood behind him and believed that he stood behind me as well. But at the first sign of adversity, Adrian wanted to abandon ship. I felt very sad about that."

Horner added that, despite Newey's importance to the team, "I could no longer rely on him. Our partnership was not as solid as I had previously believed."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Christian Horner explains how he convinced Niki Lauda to sign Hamilton for Mercedes in 2012.

Horner's comments were put forward to Newey in Friday's team principals' press conference at the United States Grand Prix.

"You're quite right in saying that, no, I haven't read any of it [the book] yet," replied Newey.

"I think 2014, as a chassis designer, if the PU [Power Unit] manufacturer has a bad year, that happens and you accept it.

"If the PU manufacturer has a bad year and doesn't appear to have any intention of trying to address the problem, that's altogether a different matter and that's quite bleak at that point. And that's the situation that unfortunately we faced in 2014.

Image: Adrian Newey and Christian Horner on the Red Bull pit wall in 2014

"And as it turned out, that situation didn't really change with that supplier until we changed to Honda in 2019.

"So, you can imagine my pain and frustration at that. I don't think Christian fully understood that, perhaps. But I was in conversation."

Ultimately turning down Ferrari's offer in 2014, Newey signed a new contract to stay at Red Bull but began to split his time with other projects at the company outside of F1.

Newey stayed a further decade at Red Bull before leaving eventually in 2024 to join Aston Martin the following year, where he is team principal and managing technical partner.

Newey added: "The rest of it [in the book] I really can't comment, but Christian and I remain friends. As many of you know, I am godfather to his daughter Olivia, so, yeah."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Christian Horner explains the reasons behind why he left Red Bull Racing.

In interviews publicising his book, Horner said he saw similarities between Newey's current experience of trying to turn around a struggling Aston Martin team to their early years at Red Bull following the energy drink's buyout of an underachieving Jaguar outfit in 2005.

It was a comparison that Newey agreed with.

"I think there are actually a lot of parallels between when I started at Red Bull and when I've started at Aston Martin," said Newey.

"Both teams that through their history had had quite a lot of turmoil with changes of owners, changes of senior managers, etcetera.

"It's then really trying to, as we've spoken before, get everybody working together, try to break down silos, improve the culture. And that's been exactly the same again."

Speaking to Sky Sports News earlier this week, Horner said: "Adrian is without doubt the best designer that Formula 1 has ever seen. His track record speaks for itself.

"Lawrence [Stroll] is a very successful guy. He's a very driven guy and has obviously invested heavily in that team. Honestly, I think they've got their own journey that they're on, and it'll be interesting to see how it plays out."

Sports.title: Vincent Kompany to miss ‘weeks, not days’ with virus treatment, say Bayern Munich
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich expect Vincent Kompany to miss an extended period as their head coach continues his hospital treatment for a virus after collapsing on the training pitch on Friday. Speaking at a press conference on Saturday, Bayern’s sporting director, Max Eberl, confirmed Kompany was still in hospital in a stable condition.

Kompany’s English assistant coach, Aaron Danks, will replace the 40-year-old for Sunday’s Bundesliga match at Freiburg. Eberl said examinations were continuing to determine the nature of the former Manchester City and Belgium captain’s condition, with a recovery timeframe yet to be determined.

“Vinnie will be given all the time he needs. We’re not starting to put together any timeframes. We need to firstly figure out what it is and then we’ll discuss calmly what recovery time is to be. We won’t be talking about days, but weeks. We need to all be clear on that.”

Taking Saturday’s press conference in Kompany’s absence, Danks said he had spoken with the former centre-back briefly on Friday but only to wish him well. “I explained to him that we wouldn’t be having no football conversations. It was just checking in on his health and making sure he’s OK.”

Danks added: “All the football operations are in our hands and we’ll work together as a team to keep the club moving forward.”

Bayern’s second team’s game was postponed on Friday after Kompany’s collapse but Eberl said the club did not consider trying to postpone Sunday’s Bundesliga game. “I think the greatest joy for Vinnie would be for us to play well tomorrow and, ideally, get a positive result,” Eberl said. “That would probably be one of the best things we could do to help him recover.”

Danks confirmed the Germany captain, Joshua Kimmich, who has been on bereavement leave since Tuesday, would also miss Sunday’s game.

Kompany returned to the dugout for Wednesday’s home Champions League 2-2 draw with Arsenal despite missing the pre-match press conference due to the virus. Speaking after the Arsenal game, Kompany said his body reacted after he tried to push through the illness. “I caught a pretty nasty virus last week, and of course I didn’t listen to my body – and then at some point my body just said: ‘Enough is enough!’”
