Sports.title: Andy Ruiz vs Dave Allen Targeted For Spring
Sports.content:
Andy Ruiz Jr. and Dave Allen could meet in Sheffield in March or April 2027, with Allen revealing that Matchroom’s Frank Smith has told him the company is targeting that window for the heavyweight fight.

The Fight Wire reports Allen also indicated that he would likely retire afterward. The fight has not been officially announced, and the proposed dates remain a target.

Ruiz (35-3-1, 22 KOs) would enter the bout coming off a defeat against Damian Knyba in September. His last victory came against Luis Ortiz in September 2022, with a draw against Jarrell Miller and another lengthy absence between that win and the Knyba loss.

That represents a dismal drop for a man who battered Anthony Joshua to win the unified heavyweight crown in 2019. Ruiz held all the gold, dominated global sports headlines, and blew the chance to become a generational heavyweight star. He surrendered the titles in the rematch and spent the next seven years fighting just four times.

Allen keeps fighting to stay relevant and earn a living, but nobody expected him to rule the division. He has spent much of his career taking punishment from better heavyweights. Ruiz reached the top, won three world titles, and then wasted the opportunity.

A win over Allen gets Ruiz back in the win column, but beating a domestic trialhorse proves nothing about his ability to mix with elite heavyweights. An upset loss drops him off the boxing map entirely.

Take Allen’s retirement talk with a grain of salt. Sharing the ring with Ruiz hands him a big-name scalp to target along with a solid payday. Even in defeat, a decent showing will keep promoters dialing his number.

Expect Allen to stick around if matchmakers keep waving checks in his face. Giving a former unified champion a real scrap will open doors for future paydays, not push him into retirement.

Right now, the story is Matchroom penciling in that spring date in Sheffield. Calling it a farewell bout looks like wishful thinking, especially since another decent payday will easily tempt him back into the ring.

Sports.title: WBO Set To Strip Denzel Bentley Of Title
Sports.content:
Denzel Bentley is set to lose his WBO middleweight title after allowing the deadline to commit to mandatory challenger Yoenli Hernández to pass, leaving his November 7 fight against Shane Mosley Jr. as his next bout.

WBO president Gustavo Olivieri told EverythingBoxing’s Darshan Desai that the organization received no formal communication from Bentley’s team confirming he would go ahead with the Hernández defense within the allotted 24 hours. According to Desai, the WBO will now strip him.

Bentley has already signed to face Mosley Jr. in his Zuffa Boxing debut. That looks like a more winnable fight than defending against Hernández, although Bentley would enter it without the championship he had hoped to keep.

Hernández (11-0, 9 KOs) would be a dangerous fight for Bentley, with the power to knock him out. A loss like that would be a rough way to begin his time with Zuffa.

Bentley would have a chance against Hernández, but this would be a dangerous defense against a challenger who has been finishing most of his opponents. From a career standpoint, accepting the loss of his belt and going ahead with Mosley Jr. is understandable. He keeps his scheduled fight and avoids the immediate possibility of a punishing defeat.

The WBO cannot justify letting him keep the belt while pursuing a side attraction. Hernandez did the work to earn his mandatory ranking, and he shouldn’t be put on hold just because Bentley decided to take a different path.

Vito Mielnicki Jr. could step into the opposite corner against Hernandez for the vacant belt. Mielnicki holds the number two spot in the WBO ratings just behind the Cuban, positioning the American contender as the frontrunner if he accepts an invitation to fight for the strap. Sanctioning body officials have not made an official announcement regarding the pairing.

Bentley can still get off to a good start with Zuffa by beating Mosley, but he’ll be giving up his world title to take the easier fight.

Hernández would then get his shot at the vacant belt against someone prepared to face him.

Sports.title: Devin Haney Talks DAZN Benefits As Inactivity Continues
Sports.content:
Devin Haney credits DAZN with offering the opponents he needs to build his legacy. After 11 months outside the ring, however, he still needs a fight date to turn that explanation into something fans can judge.

Haney has not fought since beating Brian Norman Jr. last November. His DAZN agreement gives him a broadcasting home, but the next opponent and an official event announcement remain the real test of its value.

“All the opponents are on DAZN. Zuffa Boxing, they offered me a ton of money. I’m thankful for that,” Haney told Chris Mannix on DAZN. “I’m thankful for them to reach out to my team, but all the opponents are on DAZN. It’s not just about money for me. It’s about me being the best and me putting on the best fights.”

That is a reasonable explanation for choosing a platform. It is also a promise that requires action. Having potential opponents under the same broadcasting umbrella does not put their names on Haney’s record.

“I’m a legacy fighter. I love the money. The money is massive at DAZN as well. It’s great, but I need to have the opponents too to showcase my skills.”

Haney is getting paid well by his own account. The missing part is the opportunity to showcase those skills. Interviews can explain his intentions, but they cannot replace rounds, title defenses, or victories.

A unification with Liam Paro has reportedly been agreed, although an official announcement is still pending. Getting that fight scheduled would give Haney something concrete to support his comments. Until then, it remains another proposed contest following a lengthy absence.

The inactivity does not establish that Haney alone caused the delays. Negotiations require cooperation. Still, the time comes out of his career regardless of who holds up an agreement.

Prime years pass quickly. Haney can prefer DAZN and have sound reasons for doing so, but his legacy benefits when he fights. Right now, he is explaining what the platform can offer while fans wait to see it delivered.

Devin wants to make the BIGGEST fights happen! 🔥 #DAZNfighter https://t.co/FiGnjttNvf — DAZN Boxing (@DAZNBoxing) October 23, 2026

Sports.title: Rocky Marciano vs Mike Tyson: Speed Against Stamina
Sports.content:
Rocky Marciano against Mike Tyson would match relentless pressure against explosive speed. Both heavyweight champions could end a fight with one punch, but the deciding factor might be whether Marciano could survive Tyson’s early attacks and force him into a longer fight.

The comparison should involve both men at their best. Tyson’s late-career defeats tell us little about how the fighter who demolished Michael Spinks would have handled Marciano.

Tyson would have the advantages in hand speed and weight. Although similar in height, he generally fought substantially heavier than Marciano. His quick combinations to the body and head would present an immediate threat to a fighter who needed to get close to do his best work.

Marciano retired at 49-0 with 43 knockouts and six successful heavyweight title defenses. His unbeaten record did not mean he avoided trouble. Jersey Joe Walcott dropped him in the opening round and led on the scorecards before Marciano knocked him out in the 13th.

Against Ezzard Charles in their rematch, Marciano fought through a severe nose injury to secure an eighth-round knockout. Those victories demonstrated his ability to remain dangerous when a fight was going against him.

Tyson’s first championship reign showed how quickly he could take control. He stopped Trevor Berbick in two rounds to win the WBC title and later knocked out Pinklon Thomas, Tyrell Biggs, Larry Holmes, Tony Tubbs and Spinks. James “Bonecrusher” Smith and Tony Tucker took him the distance, with Tyson winning both fights on points.

Against Marciano, Tyson’s uppercuts would be particularly dangerous. Rocky often advanced from a low crouch, bringing him into range of short punches as he worked his way inside. Tyson could also attack the body before bringing his hooks upstairs.

Marciano’s answer would be to keep punching and deny Tyson comfortable breaks. He attacked the chest, shoulders, and arms when an opponent’s head was protected. Those punches could contribute to wearing Tyson down, although they would leave Marciano close enough to be countered.

Tyson’s peek-a-boo style was more than a stationary high guard. At his best, he used head movement and quick changes of angle to create openings. Marciano would have to deal with that movement before he could establish his own attack.

A longer fight would give Marciano more opportunities. His conditioning and sustained output were major strengths, particularly over 15 rounds. If he could survive the early combinations and continue forcing Tyson to work, his chances would improve.

That does not make an early Tyson knockout inevitable or a late Marciano victory automatic. Marciano could be dropped, while Tyson could win over the distance, as his victories over Smith and Tucker demonstrated.

Tyson would have the stronger chance of an early stoppage because of his speed, combinations, and greater size. Marciano’s best route would be to withstand that opening assault and turn the contest into a prolonged, punishing fight.

Would Tyson’s speed settle it early, or could Marciano survive and wear him down?

Sports.title: WBC World Title Bout Smith vs Puello
Sports.content:
In what will be his first title defense, the WBC super-lightweight world champion Dalton Smith will defend his title against the number one-ranked contender Alberto Puello.

Smith plans on having a successful homecoming while Puello wants to play the role of spoiler, as he looks to become a two-time world champion. The action is set to take place at Utilita Arena in Sheffield, England, live on DAZN.

The most notable victory on Alberto Puello’s record occurred in June 2024 when he outboxed Gary Antuanne Russell and won the vacant WBC Interim title. A short time later, Puello was elevated from Interim to full world champion.

Puello had one successful title defense, and then he lost his title to Subriel Matias. Now the Dominican boxer Alberto “La Avispa” Puello (25-1,11KOs) is ready to reclaim his WBC belt.

Back in January 2026, the British boxer Dalton Smith experienced his crowning moment.

During the course of four rounds, Smith stood inside the pocket and went toe-to-toe with Subriel Matias.

With 55 seconds left to go in the 5th round, Smith landed a hard overhand right that wobbled Matias. Seconds later, Smith connected with another overhand right that sent Matias down to the canvas.

A dazed Matias was able to stand up, but after witnessing him stumble, the referee stepped in and put a halt to the contest. With the victory, Smith won his first world title.

Now Dalton “Thunder” Smith (19-0, 14 KOs) plans to entertain his home fans while successfully defending his WBC belt. He faces a difficult task as the challenger is a very proficient opponent.

The southpaw Alberto Puello is a skilled technical counterpuncher who has a solid jab, he routinely utilizes lateral movement, he has good ring generalship, and a sharp straight left hand.

Dalton Smith is an aggressive boxer-puncher who has a high boxing IQ, good footwork, is an expert at controlling distance, is accurate, has good timing, and punching power.

Alberto Puello believes he’s well prepared for this fight, and on Saturday night he’s going to take back what belongs to him. Dalton Smith also feels he’s ready, and he’s going into this title bout in a particular mindset.

“I have prepared for this like I’m the challenger, and on Saturday night I will prove to the boxing world why I am No.1. I am cool, calm, collected, and I will do it again on Saturday,” Smith stated.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson’s Team Opens Talks With DAZN
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson is looking for a way back into the ring early next year, and manager Jay Prince is actively exploring options with DAZN. Prince insists that chasing a showdown with Devin Haney wasted valuable time, stalling Stevenson after promised fights failed to materialize.

While Prince confirmed dialogue with the streaming giant, nothing is locked down yet.

“We’re having conversations with quite a few people, and DAZN definitely is one of them,” Prince said to Fight Hub TV.

Prince explained that the split from Zuffa Boxing came down to fight delivery rather than money. Financial terms were settled, yet getting viable rivals into the ring proved impossible.

“We had a contract so the purses and different things were pretty much agreed upon. It’s just getting opponent,” Prince said.

According to Prince, several names were listed in the paperwork, but everything ground to a halt around Haney. Once those talks collapsed, Stevenson chose to cut his losses instead of idling.

“We no longer want to go down the road of focusing on this one guy, Devin, when there’s other things to do.”

Prince also shut down talk that Stevenson turned down a $7 million payday to face Rayo Valenzuela.

“Never was discussed with me. And if it was discussed, I would be the first to know,” Prince said.

That rebuttal dismisses rumors of an easy purse left on the table. Still, Prince gave little detail on why none of the other contracted names crossed the finish line.

He took aim at Haney over weight demands too, denying that a rehydration limit derailed the matchup.

“No dehydration clause. We agreed at 45, and Shakur was training for the fight.”

Prince claimed Bill Haney killed the deal by attempting to drag the contest up to 147 pounds, offering his side of an affair both camps view quite differently.

For now, the DAZN talks remain exploratory. Stevenson has a targeted window, but until an opponent signs on the dotted line, the layoff continues.

Sports.title: Richardson Hitchins Declares Keyshawn Davis Fight Off
Sports.content:
Richardson Hitchins says his proposed fight with Keyshawn Davis is off, claiming Davis demanded $6 million for a bout Hitchins had already agreed to nearly two months ago.

If that account is accurate, Davis has put a high price on an opportunity that could help him earn bigger purses. Beating Hitchins would give him something he cannot produce through callouts alone: a quality victory to strengthen his position in future negotiations.

“He was asking for 6ms to fight me,” Hitchins said on social media. “I been agreed to the fight going on 2 months. I was wondering what was the hold up.”

Hitchins also claimed Davis had never earned more than $1 million in boxing. That assertion and the alleged $6 million demand remain his account of the negotiations. The statement does not establish what Davis was offered, how the proposed purse was structured, or his side of the dispute.

Still, Hitchins has put an uncomfortable figure into public discussion. Davis now faces criticism over whether his asking price reflects what this particular fight can generate.

Davis is entitled to negotiate for the biggest purse available. Facing Hitchins is a serious undertaking, and neither fighter should be expected to accept whatever number gets placed in front of him. But the money has to come from someone willing to fund the event.

A competitive matchup does not automatically produce enough ticket sales or broadcast revenue to support every purse request. If Davis wanted $6 million, the people financing the fight would need a reason to believe that investment made sense.

That is where losing this opportunity could hurt him. Hitchins would offer Davis a chance to prove himself against a skilled opponent whose jab and boxing ability could force him to solve difficult rounds. A strong performance would give Davis more to sell the next time he asks for a major payday.

Instead, Hitchins is now telling fans he accepted while Davis priced himself out. That version gives Hitchins the better public argument until Davis provides his own explanation.

The immediate cost is a worthwhile fight slipping away. The longer Davis waits for a purse that satisfies him, the longer he goes without the victory that could make his next demand easier to justify.

Sports.title: Devin Haney Must Give DAZN Reasons To Celebrate
Sports.content:
Devin Haney needs to give DAZN more than victories if he wants the broadcaster to celebrate its investment. The WBO welterweight champion must produce performances that leave viewers wanting to watch his next fight.

Haney confirmed his partnership with DAZN on social media, promising big fights and plans to promote other fighters through Devin Haney Promotions.

Happy to announce the partnership with @DAZNBoxing! Looking to make the best fights & promote the best fighters in the world! InshaAllah 🤝 — Devin Haney (@Realdevinhaney) October 23, 2026

That sounds good on announcement day. Delivering entertainment once the bell rings is the harder part.

Wins over Jose Ramirez and Brian Norman Jr. did nothing to silence critics who find his style unwatchable. The excessive clinching, light jabs, and constant retreat got his hand raised, but they created long, dreary rounds that send casual fans looking for the remote.

DAZN can trumpet his belts across three weight classes all it wants. Glossy marketing only goes so far when the audience remembers spending twelve rounds waiting for a fight to break out.

A unification bout with IBF titleholder Liam Paro gives Haney another belt to collect, but it changes nothing if he falls back into his default mode. Nobody expects him to take foolish risks, yet there is a massive gap between smart defense and simply running out the clock behind a jab-and-grab routine. He needs to throw combinations, follow up when he lands, and stop killing the action with constant holding.

Belts look nice on digital flyers, but thrilling action is the only thing that sells subscriptions. As for his promotional ambitions, signing fighters means nothing until he actually secures dates and spends money on someone other than himself. Right now, his value begins and ends with what he produces in the ring, and if he keeps putting fans to sleep, DAZN will have an impossible task trying to sell his appearances.

Ghana News.title: Agitation at Bimbilla NDC elections as police arrest delegates over ballot photos
Ghana News.content:
Police have arrested some delegates at the Bimbilla constituency election centre for allegedly photographing their ballot papers during the National Democratic Congress (NDC) constituency elections.

The arrests triggered agitation at the polling centre as officers moved to prevent delegates from taking photographs of their votes.

The incident occurred as delegates voted to elect constituency executives for the governing party, raising concerns about maintaining order and calm during the exercise.

A total of 60 aspirants are contesting 17 executive positions in Bimbilla, with 1,764 delegates expected to cast their ballots.

The Bimbilla elections form part of the NDC’s nationwide constituency polls scheduled for October 24 and 25, 2026, across the party’s 276 constituencies.

Ghana News.title: Obuasi SHTS scandal: GES Director-General must resign – Former GNAT General Secretary
Ghana News.content:
Former General Secretary of the Ghana National Association of Teachers (GNAT), David Ofori Acheampong, has called for the resignation of the Director-General of the Ghana Education Service (GES) over the handling of sexual abuse allegations involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School.

Speaking on Asempa FM's Kukurantumi show on Saturday, October 24, Mr Ofori Acheampong argued that the GES leadership must take responsibility for the situation, which has raised serious concerns about student safety and accountability within the education sector.

"In my opinion, the Director-General of GES must resign and take responsibility for this situation," he stated.

He also questioned the response of the headmaster, who has reportedly claimed that eight teachers at the school conspired against him amid allegations of sexual misconduct involving 19 female students.

"How can a headmaster claim that eight teachers have plotted against him when he is facing allegations of having sexual relations with 19 female students?" he questioned.

Mr Ofori Acheampong further expressed concern about the motivation of some individuals entering the teaching profession, arguing that teaching should be regarded as a calling rather than merely an employment opportunity.

According to him, the limited availability of jobs in Ghana has compelled many people to pursue teaching primarily as a means of escaping unemployment, rather than out of a genuine commitment to educating and protecting children.

He maintained that teaching requires dedication, professionalism and a strong sense of responsibility towards students, particularly those entrusted to the care of school authorities.

His comments follow allegations of sexual abuse involving 19 female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School, brought to public attention through an investigative documentary by journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni.

Ghana News.title: Aggrieved NDC delegates invoke curses on party executives over alleged bloated register in Atwima Kwanwoma Constituency
Ghana News.content:
Some aggrieved delegates of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Atwima Kwanwoma Constituency of the Ashanti Region, who allege that their names have been removed from the party’s electoral register, have invoked curses on party executives over what they describe as their failure to address the issue.

Tension is mounting at Twedie, where the NDC constituency elections are taking place.

Some aggrieved delegates allege that the names of qualified delegates have been removed from the electoral register and replaced with those of persons they consider unqualified, purportedly to favour certain candidates in the elections.

The aggrieved delegates say they have repeatedly reported the matter to the party’s regional executives for resolution, but their concerns have allegedly not been addressed.

They claim the failure of the executives to intervene has left them with no option but to invoke the Antoa deity, calling for spiritual retribution against anyone found culpable in the alleged manipulation.

“We have poured libation and slaughtered sheep while invoking Antoa Nyamaa and other river deities to deal with those allegedly responsible for the disputed changes,” they said.

Speaking to the media, one of the aggrieved delegates, Gifty Kobbina, expressed frustration over the development, insisting that their sacrifices and commitment to the party should not be undermined by what they describe as an attempt to disenfranchise legitimate delegates.

“We have suffered for this party, and we will not allow anyone to cheat us. We are calling on Antoa to strike anyone who has a hand in this album manipulation,” she alleged.

The aggrieved delegates have warned that failure to resolve their concerns could undermine the credibility of the constituency elections and deepen divisions among party members.

Ghana News.title: Obuasi school scandal: NETRIGHT demands offenders’ register, annual GES reports on abuse cases
Ghana News.content:
The Convener of the Network for Women's Rights in Ghana (NETRIGHT), Professor Akosua Darkwah, has called on the Ghana Education Service (GES) to establish an offenders’ register and publish annual reports detailing sexual abuse cases reported in schools and how they were handled.

Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 24, Prof. Darkwah said the sexual abuse allegations involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School should serve as a turning point for the GES to review its child protection policies and strengthen enforcement.

She expressed concern that Ghana has numerous laws intended to protect children, but their implementation remains a major challenge.

"I would like to end on the GES and to ask that they use this as a reflection point and go back to their policies and enforcement because Ghana, we don't have trouble with passing laws," she stated.

Prof. Darkwah referenced Ghana's child protection legislation, arguing that the country's willingness to adopt laws has not always translated into effective measures to safeguard children.

"We sign nicely, then we go to sleep. I would like to see this be the point from which we begin to see some real changes," she said.

She particularly questioned the GES's policy of transferring teachers, urging the Service to reconsider whether such arrangements adequately address cases involving allegations of sexual misconduct.

"Are we going to continue to transfer teachers? So they need to go back and think about their transfer policies, whether it makes sense," she stressed.

The NETRIGHT Convener further demanded greater transparency in the handling of sexual abuse complaints, proposing that the GES publish annual statistics on reported cases and the actions taken.

"We would like to have a report annually. How many sexual abuse cases did the GES get, and how did they resolve them, so that when you are taking your daughter to school, you will know comfortably that she is protected," she stated.

"We want an offenders' register," she added.

According to her, such accountability measures would help reassure parents that schools have effective systems to protect children from sexual abuse.

Her comments follow allegations of sexual abuse involving female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School, brought to public attention through an investigative documentary by journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni.

Prof. Darkwah maintained that the controversy should prompt lasting institutional reforms rather than temporary responses, with particular emphasis on safeguarding students, reviewing teacher transfer policies and ensuring accountability in the handling of sexual abuse complaints.

Ghana News.title: Obuasi SHTS sexual abuse: Zakaria Abdulai is a free man now, as I know – Manasseh
Ghana News.content:
JoyNews investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni says the suspended headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS), Zakaria Abdulai, is moving freely despite allegations of sexual abuse involving female students.

Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 24, Mr Awuni said that, to his knowledge, the headmaster had not been detained and was able to move around following his engagement with the police.

“Zakaria, as far as I know, is a free man at least for now because I left Obuasi on the 25th of August and at the time, he hadn't been arrested,” he said.

Mr Azure explained that although there had been reports of an attack on the headmaster by students, he understood that the incident was being used as a reason to allow him to recover.

"They claimed he had been attacked, I think, on the 4th by the rioting students, so they wanted him to heal."

He also recounted claims that the father of one of the alleged victims had been contacted by the police and that there had been an attempt to settle the matter privately.

“But even before that, the girl's father said the police had called him. The man wanted them to sit down and settle so that the case wouldn't go out, and the girl's father said no,” he said.

According to Mr Awuni, the headmaster had subsequently indicated on other platforms that he had been cautioned by the police and granted self-recognisance bail.

“He literally walked to the police. They listened to his story and then said you can go,” the journalist added.

Mr Awuni further claimed that the headmaster had been in Accra recently to meet the NDC Functional Executive, arguing that he continued to move around despite the allegations.

Background

The controversy follows a JoyNews investigation by Mr Azure, titled Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow, which detailed allegations of sexual abuse involving female students at the school.

One of the cases concerns a 20-year-old student who alleged that Mr Abdulai raped her at his official residence on campus on July 25, 2026.

According to a police statement, the student reported the incident to the Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit in Obuasi on August 4, accompanied by her father. She further alleged that the headmaster gave her GH¢100 to keep quiet. The allegations remain under investigation.

The investigation also reported that complaints about alleged sexual abuse had been brought to the attention of school management, education officials and other authorities months before the headmaster’s suspension.

Following the revelations, Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu directed the Ghana Education Service (GES) to suspend Mr Abdulai and referred the matter to the Criminal Investigations Department for investigation.

Interior Minister Mohammed Muntaka Mubarak subsequently disclosed on October 20 that the headmaster had been arrested in connection with the allegations.

Police investigations have included efforts to obtain DNA evidence, while the case docket has been forwarded to the Attorney-General’s Office for advice.

Mr Abdulai has denied wrongdoing and has said he was cautioned and granted self-recognisance bail. He has also resigned as Juaben Constituency Secretary of the National Democratic Congress and withdrawn from the constituency chairmanship race amid the controversy.

The allegations have triggered public concern and calls for a thorough investigation into both the claims against the headmaster and the handling of earlier complaints by school and education authorities.

Ghana News.title: Sexual abuse should trigger police investigations, not community intervention – Felicity Nelson
Ghana News.content:
The Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Tourism Development Company, Felicity Nelson, has called for an end to the practice of traditional and religious leaders intervening to seek private settlements in sexual abuse cases instead of allowing the police to investigate.

Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 24, Ms Nelson said the practice of elders, chiefs, queen mothers, pastors and imams pleading on behalf of alleged perpetrators of sexual offences undermines accountability and must be discouraged.

Her comments follow allegations of sexual abuse involving female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School, which have raised concerns about child protection and the handling of complaints within educational institutions.

"We have to look culturally as Ghanaians and say this idea that when someone commits a crime, especially of a sexual nature, where elders, church leaders, imams, chiefs and queen mothers go and beg on their behalf needs to stop," she stated.

"If it was even my wish, we need to criminalise it," she added.

Ms Nelson stressed that allegations of sexual abuse must be subjected to thorough investigations rather than resolved through informal interventions, while safeguarding the rights of all parties involved.

She also urged authorities to prioritise the welfare of the alleged victims by ensuring they receive adequate psychological, emotional and medical support.

"Of course, all allegations must be investigated. As it stands now, these still remain allegations, so we are still saying yes, let's investigate. However, I want us to prioritise the victims in this case, their wants, their needs," she said.

"We need to ensure that they are fine. We need to ensure that psychologically they are okay, emotionally they are fine. In terms of health, we need to do those checks," she emphasised.

Highlighting the broader problem of sexual abuse in Ghana, Ms Nelson cited UNICEF reports which, according to her, indicated that 22 per cent of adolescent girls had experienced some form of sexual abuse, while another report suggested that 51 per cent of girls in secondary schools experienced sexual abuse between 2019 and 2021.

She described the situation as endemic, warning that the allegations at Obuasi Senior High Technical School reflect a wider national concern, with many incidents going unreported.

"This is endemic, it's a serious issue. Inasmuch as we are talking about Obuasi, we need to be mindful of the fact that this is not just happening at Obuasi," she noted.

The Deputy CEO further called for stronger safeguarding systems to protect children, ensure complaints are appropriately handled and prevent alleged perpetrators from escaping scrutiny through community interventions.

Ghana News.title: Abeiku Santana raises concerns over access to GTA CEO Maame Efua Houadjeto
Ghana News.content:
created by photogrid

Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Tourism Authority (GTA) in charge of Marketing and Special Duties, Gilbert Abeiku Aggrey aka Santana, has asked the Tourism Minister to intervene in recurring difficulties accessing the Authority’s CEO, Maame Efua Houadjeto, for urgent consultations.

In a letter dated Thursday, 22nd October 2026, and addressed to the Minister of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, Abla Dzifa Gomashie, Abeiku said the challenge was affecting his ability to obtain timely guidance, approvals and decisions needed to carry out his responsibilities, particularly in domestic tourism, special events and marketing.

“On several occasions, I have had to request meetings through the CEO’s secretary or personal assistant, only to be informed that she is unavailable,” he stated.

He acknowledged the demands on the CEO’s schedule but said the situation had made it difficult for him to perform his duties effectively.

“This situation sometimes causes delays in operations, stakeholder engagements, and the implementation of key assignments,” Mr Aggrey wrote.

He also stressed that his concerns were not intended as a personal complaint but were aimed at addressing what he considers a communication gap within the institution.

“My intention is not to make a personal complaint, but to highlight a communication gap that needs to be addressed in the interest of effective management and institutional efficiency,” he said.

Abeiku has consequently asked the Minister to intervene to help establish a more effective arrangement for communication and consultation between himself and the CEO, particularly on urgent official matters.

“I therefore respectfully seek your intervention, with the knowledge of the Board Chairperson, to help establish a more effective communication and consultation arrangement between the CEO and my office, especially on urgent official matters,” he stated.

Despite the concerns raised, Mr Aggrey reaffirmed his commitment to working with the CEO and the Authority’s management team.

“I remain committed to working professionally with the CEO and the entire management team to achieve the Ministry’s objectives and strengthen the performance of the Ghana Tourism Authority,” he said.

Abeiku’s Appointment

President John Dramani Mahama appointed Abeiku Santana as Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Tourism Authority in February 2025 after the National Democratic Congress assumed office on 7th January 2025.

Abeiku Santana is a broadcaster, tourism advocate and entrepreneur with experience in media, marketing, travel and hospitality. He is the Chief Executive Officer of Kaya Tours Ghana Limited and holds a master’s degree in Tourism Management from the University of Cape Coast and a master’s degree in Marketing Strategy from the University of Ghana Business School.

Ghana News.title: Obuasi SHTS sexual abuse: FIDA Ghana calls offence first-degree felony, says it’s not bailable
Ghana News.content:
The President of the International Federation of Women Lawyers (FIDA) Ghana, Gloria Ofori-Boadu, has described the alleged sexual abuse involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School as a “first degree felony” and argued that the offence should not be bailable.

Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, October 24, she said the seriousness of the allegations and the potential danger to society should be considered in decisions regarding bail.

“Secondly, we want to see the charge sheets, the bill of indictment. This is an indictable offence because it’s, I’ll call it a first degree felony. It’s so bad,” she said.

She added that although bail decisions depend on the discretion of the court, the alleged conduct should be considered when assessing whether the accused poses a danger to society.

“We want to see how it translates into prosecution, the trial, right from the beginning to the final decision of the court. And even if there’s a jail sentence, we want to see him entering the jail place,” she said.

Madam Ofori-Boadu said FIDA Ghana wanted to follow the case through every stage of the justice process, from the charges filed by the police to the trial and the court’s final decision.

“We even believe that this is not a bailable offence because at the end of the day, even though bail depends on the discretion of the court and all that, there’s a need to look at the danger to society that this person has, seems to always indicate that he’s dangerous,” she added.

The FIDA Ghana president also criticised the Ghana Education Service (GES), arguing that its policies on how teachers accused of sexual assault are handled require review.

She said the organisation had already issued a statement on the matter and had been engaging the media to educate the public on the issue.

According to her, the GES must account to taxpayers for its handling of cases involving teachers accused of sexual misconduct, particularly where disciplinary measures such as interdiction, dismissal, transfer or promotion have been applied.

Madam Ofori-Boadu said the organisation was also concerned about the wider cost of sexual abuse to victims and the country, particularly its impact on the mental and physical well-being of those affected.

“The cost to the nation of depriving the mental health and physical wellbeing of one citizen is very huge,” she said.

She urged the media to help monitor the case by seeking information on the charges and the prosecution process to ensure that the matter is followed through to its conclusion.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: German police detain suspect after fire engulfs Hitler’s Eagle’s Nest
World.content:
No injuries were reported at the building, known locally as the Kehlsteinhaus, while police said a ‘suspicious person’ has been taken into custody.

German police have detained a suspect after a fire engulfed the Eagle’s Nest, Adolf Hitler’s notorious Nazi-era mountain retreat in Bavaria, prompting an overnight emergency operation involving about 200 firefighters.

No injuries were reported at the building, known locally as the Kehlsteinhaus. Police said investigators were examining whether a “suspicious person” taken into temporary custody was connected to the blaze.

The fire alarm was triggered by a smoke detector at about 9:50pm (19:50 GMT) on Friday. Emergency crews could see flames rising above the building as they approached and found it “completely ablaze”, according to police.

The retreat’s remote Alpine location, at an altitude of more than 1,800 metres (about 6,000 feet), complicated efforts to extinguish the fire, police spokesperson Lisa Maier said.

While authorities have not announced a cause, German media reported that investigators suspected arson.

The newspaper Bild said emergency responders had encountered a motorcyclist travelling towards them on their way to the scene and that he was subsequently detained. His possible involvement remained under investigation.

Maier said inquiries were continuing, with police planning a news conference later on Saturday.

Built between 1937 and 1938, the stone-and-granite retreat stands on the Kehlstein mountain above Obersalzberg, near Berchtesgaden in southern Germany.

Designed as a monument to Hitler’s rule and a setting for receiving foreign diplomats, it offers sweeping views across the Bavarian Alps. Hitler himself visited the resort.



The site, which remains part of the legacy of Nazi Germany, survived World War II undamaged. It has operated as a restaurant since 1952 and also houses an exhibition examining its Nazi history.

World.title: Bayern say coach Kompany ‘stable’ in hospital but will be out for weeks
World.content:
Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany collapsed during training on Friday but is said to be ‘stable’ in hospital.

Share Bayern say coach Kompany ‘stable’ in hospital but will be out for weeks on social media

Bayern Munich expect coach Vincent Kompany to miss an extended period as he continues his hospital treatment for a virus after collapsing on the training pitch.

Speaking at a news conference on Saturday, a day after the collapse, Bayern Director of Sport Max Eberl confirmed Kompany was still hospitalised in a “stable” condition.

Kompany’s English assistant coach Aaron Danks will replace the 40-year-old for Sunday’s Bundesliga match at Freiburg.

Eberl told reporters “examinations were continuing” to determine the nature of the former Manchester City and Belgium captain’s condition with a recovery timeframe yet to be determined.

“Vinnie will be given all the time he needs. We’re not starting to put together any timeframes.

“We need to firstly figure out what it is, and then we’ll discuss calmly what the recovery time is to be. We won’t be talking about days but weeks. We need to all be clear on that.”

Taking Saturday’s news conference in Kompany’s absence, Danks said he had spoken with the former centre back briefly on Friday but only to wish him well.

“I explained to him that we wouldn’t be having no football conversations. It was just checking in on his health and making sure he’s OK.

“All the football operations are in our hands, and we’ll work together as a team to keep the club moving forward.”

Bayern’s second team’s game was postponed on Friday after Kompany’s collapse, but Eberl said the club did not consider trying to postpone Sunday’s Bundesliga game.

“I think the greatest joy for Vinnie would be for us to play well tomorrow and, ideally, get a positive result,” Eberl said.



“That would probably be one of the best things we could do to help him recover.”

Danks confirmed Germany captain Joshua Kimmich, who has been on bereavement leave since Tuesday, would also miss Sunday’s game.

Kompany returned to the dugout for Wednesday’s home clash against Arsenal despite missing the pre-match news conference due to the virus.

Speaking after the Arsenal game, Kompany said his body reacted after he tried to push through the illness.

“I caught a pretty nasty virus last week, and of course, I didn’t listen to my body, and then at some point, my body just said, ‘Enough is enough!'”

The defending champions sit on top of the Bundesliga table before Sunday’s game, one point above Freiburg.

Their next Champions League match is on November 3 in Madrid against Atletico.

World.title: Deadly ‘racist’ attack in France: Are hate crimes rising in Europe?
World.content:
Monitoring group reports more Muslims in Europe face racial discrimination as ‘terrorist’ attack kills one in France.

Share Deadly ‘racist’ attack in France: Are hate crimes rising in Europe? on social media

A gunman in northern France has killed one person and injured five, including a 12-year-old girl who was seriously wounded, in what authorities are calling a racially motivated “terrorist” attack.

The shooting on Friday was carried out as mounting and often violent cost-of-living protests grip the country with more demonstrations expected on Saturday.

President Emmanuel Macron called the shooting “a terrorist and racist attack”.

So what was behind this attack? And has there been a rise in Islamophobia in Europe?

Here’s what we know:

What has happened in France?

About 10:30am (08:30 GMT) on Friday, a gunman drove through the towns of Trappes and La Verriere, a working class area on the outskirts of Paris with a large immigrant and Muslim population, and fired an automatic weapon randomly at a petrol station, a medical centre and a children’s playground.

The rampage lasted about 15 minutes before the suspect, identified as 39-year-old Kevin T, was arrested. Laurent Mazaury, the local MP, said the suspect told police he wanted to “kill foreigners”. He added: “I think we are facing a racist person.”

French media reported a young Black man was killed and a woman wearing a headscarf and a 12-year-old girl wearing a headscarf were among those shot and injured.

The man who was killed was identified as Pengo Bassio Wangi.

The girl, of North African descent, was shot eight times, according to her mother, and was transferred to a children’s hospital for surgery.

In a statement, prosecutors said of the five people injured, three were in critical condition.

How have the French authorities responded?

Interior Minister Laurent Nunez told reporters on Friday that investigations are “ongoing but it is clearly a terrorist crime”.



Prosecutors said they were investigating whether the suspect had conspired with a “terrorist group” and added that a member of the gunman’s immediate “family circle” had also been taken into custody.

A local police chief told French media that the authorities had found an “older-style semiautomatic weapon” used in World War II in the suspect’s car as well as tear gas grenades.

The mayor of Trappes, Ali Rabeh, said the suspect was “firing at random” and wanted to cause a “bloodbath” in the communities, calling it “objectively a racist attack, probably Islamophobic”.

Writing on X, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said the case was “very serious” and “all resources of the security forces and the judiciary are fully mobilised”.

The shooting comes at a moment of great tension in France as violent cost-of-living and student protests grip the country.

French authorities are to deploy 70,000 police officers on Saturday as protests, which some far-right voices have blamed on Muslim youths, are expected to continue.

What have the reactions to the shooting been?

Macron released a statement on Friday calling the “racist terrorist attack” a “turning point in the life of our Republic and our nation”.

“Tonight, I have reiterated the Nation’s support for all the victims and their families,” he said on X. “I have also reaffirmed our absolute determination to continue the fight against racism, in all its forms.”

Mayor Rabeh, who has Moroccan roots, said the people targeted “could just as easily have been my mother, my brothers or my sisters-in-law”.

“A 12-year-old girl is between life and death after being targeted by a volley of automatic gunfire in our country,” he said. “Her crime was probably being of colour.”

The girl’s mother told French broadcaster RTL: “How could anyone do this to a child?”

She questioned whether her daughter had been targeted because she was wearing a headscarf.

“She’s a child who was born in France, in Trappes,” she said. “She has the right to live in France, to make her life in France.”

The leader of the far-right anti-immigration National Rally party, Marine Le Pen, condemned the attack, calling it “barbaric”.

However, Muslim groups accused the populist right of creating a climate of hatred in the country with Islamophobic rhetoric. Most recently, Le Pen, who is campaigning for the French presidency, has proposed that women who wear the headscarf in public spaces should be fined.

Some members of the far right have also sought to blame Muslim young people for the violence taking place during ongoing protests, Farid Hafez, a senior researcher at Georgetown University’s The Bridge Initiative, which monitors incidents of Islamophobia in Europe, wrote in an article for Al Jazeera.



Last week, the European Parliament passed a resolution “on the need for an EU strategy to counter Islamist entryism and the influence of the Muslim Brotherhood network”. It was tabled by the centre-right European People’s Party and passed in a 381-167 vote with 15 abstentions.

“Symbolically, the resolution is a major victory for Europe’s right-wing anti-Muslim forces,” Hafez wrote. “It shows that the European Parliament has started abandoning any firewall against the far right as the centre right draws closer and closer to the far right.”

Rabeh said Friday’s shooting was a result of people “blaming all the ills of this society on Arab Muslims. All these comments cause deaths,” an apparent reference to the rhetoric of far-right political groups such as the National Rally. He denounced lawmakers who have made negative comments about Muslims as “criminals” who “ideologically weaponise those who are capable of committing crimes”.

The French Muslim Council blamed “the promoters of anti-Muslim hate speech who have blood on their hands”.

Are Islamophobic attacks on the rise in Europe, US?

Advocacy groups and monitors said they are.

In June, Amnesty International reported that Islamophobic violence in the United Kingdom has reached “emergency levels” with an escalating wave of hate crimes and targeted attacks, including rapes and firebombing of mosques.

The European Union’s Fundamental Rights Agency says racism against Muslims has risen in recent years and reported that one in two Muslims in Europe experience racial discrimination, especially when it comes to applying for jobs and housing.

In the UK, the monitoring group Tell MAMA reported 1,909 anti-Muslim cases last year, a 5 percent rise on the previous year, but said the true figure is likely to be much higher because many people don’t come forward.

The Council on American-Islamic Relations released a report on Friday condemning the attacks in France. It also revealed that reports of anti-Muslim bias are at an all-time high in the United States with California’s attorney general reporting a 54 percent rise in anti-Muslim hate crimes in 2025, from 24 to 38.

World.title: France braces for another day of mass protests as security on high alert
World.content:
Several planned marches in major cities in France have been banned by authorities, provoking an uproar by rights groups.

Share France braces for another day of mass protests as security on high alert on social media

France braces for a second wave of protests after worst riots in years

Paris, France – More than 70,000 police officers and gendarmes are set to be deployed across France as the country braces for a new round of protests against deteriorating school conditions and the rising cost of living.

French authorities have made clear they are determined to prevent Saturday’s demonstrations from descending into the violence that erupted last weekend.

On October 17, protests that had been largely peaceful were marred by widespread looting, vandalism and clashes, with thousands of businesses damaged or ransacked. More than 2,000 people were taken into police custody, according to official figures.

To prevent a repeat, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said 20 percent more officers would be deployed than during the previous weekend.

The operation will also involve RAID, an elite police unit usually tasked with counterterrorism and other high-risk interventions. Nunez said its officers would not be directly involved in crowd control but would support other police operations.

Ban on protests

Authorities have also adopted a highly restrictive approach to demonstrations on Saturday. President Emmanuel Macron said requests to protest from trade unions would be examined by local authorities, while demonstrations organised by other groups would be banned wherever possible.

In several cities, including Montpellier, Rouen and Nice, protests were prohibited in their downtown areas. In Lyon, demonstrations have been banned in the city centre, while in Marseille, a union-organised march has been authorised under strict conditions.



In Paris, a coalition of unions is due to lead a march from Porte d’Italie to Porte de Vincennes, along the Boulevards des Marechaux, between 1pm and 7pm, after the originally negotiated central route between Place de la Bastille and Place de la Nation was banned.

The ban – and the push of the march to the city’s edge – triggered an uproar.

“This security escalation comes at the expense of our freedoms, seriously endangering the right to demonstrate peacefully and raising fears of a further escalation of violence in our country,” said Amnesty International France.

In central Paris, businesses were shuttered and shop windows covered with protective panels, while some retailers hired private security. At least 24 metro stations were closed at the request of the police prefecture. Major cultural institutions, including the Louvre and the Musee d’Orsay, also closed for the day, while Art Basel Paris cancelled its weekend programme.

On Friday, Macron met representatives of the student movement for the first time since the protests began. He promised more teachers and a deep overhaul of Parcoursup, the admission system to access universities. But the meeting failed to defuse tensions, with student representatives calling for further mobilisation until the government presents concrete actions.

Wider discontent

The protests began in mid-September, when high school students blockaded their schools over what they described as deteriorating conditions, including dilapidated buildings and teacher shortages, as well as what they see as an unfair system for accessing higher education.

The movement has since become a focal point for wider discontent over the cost of living, inequality and Macron’s presidency.

On October 17, more than half a million people took to the streets, following calls from student organisations and remnants of the Yellow Vest movement.

The unrest comes as France approaches a pivotal presidential election in six months. Macron, who is constitutionally barred from seeking a third consecutive term, will leave office in 2027.

The violence has also put a renewed focus on the far right, whose leading figure, Marine Le Pen, has long campaigned on a promise to restore law and order. Recent polls have placed her as the leading contender for the presidency by a wide margin.

Tensions are also expected in Orleans, where Le Pen’s National Rally is holding its party congress on Saturday, marking the start of its presidential campaign.

Authorities expect between 20,000 and 30,000 people to join a counter-demonstration against the far-right party, prompting a major security operation.

World.title: Brazil’s Lula and Bolsonaro debate policy proposals before run-off
World.content:
Polls indicate Brazil’s presidential candidates are neck and neck before Sunday’s voting.

Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and his right-wing rival Flavio Bolsonaro have focused on policy proposals in the final debate before their presidential run-off.

The candidates questioned each other on Friday, two days before the election, about Brazil’s economy, infrastructure and regional development.

Lula challenged his rival’s plan to take a “chainsaw” to public spending in a manner similar to that of Argentina’s libertarian president, Javier Milei.

“I’ll have the same job here [as Milei in Argentina] because you’re leaving the country bankrupt,” Bolsonaro responded.

Bolsonaro, son of former right-wing President Jair Bolsonaro, accused the incumbent of allowing organised crime to expand, driving families into debt and not addressing the higher cost of living.

“He doesn’t know what hunger is,” Brazil’s first working-class president said of Bolsonaro, who responded, “Why are things so expensive?”

Lula questioned the senator’s experience, saying, “He doesn’t know Brazil.”

His challenger doubled down on presenting himself as a capable candidate who represented change for the country.

Tense moments

Friday’s debate in Rio de Janeiro, which was broadcast on TV Globo, was notably more diplomatic than their initial face-off on Sunday but also saw its share of personal attacks and tense moments.

Bolsonaro called Lula “Nine Fingers”, a pejorative nickname used by many of his supporters that references an accident the Brazilian president suffered during his time as a metalworker. The 80-year-old leader demanded an apology, which Bolsonaro gave him.



Lula in response called Bolsonaro a vigilante, referring to allegations that his rival has ties to paramilitary groups in Rio de Janeiro. Bolsonaro said he would classify those groups as “narcoterrorists”.

The third tense exchange was between Bolsonaro and the mother of a five-year-old who was killed in a shootout that involved a policeman who had the presidential candidate as his lawyer. Bolsonaro said he doesn’t believe his client was guilty.

Bolsonaro finished first in the initial round of voting on October 4 with 47 percent of the vote to Lula’s 45 percent.

A Datafolha institute survey published on Thursday suggested the pair are now tied with 50 percent support each, compared with Bolsonaro’s four-point lead in polls published two weeks ago.

Both candidates are expected to join supporters in the streets of Rio de Janeiro and Sao Paulo in their last campaign effort before Sunday’s run-off.

World.title: Ethiopian PM’s advisor: Tigrayan forces and others hinder stability
World.content:
NewsFeed Ethiopian PM’s advisor: Tigrayan forces and others hinder stability

An advisor to Ethiopia’s Prime Minister spoke to the press at the Tana Forum, stating that Tigrayan forces and regional actors are blocking the Pretoria Agreement and hindering regional stability.

World.title: Just Eat apologises after AI-generated images blunder
World.content:
NewsFeed Just Eat apologises after AI-generated images blunder

Just Eat has apologised after its AI-generated food images went viral for grossly misrepresenting menu items. The company said it was testing the technology to illustrate dishes without photos, but has paused the trial until the AI is further developed.

World.title: Why is Israel launching a new military operation in the occupied West Bank?
World.content:
Netanyahu says ‘we will destroy this place’ as Israeli forces begin days-long operation with raids and demolitions.

Share Why is Israel launching a new military operation in the occupied West Bank? on social media

Israel’s military has launched another major operation in the occupied West Bank, during which it plans to carry out mass arrests, demolish homes and forcibly displace residents.

The operation comes after an attack at an Israeli military checkpoint near Hebron on Friday in which two Israeli soldiers were killed. The two suspected Palestinian gunmen were shot dead.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who ordered a full lockdown of the West Bank, said Israeli forces would go house-to-house in the Hebron neighbourhood that the suspected attackers came from.

“We will act to destroy this place, ⁠to change it completely,” he said.

Israeli rights group B’Tselem warned the Israeli government’s planned offensive amounts to “collective punishment and acts that could constitute war crimes”.

Here’s what we know about the Israeli military operation.

What’s happening in the West Bank?

Israel’s military announced late on Friday that a major “counterterrorism” operation, involving Israeli soldiers, police and other security agents, was under way in the Hebron area of the occupied West Bank.

It said the “targeted” campaign would last “several days”, in addition to operations in “dozens” of other areas across the West Bank.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu earlier said Israeli forces would go “house-to-house” in the Hebron neighbourhood where the suspects involved in Friday’s attack came from, replicating tactics previously used in refugee camps in the northern West Bank. The operation will involve demolitions and forced displacement, he said.



By Saturday morning, Israeli forces had raided at least 15 towns in the northern West Bank, including Nablus, Jenin, Tubas and Qalqilya, arresting dozens of Palestinians, Al Jazeera correspondents reported.

On Saturday, videos posted on Telegram by Palestinians in the al-Jalda area of Hebron city showed Israeli soldiers standing guard and military vehicles, shopping trolleys and other objects blocking the roads.

Israeli forces in the area had also sent in a bulldozer that could be seen alongside other Israeli military vehicles.

Earlier, Israeli bulldozers wrecked a three-storey building in Hebron, while ordering hundreds of Palestinian families to leave their homes in the Ein Deir Bahha area of the city and its surroundings.

Al Jazeera’s Nour Odeh, reporting from Ramallah in the West Bank, said there was “a lot of anxiety” in the occupied territory as people largely avoided going into the streets.

“Hebron is sealed off; seven district entrances are closed,” Odeh reported on Saturday. “Only one or two may allow some pedestrian traffic at times, and it’s extremely unpredictable.

“The Hebron municipality has told us that up to half of the neighbourhood attacked overnight by Israeli soldiers in Hebron has been forcibly displaced. At least 200 families are now forced to be outside their homes.”

Why has Israel locked down the West Bank?

The measure is a response to Friday’s attack at an Israeli checkpoint near Hebron.
