But it also takes place just days before Israel’s election on Tuesday, during which Israel had already been planning to lock down the occupied territory, reported The Times of Israel.

During the lockdown, Netanyahu said Israeli troops would conduct “extensive waves of arrests” and pursue Hamas fighters “wherever they are and at all times”.

Is this related to attacks possibly restarting on Iran?

The operation comes amid signs that Israel and its ally the United States are preparing for a potential new wave of attacks on Iran.

According to The New York Times, the US and Israel have drafted plans for a campaign of attacks on Iran that would take place after the US midterm elections on November 3.

Citing unnamed US officials and other informed sources, The New York Times reported that the US and Israel have intensified drills for a “a short but intensive operation” against Iran, with potential targets to include the country’s “energy infrastructure, nuclear facilities, and missile and drone arsenal”.

US President Donald Trump appeared to confirm on Friday that the US was weighing a new military campaign against Iran. Speaking at a rally, Trump said, “We may do another little epic fury,” using the codename of the US-Israel war against Iran that started with attacks across the country on February 28.



How have attacks on Palestinians escalated?

Since the beginning of 2025, more than 40,000 citizens have been forcibly displaced from their homes by Israeli settler violence and raids by armed forces in the West Bank, and displacement continues to this day, The Palestinian Authority said in a statement on Saturday.

It warned of the dangers posed by the ongoing Israeli operation in Hebron, “where collective punishment measures include the forced displacement of entire neighbourhoods, the demolition of homes and structures, and the closure and siege of Palestinian cities”.

Israeli settler pogroms against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank have been particularly rife in recent weeks, coinciding with the annual olive harvest season.

On Saturday morning, Israeli settlers stormed the villages of Yabrud and Al Mughayyir, east of Ramallah, to forcibly graze their sheep on the agricultural lands of Palestinians and damage their crops, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.

On Thursday, the Palestinian Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission said it had recorded 409 attacks by Israeli forces or settlers against Palestinian farmers, their land, olive trees and agricultural equipment so far during October. It called the attacks part of a pattern of “direct violence to force farmers from their land”.

Visiting Western officials have also found themselves caught up in the violence.

On October 17, Israeli settlers assaulted European diplomats, including a French mayor, near the Palestinian village of Taybeh in the occupied West Bank as they visited Palestinian olive farmers. Then on Wednesday, US Democratic congressional candidate Brad Lander was briefly detained by the Israeli military while volunteering to help Palestinian farmers harvest olives.

What has the response been to Israel’s West Bank operation?

The operation has been cheered on by far-right Israeli officials, but criticised by the United Nations and human rights watchdogs.

Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, who also holds a position within Israel’s Ministry of Defence where he oversees the administration of the occupied West Bank and its settlements, called for Israel’s large-scale offensive in the West Bank to proceed “exactly like in Gaza”.

Israel’s National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir called for the Ramallah-based Palestinian Authority to be “dismantled” and for tighter restrictions on Palestinian movement.

Mustafa Barghouti, secretary-general of the Palestinian National Initiative party, said incitement from far-right Israeli ministers was making the situation worse.

He told Al Jazeera the West Bank lockdown was turning every city and village into “a small prison”, a form of collective punishment that would “lead to explosions”.

Mayy El Sheikh, spokesperson for the UN’s Human Rights Office in the occupied Palestinian territory, said Israel’s move to lock down the West Bank marked “yet another episode in a never-ending stream of suffocating measures making life more and more unbearable for Palestinians”.



UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, through his spokesperson, also expressed concern about West Bank closures that would restrict Palestinians’ “access to basic services and livelihoods”.

B’Tselem sounded the alarm over Israeli “plans for collective punishment and acts that could constitute war crimes”.

“The world cannot stand by as Israel continues its assault on Palestinians, waiting for yet more neighbourhoods to be emptied and erased before intervening, despite what we have already witnessed in Gaza and the northern West Bank,” said the rights group.

World.title: Ukraine says Starlink connection 'now stable' after network limits
World.content:
Ukraine now has a "stable connection" to Starlink, its defence minister has said, after its military suffered days of restricted connectivity on the satellite network.

Kyiv relies on the Starlink and its military-grade counterpart Starshield for piloting drones and operations within Ukraine, but last week accused US President Donald Trump of telling owner Elon Musk to place limits on it.

This meant drones would lose connection when travelling at 161km/h (100mph) or more, it said. Trump denied doing so before saying Musk had "put it back".

Defence Minister Yevhenii Khmara said that speeds of more than 400km/h were now possible on the network, indicating that full capability had been restored.

"This result is above all important for our front, for our soldiers, for the operation of drones, for logistics and for communications," he said in a statement on Saturday.

Ukraine's military uses the network of 10,000 low Earth orbit satellites extensively for military operations, particularly in remote areas on the battlefield.

Ukraine uses both the civilian service Starlink and the more secure Starshield, which Musk said was controlled by the US military when he suggested the Pentagon could be behind the recent issues.

Russia is not authorised to use Starlink, so when Ukraine sends long-range missiles or drones deep into Russia to hit oil refineries, the network does not work.

The debacle over Starlink began last week, and emerged during a broader diplomatic row between Trump and his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky over Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil infrastructure.

Faced with midterm elections next month, Trump has waived some sanctions on Russia and agreed a deal to import Russian diesel for the US market - a move criticised by Ukraine and its European allies.

Trump said the strikes on Russian oil refineries, which Kyiv says are crucial to stemming the main revenue source for Moscow's war effort, have pushed global prices higher.

While the attacks have had an impact on global fuel prices, rises seen this year have primarily been due to the Iran war.

Zelensky said that, as well as seemingly limiting Starlink capability in Ukraine, the US had also threatened to withdraw intelligence sharing if the strikes did not stop, something Trump also denied.

Meanwhile, fighting on the ground continues.

Russian authorities said on Saturday there were power cuts in Russian-annexed Crimea following a Ukrainian drone attack.

Sergey Aksyonov, the Moscow-backed governor of the region, said restrictions on electricity and water had been put in place.

Separately, Russian-backed authorities said at least three people had been killed and another wounded in a separate Ukrainian strike in Kharkiv.

World.title: Arrest made after fire at Hitler's mountaintop Eagle's Nest retreat
World.content:
Police in the southern German state of Bavaria have detained a suspect during a fire at Adolf Hitler's Alpine mountain retreat, the Kehlsteinhaus, also known as the Eagle's Nest.

Dispatchers in Traunstein received a fire alarm from the building at 21:15 local time (19:15 GMT) on Friday and firefighters found it engulfed in flames.

Difficult terrain was hindering efforts to extinguish the blaze and it was still burning early on Saturday, police said, with some 200 emergency personnel deployed. There were no reports of injuries.

The retreat, above the town of Berchtesgaden, was one of several buildings in the area used by the Nazi dictator and his entourage during World War Two.

Hitler and top Nazi officials used his nearby Berghof residence to plan the invasion of the USSR in 1941 and the whole complex was considered one of his headquarters.

He also used the area as a backdrop for propaganda films portraying him as a lover of animals and nature.

A criminal investigation is under way to determine whether the suspect is connected to the fire.

World.title: Father who killed Oregon school gunman describes anguish over children he couldn't save
World.content:
A father who fatally shot a gunman at his daughters' school in the US state of Oregon has described his anguish over being unable to save more pupils after "hearing children pleading for their lives".

Three students and a teacher were killed by a 16-year-old former student at Silver Rail Elementary School earlier this month. The attacker was then killed by Kaylub Giamanco.

"I want to apologise for not saving their babies," Giamanco, who has been hailed as a hero, said of his thoughts for the parents of the children killed, in an interview with Oregon Public Broadcasting (OPB) that aired on Friday.

"The gratitude for saving people's children is awesome, but there were ones that I didn't save."

Giamanco, 36, said he wanted to meet the victims' families and "cry with them and hold them".

He credited a teacher who fought the attacker with giving him the chance to intervene without losing his own life.

"I would love to give her a hug because that's a real true hero," he said.

The students who were killed were all boys, aged five, eight and 11. They were among six people in total who were shot in a classroom at the school, police said. Alongside the teacher who was killed, another child and a teacher were wounded.

Giamanco told OPB that the day of the attack began with breakfast and making packed lunches. He and his wife had spent extra time getting their daughters ready because it was school picture day.

The carpenter had taken lunch to work but decided to go home to eat with his wife instead. That decision brought him past the school as the attack began.

He initially wondered whether someone carrying a long gun was playing a prank. Then he saw him fire at a pickup truck and head towards the school.

Giamanco retrieved a handgun from his vehicle and called emergency services.

"I said, 'I'm sorry, I have to go in. People are going to die'," he told the broadcaster.

He followed the attacker, who shot through the school's locked glass doors. Hearing children pleading for their lives and more gunfire, Giamanco crawled towards the building.

"I told myself this is probably the last thing that I'm ever going to do," he said.

World.title: British woman dies after trying to rescue sons swept away at sea in the Bahamas
World.content:
In a statement, posted on social media, the Royal Bahamas Police Force said: "According to the preliminary report, shortly after 10am, officers at the Alice Town police station received information that a female was unresponsive at the North Bimini Ferry Dock.

"Officers responded and, upon arrival, learned that the woman had been transported to the local clinic for medical attention, where she was subsequently pronounced dead by a local doctor despite efforts to save her life.

"Preliminary information indicates that the deceased was snorkelling with her husband and two sons near the southern point of the island when a strong current reportedly swept both children away.

"In an attempt to rescue her sons, the woman was also swept away.

"She was later rescued and transported to the ferry dock, where CPR was reportedly administered.

"Foul play is not suspected at this time.

"An autopsy will be conducted to assist in determining the exact cause of death."

A spokesperson for the Foreign Office added: "Our thoughts are with the family of a British woman who has died in the Bahamas.

"We are in contact with the local authorities and providing support to her family."

World.title: Student movement takes Serbia's Vučić to the wire in neck-and-neck election
World.content:
Ilija SrdanoviÄ may head the list of candidates â but he is not the movement's leader and would not necessarily be first choice prime minister if they won.

SrdanoviÄ insists that the Student List has a clear vision: "We offer to our citizens the core values of civilised society, which this previous regime has taken away from our citizens for the last time."

The other candidates on the Student List range from academics to athletes â and economists to engineers. None of them has a political background. But the students who selected them believe that is a strength, rather than a weakness.

"We've gathered people who are actually the best in their fields, and we really think that they are competent enough to rule the country," says Aleksandra, a student at Novi Sad University who only wants to give her first name.

"All of them are gathered around the same vision of a country where the freedom of speech is ruling, where you can walk to your home in the middle of the night and you will not be beaten up by some hooligans," she adds.

The Student List and its supporters say that Aleksandar VuÄiÄ and the SNS dominate state institutions and media coverage.

At the last parliamentary election in 2023, the International Election Observation Mission noted "overwhelming ruling party advantage" due to "bias in the media" and "misuse of public office and resources".

The BBC approached leading figures in the SNS for an interview but was not offered a response.

World.title: Woman, 65, becomes second patient to die of Ebola in Kenya
World.content:
Kenya has recorded its second death from Ebola as it handles its first ever outbreak of the disease.

A woman, aged 65, who was a close family member of the first victim, a man who had travelled from the Democratic Republic of Congo, died after being placed in quarantine, the health ministry said.

Seven other Ebola patients were receiving treatment at two isolation facilities, it added.

All the cases were within "one cluster, with no evidence of community spread", the ministry said.

More than 4,000 people have died in Africa since Ebola was confirmed in DR Congo in May, making it the second most deadly outbreak of the disease.

Kenya's latest victim had been under quarantine when she developed symptoms on 13 October, the health ministry said.

The first death, on 5 October, was that of a man who fell ill in September and was treated in several hospitals in DR Congo before arriving in the Kenyan capital, Nairobi, where he died a few days later.

Those still being treated are three other relatives of the first victim, three health workers and a hospital cleaner.

World.title: Australian MP's condition improves after alleged car attack
World.content:
The condition of Helen Haines, the Australian MP hit by a car five days ago in north-east Victoria, has improved from critical to serious but stable.

The independent MP, 65, had both her legs amputated after what authorities say was a deliberate attack outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, north-east of Melbourne, on Monday.

In the latest update on Saturday morning, the Alfred Hospital in Melbourne said Haines was in a serious but stable condition, the first improvement since she was airlifted there.

Her alleged attacker, 43-year-old Brendan Nugent, was arrested shortly after the incident and has since appeared in court on three charges.

The politician's husband, Phil Haines, said on Wednesday that the "horrendous incident" had caused his wife significant injuries but "her heart and her mind" were "in good shape".

World.title: White House lifts tariffs on some Canadian goods as midterm elections loom
World.content:
The Trump administration is lifting some of its 50% tariffs on Canadian goods two weeks before the midterm elections, after a Republican candidate in a key US Senate race said she had lobbied for the change.

From 30 October, tariffs will be eased on products including "plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment", the White House said on Friday.

Republican Senator Susan Collins, who is in a tight race to keep her seat in Maine, first announced the exemptions, saying they would help her state's agriculture industry.

The US imposed a 50% levy on $20bn (Â£15bn) worth of Canadian goods after trade talks between the two countries collapsed in August.

Canada has imposed a series of countermeasures in response to the US tariffs, which Prime Minister Mark Carney said were "necessary to protect our workers".

Last month, Carney matched the US tariffs "dollar for dollar" after the breakdown in talks. Trump had imposed them for what he called "unequal treatment" of US car, dairy and alcohol exports.

The White House said that, while tariffs would be lifted from some items, including some packing crates and boxes, they would be introduced on other items such as carpets and "waste products".

It said the action reflected US President Donald Trump's "continued efforts to defend American workers and ensure fair trade".

World.title: Ebola: Uganda restricts transit for travellers from DRC
World.content:
Uganda has barred travellers with a history of travel to the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) from transiting through the country as it investigates the traveller who tested positive for Ebola disease in Nigeria.

The Ugandan Ministry of Health announced the measure on Friday, alongside the reinstatement of traveller locator forms “to facilitate timely follow-up and contact tracing where necessary.”

“The Ministry of Health wishes to update the country on an ongoing investigation into the traveller who tested positive for Bundibugyo Virus Disease in Nigeria.

“Available information indicates that the traveller did not exhibit symptoms at the time of departure from Uganda. However, investigations are continuing to establish the timing of symptom onset and the circumstances surrounding her infection,” the ministry noted in a statement signed by its Director General of Health Services, Charles Olaro.

It added that Uganda is working with Nigerian health authorities to establish the traveller’s full travel history, movements and possible exposure. It has also requested additional information from Nigeria, including detailed travel records and genomic sequencing results, where available.

The country insisted that it “remains Ebola-free.”

Uganda had earlier battled an outbreak of Ebola disease caused by the Bundibugyo virus, which was declared on 15 May 2026 after cases were imported from the DRC.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The country recorded 20 confirmed cases, including two deaths, before declaring the outbreak over in August after 42 days without a new locally acquired case.

As of 20 October, the DRC had recorded 9,704 confirmed cases and 4,687 deaths across eight provinces, according to the World Health Organisation (WHO).

Uganda tightens controls

The ministry said infection prevention and control measures had been reinforced at all points of entry and exit and health facilities, while surveillance continued across the country.

It also warned that provisions of Uganda’s Public Health Act would be invoked where public health requirements were breached.

The ministry urged communities to report suspected unauthorised border crossings to relevant authorities for screening and public health follow-up.

The ministry urged travellers and the public to remain calm and vigilant, practise proper hand hygiene and comply with screening and other public health measures.

Earlier Uganda clarification

Uganda’s latest measures follow an earlier clarification after Nigeria announced its Ebola case and said the patient had arrived on an international flight from Uganda.

On 21 October, Uganda said the traveller’s passage through the country does not establish that she contracted Ebola there. The ministry said preliminary information indicated that she had travelled to eastern DRC for business before passing through Uganda and that she had not shown symptoms while in the country.

Uganda also said at the time that it had no active Ebola cases. The latest statement maintains that position, saying investigations with Nigerian authorities are still ongoing.

Nigeria case linked to Kenya

On Friday, Nigeria announced a genomic finding showing that the virus detected in its patient is highly similar to the virus found in Kenya’s first imported case.

Nigeria’s Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, said the finding does not establish that the Nigerian patient was infected in Kenya, as there was no evidence that she had travelled there.

The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) had earlier said it was investigating a possible link between the Nigerian and Kenyan cases because both patients travelled through Uganda’s Entebbe International Airport on 3 October.

Kenya’s first case was imported from the DRC through Uganda. The country has since recorded nine confirmed cases, including two deaths, with the eight additional cases linked to the first patient.

World.title: 2027: APC supporters slept at Kaduna venue, streets ahead Tinubu campaign flag-off
World.content:
Several All Progressives Congress (APC) supporters spent Friday night at the Ranchers Bees Stadium and on surrounding streets in Kaduna ahead of the official launch of the party’s presidential campaign by President Bola Tinubu.

The eager supporters made their way into the stadium late Friday to secure seats ahead of the event. By 6 a.m. on Saturday, several others had arrived at the venue, making frantic efforts to gain entry, while another crowd created a carnival-like atmosphere outside the arena.

Many supporters slept on the streets near the stadium to ensure they gained entry ahead of the campaign rally, awaiting the arrival of President Tinubu, who was scheduled to arrive in Kaduna at noon.

The rally marks the flag-off of the APC presidential campaign, drawing party faithful and elected officials from across the seven North-West states – Kano, Jigawa, Zamfara, Sokoto, Kebbi, Katsina and the host state.

Zaidu Bala, a media aide to the Governor of Kebbi State, described the supporters’ vigil at the venue and on the streets as a strong display of political resilience that signalled an APC victory.

He claimed that many were forced to spend the night outdoors because hotels and guest accommodations across Kaduna were fully booked.

“Politics is not for the faint-hearted; any party that does not have resilient and dedicated people like these (who spent the night on the streets) will not win an election in Nigeria.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Hotel rooms in Kaduna are exhausted; guest accommodations are full because of the love for Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” Mr Bala said on Facebook.

Why Kaduna?

A Kaduna-based political analyst, Haruna Ibrahim, told Daily Trust that the choice of Kaduna for the campaign flag-off is strategic because of the state’s position in northern politics.

According to Mr Ibrahim, Kaduna is home to people from different ethnic, religious and social backgrounds, making it a meeting point for political interests across the country.

He said supporters from other northern states could find it easier to travel to Kaduna than some other destinations in the region.

“The rally should hold in Kaduna rather than Sokoto, Zamfara or Katsina states because Kaduna is more or less the centre of northern Nigeria and also a bit safe compared to others,” the newspaper quoted him as saying.

He added that people from Bauchi, Gombe, Borno and Yobe might prefer to attend a rally in Kaduna because of its location and transport connections.

Mr Ibrahim also argued that the state’s concentration of security formations could make it a more suitable location for a large political gathering than some other parts of the North-west.

The Saturday’s campaign flag-off in Kaduna came on the heels of heated politics between the ruling APC and the opposition African Democratic Congress (ADC).

​The ADC accused the ruling party of deploying enormous state resources and security operatives to guard its presidential campaign posters.

However, APC supporters in the state dismissed the allegations, maintaining that security personnel were not assigned to protect campaign materials, but were stationed at strategic locations to safeguard the public.

​In turn, the APC alleged that it had uncovered plots by opposition figures and supporters in the state to deface and destroy its candidate’s billboards to create a false narrative on social media that the party lacks grassroots support in Kaduna.

Why the politics is hot in Kaduna

​Governor Uba Sani was widely regarded as former governor Nasir El-Rufai’s political protégé and handpicked successor; but their relationship deteriorated after Mr Sani took office in May 2023.

​The division became public in March 2024 during a town hall meeting in Kaduna, where Governor Sani revealed that his administration inherited a staggering debt burden of approximately $587 million in foreign loans, ₦85 billion in domestic debt, and 115 contractual liabilities from Mr El-Rufai’s eight-year tenure – 2015 to 2023.

Mr Sani explained that federal allocations were heavily deducted at source to service these obligations, severely constraining his ability to pay civil servants’ salaries and execute new capital projects.

Following Governor Sani’s statements, the Kaduna State House of Assembly established an ad hoc committee to investigate financial dealings, contract awards, and loan disbursements during the Mr El-Rufai administration, who is now a figure in the opposition ADC.

The committee recommended investigations by anti-graft agencies (such as the EFCC and ICPC) into billions of naira in state spending, effectively ending the alliance between the two political camps. While the APC is flagging its 2027 reelection campaign, Mr El-Rufai is under court-authorised detention, facing corruption charges.

World.title: U-17 WWC: Busari reveals how Flamingos recovered from Poland shock
World.content:
Nigeria’s Flamingos head coach Akeem Busari has praised his players for their resilience and determination after they bounced back from their defeat to Poland to stun defending champions North Korea 3-1 in their final Group B fixture at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup.

The victory marked a significant response from the Nigerian side, who had suffered a disappointing 2-1 loss to Poland before recovering with a 2-0 win over Puerto Rico and an impressive performance against the North Koreans.

Busari, who took charge of the team in April, reflected on the progress made under his leadership, the disappointment of losing to Poland, and the need for his players to maintain their belief as they pursue their ambitions at the tournament.

The coach explained that the defeat to Poland was a rare setback for a team that had enjoyed an encouraging run of results in preparation for the competition.

“Like I said to somebody while we were talking, the Poland game was the first game we had lost since I took over the team in April this year. We have played a series of about 20-something friendlies,” Busari said.

“During the qualification, we played four games and won all of them, while at WAFU-B, we won all five games. Poland was a shocker to us, but we just had to let it go. We had to restrategise and look at ourselves.

“We had to ask ourselves if that was really what we saw within ourselves. We needed to come back, and this victory was one of the fights for that comeback.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Busari urges Flamingos to show perseverance despite refereeing decisions

The Flamingos coach also addressed the role of officiating in football, acknowledging that mistakes can happen while insisting that his players must respect decisions made by match officials and remain focused on their own performance.

Busari stressed that resilience, self-belief and discipline were essential qualities for any team hoping to compete for a major title.

“Human errors happen. Referees are human beings, and they can make mistakes, just as we can as humans,” he said.

“But nevertheless, it is a game in which they are in charge. We just have to respect whatever decisions come. We cannot be a team or even champions without perseverance and self-belief. These are part of the discipline required of a good team with a good culture.

“Whatever they are doing to us, they are balancing it with the other team as well.”

The coach also pointed to fatigue and lapses in concentration as factors that affected his players during the match, explaining that the technical crew attempted to manage the game through substitutions and other tactical adjustments.

According to Busari, the Flamingos had to work hard to preserve their energy as the contest progressed, but the opposition continued to introduce fresh players.

“For our girls, it was a loss of concentration at that moment. You could see that we tried to slow things down with substitutions and do everything possible to manage what we had,” he explained.

“But they kept introducing players, and endurance was really beginning to tell on our girls. Nevertheless, the players kept fighting.”

The victory over North Korea will provide the Flamingos with renewed confidence as they continue their campaign, but Busari’s message remains clear: Nigeria must maintain its discipline, learn from its setbacks and keep believing in its ability to compete with the best.

Rodiat Yusuf celebrates memorable performance after North Korea win

Flamingos midfielder Rodiat Yusuf was equally delighted after Nigeria’s impressive victory, describing the result as the product of teamwork, determination and the players’ commitment to carrying out their coach’s instructions.

Yusuf, who was named Player of the Match, said the team approached the encounter determined to secure the result they needed and was pleased that their collective effort delivered the desired outcome.

“I feel so excited because we were determined to get the result we wanted, and we achieved it through hard work, consistency and working as a team,” Yusuf said.

“With the help of the coach’s instructions, we were able to get the result. It is a good moment for me, scoring my first goal this March.”

Reflecting on the personal significance of her performance, Yusuf described the experience as a special memory while urging her teammates to maintain their focus and continue giving their best in every match.

“It is a good thing for me. It is a remarkable memory for me, and I am so excited. We got the win we wanted,” she said.

“We should just keep our heads up. This game has been played and it is gone. We just have to keep doing our best every time, in every match. We should give our 100 per cent and always get our maximum result.”

Yusuf’s comments reflect the determination within the Flamingos camp to move beyond individual achievements and concentrate on the bigger objective of progressing further in the tournament.

Kemi Adegbuyi backs Flamingos to fight for U-17 World Cup glory

Meanwhile, Kemi Adegbuyi, who scored Nigeria’s opening goal against North Korea, expressed her gratitude after helping the Flamingos secure a memorable victory over the defending champions.

The forward credited God for the achievement and said the team entered the match with a clear objective: to win and collect all three points.

“I feel very, very happy, and I am very, very grateful to God because it is not by our power. It is God, yes,” Adegbuyi said.

Explaining how she found the net, the Nigerian forward said her quick reaction and determination to reach the ball ahead of the opposition helped her convert the opportunity.

“I think I was faster to the ball, and that made me score the goal. I was faster to the ball; I was quicker,” she explained.

“Our plan was to win, so our plan was to get the three points. We came out fully to play so we could get the three points.”

Adegbuyi also expressed confidence in Nigeria’s ability to challenge for the trophy, insisting that the Flamingos would continue to work towards their ultimate ambition.

“I believe we can win this tournament by His grace,” she added.

With Busari demanding perseverance, Yusuf emphasising consistency and Adegbuyi expressing belief in the team’s title ambitions, the Flamingos will hope their victory over North Korea becomes a turning point in their campaign.

After recovering from the disappointment against Poland, Nigeria have shown they can respond under pressure. The challenge now is to build on that performance, maintain their momentum and turn their renewed confidence into further progress at the U-17 Women’s World Cup.

Based on their last performance? No one would bet against that happening.

World.title: APC accuses Atiku, ADC of plot to discredit Tinubu’s Kaduna campaign flag-off
World.content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has accused the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, of planning to discredit the ruling party’s presidential campaign flag-off in Kaduna today.

The allegation was contained in a statement signed by Dele Alake, spokesperson for the APC Presidential Campaign Council.

The council alleged that Atiku and the ADC had deployed what it described as “fake news operations,” including artificial intelligence-generated content, deepfake videos and counterfeit documents, to discredit President Bola Tinubu, Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani and other APC leaders.

The council said the alleged campaign began with the circulation of a photograph showing a security vehicle stationed near an APC campaign billboard in Kaduna.

According to the APC, the photograph was presented as evidence that security agents had been deployed to protect the party’s billboards.

The council also alleged that a purported letter from Mr Sani to the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Abdulaziz Yari, claiming that the Kaduna State Government released N2.3 trillion to host the rally, was fabricated.

The APC described the claim as “utterly baseless,” noting that Kaduna State’s budgets for 2024, 2025 and 2026 amounted to less than N2.3 trillion.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We are still at a loss as to how anyone can imagine and concoct this senseless and utterly baseless lie that defies logic and basic common sense. How much is the entire annual revenue of Kaduna State, or any state, for that matter, that a state would spend N2.3 trillion to host a rally?

“The N2.3 trillion that Atiku and his hirelings are circulating online is more than Kaduna State’s annual budget for three years,” the statement said.

The APC alleged that the figures were intended to create a negative impression about the cost of hosting the rally.

It further accused the opposition of planning to circulate “old, doctored and deepfake videos” during the rally to create the impression that residents were opposed to the APC campaign.

“We hereby use this opportunity to alert the general public about this malicious and ignoble plan,” the council said.

The APC also urged Nigerians to be vigilant and reject what it described as attempts to manipulate public opinion ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The allegations were made as the APC begins its presidential campaign for the 2027 election with a flag-off rally in Kaduna today.

President Bola Tinubu is expected to attend the rally at the Kaduna Township Stadium, where the party is expected to mobilise supporters from across the country. The APC had earlier announced Kaduna as the starting point of its nationwide campaign programme.

The Kaduna APC has said it is targeting a large turnout for the event, while a support group, Arewa for Asiwaju, said it plans to mobilise 10,000 supporters from the 19 northern states and the Federal Capital Territory.

The party’s campaign council has said the Kaduna rally will mark the formal commencement of its drive to secure Mr Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, with subsequent presidential rallies scheduled across the country.

The APC’s proposed itinerary includes rallies in Rivers State on 7 November, Plateau on 14 November, Oyo on 21 November, Borno on 25 November, Enugu on 28 November and Bauchi on 29 November, among other states.

World.title: HURIWA urges NASS to withdraw nutritionists’ council bill
World.content:
The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) has urged the National Assembly to withdraw a proposed bill seeking to establish the Nutritionists Registration Council of Nigeria, warning that it could marginalise indigenous food knowledge and create legal uncertainty around traditional nutritional practices.

HURIWA said the bill, sponsored by Chike Okafor, a member of the House of Representatives representing Ehime Mbano/Ihitte Uboma/Obowo Federal Constituency, requires a fundamental reconsideration because of its proposed regulatory powers and the absence of adequate safeguards for traditional and family-based nutritional knowledge.

The association made the call in a statement issued on Friday by its National Coordinator, Emmanuel Onwubiko.

Mr Onwubiko said the bill should be withdrawn pending transparent and inclusive consultations involving nutrition experts, traditional knowledge holders, farmers, public health professionals, civil society organisations and affected communities.

He said Nigerian communities had developed extensive knowledge of local foods, seasonal diets, food preservation, fermentation, medicinal plants, breastfeeding and complementary feeding long before the emergence of formal nutritional science.

The national coordinator argued that the bill does not adequately protect these practices or clearly distinguish professional nutritional services from ordinary family guidance and the transmission of traditional knowledge.

“HURIWA considers the Bill, in its present form, a deeply troubling legislative proposal that threatens to place Nigeria’s indigenous food knowledge, traditional nutritional practices and community-based systems of learning under the shadow of an overcentralised statutory regulator,” Mr Onwubiko said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He called for the immediate withdrawal of the bill pending a comprehensive national consultation involving relevant professionals and communities.

Mr Onwubiko said the association was not opposed to professional standards, scientific research or the regulation of qualified nutrition practitioners.

However, he argued that the proposed legislation could create an overcentralised regulatory structure that undermines Nigeria’s indigenous food heritage.

“This is not a rejection of professional standards, scientific research or the legitimate regulation of qualified nutrition practitioners. It is a principled rejection of legislation that seeks to establish sweeping regulatory powers over nutrition without first guaranteeing the protection of Nigeria’s cultural heritage, indigenous knowledge systems and the everyday food practices through which generations of Nigerians have sustained their families and communities,” he added.

Foreign funding

HURIWA also called for greater transparency regarding provisions of the bill covering international collaboration, recognition of foreign qualifications, approval of training institutions outside Nigeria, and the receipt of grants, endowments and donations by the proposed council.

The association specifically identified Sections 3, 14, 17 and 32 as requiring more scrutiny, stating that the bill should contain stronger safeguards for transparency and public oversight of external funding.

However, it cautioned against treating international cooperation or foreign funding as evidence of wrongdoing.

HURIWA urged the bill’s sponsors to disclose the consultations and research that informed the proposal and clarify whether foreign organisations, donors or commercial interests participated in developing or promoting the proposed regulatory framework.

The association maintained that Nigerians were entitled to understand the evidence underpinning the proposed regulatory structure and the measures intended to prevent potential conflicts of interest.

Previous opposition to the bill

The opposition to the bill is the second public rejection of the proposed regulatory framework by groups concerned about its implications for nutrition practice in Nigeria.

The Dietitians Council of Nigeria had previously opposed the proposal, raising concerns about its implications for the regulation of nutrition-related professions and the existing framework governing dietetic practice.

HURIWA’s position highlights the need to clarify the distinction between dietitians and nutritionists, their respective professional responsibilities and the regulatory arrangements governing their practice.

While dietitians are trained to provide medical nutrition therapy and manage diet-related health conditions, nutritionists generally focus on nutrition education, dietary guidance and public health nutrition, although their roles may overlap depending on their training and specialisation.

World.title: CAF Club Competitions: Late goals send Rangers, El-Kanemi crashing out
World.content:
Nigerian clubs Rangers International and El-Kanemi Warriors suffered painful exits from continental competition on Friday after late goals overturned their hopes of progressing against Algeria’s MC Alger and Morocco’s Raja Club Athletic, respectively.

Rangers surrendered a two-goal first-leg advantage to lose 3-0 in Algiers, crashing out of the CAF Champions League 3-2 on aggregate, while El-Kanemi Warriors conceded twice late in Casablanca to suffer a 4-2 aggregate defeat in the CAF Confederation Cup.

Both Nigerian sides had given themselves promising opportunities to advance after their first-leg results, but their continental campaigns ended in frustration as their North African opponents produced decisive performances when it mattered most.

MC Alger stage stunning comeback to eliminate Rangers

Rangers’ hopes of reaching the CAF Champions League group stage were shattered after MC Alger scored three second-half goals to overturn the Nigerian champions’ first-leg advantage and secure a dramatic qualification victory.

The Flying Antelopes travelled to Algeria with a 2-0 lead from the first leg in Abeokuta, where they had demonstrated remarkable resilience despite playing with 10 men for most of the encounter following goalkeeper Lucky Jimoh’s dismissal in the 13th minute.

Kenneth Igboke converted a penalty before James Emo struck late to give Rangers a significant advantage heading into the return fixture.

However, the Nigerian champions could not reproduce that defensive resistance in Algiers, where MC Alger gradually turned the contest around to keep their continental ambitions alive.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Chahreddine Boukholda reignited the hosts’ hopes in the 58th minute, cutting Rangers’ aggregate lead to 2-1 and giving the Algerian side the belief that a comeback was possible.

With the pressure mounting, Mohamed Bangoura struck in the 84th minute to restore parity on aggregate, leaving Rangers desperately trying to hold on as the tie edged towards a possible penalty shootout.

But the visitors’ resistance finally collapsed in stoppage time when Soufiane Bayazid found the net in the 92nd minute, completing MC Alger’s remarkable turnaround and sending the Nigerian champions out of the competition.

For Rangers, the defeat represents a bitter disappointment after putting themselves in a strong position to progress. Having secured a two-goal advantage in the first leg, the Enugu club needed to protect that lead but were unable to withstand the late pressure from their opponents.

The elimination also revives memories of a painful chapter in Rangers’ continental history. In 1976, the Nigerian club suffered a similar setback against MC Alger, losing the return leg 3-0 after winning the first encounter 2-0. MC Alger subsequently went on to claim the continental title.

Rangers must now redirect their attention to domestic football following their Champions League disappointment, while MC Alger advance to the next stage with their ambitions of another continental triumph intact.

El-Kanemi Warriors fall to late Raja souble in Casablanca

El-Kanemi Warriors also suffered a heartbreaking continental exit after two late goals handed Moroccan giants Raja Club Athletic a 2-0 victory in Casablanca, sealing a 4-2 aggregate triumph for the hosts in the CAF Confederation Cup.

The Nigerian side had entered the return leg with renewed confidence after holding Raja to a 2-2 draw in the first leg in Ikenne. With the tie delicately poised, El-Kanemi knew that a goalless draw would be enough to secure their place in the group stage.

For much of the encounter, the Nigerian representatives remained disciplined and frustrated their more experienced opponents, keeping Raja at bay as the hosts searched for the breakthrough that would swing the tie in their favour.

However, El-Kanemi’s defensive resistance was finally broken in the 88th minute when Aymen Barkok stepped up to convert a superb free-kick, giving Raja the lead on the night and shifting the aggregate scoreline to 3-2 in favour of the Moroccan club.

The goal left El-Kanemi facing an uphill task in the closing stages, with their hopes of forcing the tie back in their favour fading as Raja pushed forward to secure qualification.

Portuguese defender Marian Huja then delivered the decisive blow in the fifth minute of stoppage time, finding the net to make it 2-0 and complete Raja’s 4-2 aggregate victory.

The late double proved devastating for El-Kanemi, who had held their own for much of the contest but could not withstand Raja’s pressure in the closing moments.

For the Nigerian side, the defeat brings an end to their hopes of reaching the 2026/27 CAF Confederation Cup group stage. Their first-leg draw had kept the tie finely balanced, but they were unable to produce the performance required to finish the job in Morocco.

Raja, meanwhile, have secured their place in the group stage as they continue their pursuit of a third Confederation Cup title. The Moroccan club, two-time winners of the competition, will now turn their attention to the next phase of their continental campaign.

El-Kanemi Warriors must return their focus to domestic football after missing out on qualification, joining Rangers in an unfortunate evening for Nigerian club football on the continental stage.

A difficult night for Nigerian Club football

The exits of Rangers and El-Kanemi Warriors underline the challenge facing Nigerian clubs when competing against experienced North African opposition over two legs.

Both teams travelled for their respective return fixtures with realistic hopes of progressing, having secured results in the first legs that kept qualification within reach. Yet late goals proved decisive, turning promising positions into painful eliminations.

Rangers’ collapse in Algiers was particularly damaging, given their two-goal advantage, while El-Kanemi’s resistance in Casablanca lasted until the closing stages before Raja struck twice to settle the contest.

With both continental campaigns now over, the Nigerian sides must regroup and focus on their domestic commitments, while MC Alger and Raja Club Athletic move forward in their respective competitions.

World.title: 2027: Mutfwang rallies Plateau indigenes in Kaduna for Tinubu
World.content:
Plateau State Governor Caleb Mutfwang has urged indigenes of the state living in Kaduna to back President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, citing federal backing for infrastructure projects in Plateau.

Mr Mutfwang made the appeal on Friday while addressing members of the Plateau community in Kaduna ahead of the official flag-off of the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign on Saturday.

He said continued cooperation between Plateau and the federal government would accelerate development, urging the community to help secure another term for Mr Tinubu.

“Let us join hands to support President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for another term in 2027 so that the Renewed Hope Agenda can continue to deliver tangible benefits to our people and our nation,” he said.

The governor also described the emergence of Nentawe Yilwatda as APC national chairman as an opportunity for Plateau to strengthen its influence in national politics.

Recalling the late Solomon Lar’s role in national party leadership, he said Plateau’s representation at the national level should help advance the interests of its people.

Mr Mutfwang thanked members of the Kaduna-based community who travelled to Plateau to vote for him in the 2023 governorship election, saying their contribution to his emergence would not be forgotten.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He pledged to maintain the relationship as the 2027 elections approach and urged the indigenes to participate actively in the democratic process while maintaining peaceful relations with their host community.

READ ALSO: Troops rescue kidnap victim in Plateau

Highlighting his administration’s performance, the governor cited ongoing road projects across Plateau’s 17 local government areas, reforms in education, improvements to healthcare facilities and collaboration with security agencies.

He also mentioned the Tin City Metro bus service and federal approval of major road corridors linking Plateau with other states, saying the projects would improve transportation, facilitate trade and expand economic opportunities.

Earlier, Deputy Governor Josephine Piyo, Secretary to the State Government Samuel Jatau and Director-General of the Mutfwang/Piyo Campaign Council Joseph Ari urged the community to remain engaged in Plateau’s affairs ahead of the 2027 elections.

The chairman of the Plateau community in Kaduna, John Nanpe, thanked the governor for the visit and pledged the community’s backing for his re-election.

A patron of the community, Peter Dasat, also commended the administration and urged Mr Mutfwang to remain focused on his development agenda.

World.title: Ooni to grace Dokubo-Asari’s coronation in Rivers
World.content:
The Ooni of Ife, Adeyeye Ogunwusi, has been invited to the coronation of Mujahid Dokubo-Asari, the Amanyanabo of Elem Kalabari in Rivers State, scheduled for 19 December.

Mr Dokubo-Asari extended the invitation during a visit to Mr Ogunwusi at his palace in Ile-Ife, Osun State, according to a statement signed by Sadiq Lawal, the director of media and public affairs at the palace.

The visit also provided an opportunity for both traditional rulers to discuss strengthening cultural, historical and economic relations between Ile-Ife and Elem Kalabari.

“The visit provided an opportunity for the Kalabari monarch to formally invite the Ooni to the forthcoming Se Diye (Coronation) ceremony scheduled for December 19, 2026, in Buguma, Rivers State,” the statement read.

Mr Dokubo-Asari, also known as Da Amakiri Tubo, said traditional institutions remained important to community development, conflict resolution and the preservation of cultural heritage.

He commended the Ooni’s leadership and commitment to peace and unity, describing the meeting as an opportunity to strengthen relationships among traditional institutions across Nigeria.

Responding, Mr Ogunwusi welcomed the visit and invitation, stressing that cooperation among traditional rulers could promote national unity, peaceful coexistence and mutual respect among Nigeria’s diverse cultural communities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Ogunwusi said he wanted to establish stronger cultural, historical and economic ties between Ile-Ife and Elem Kalabari, adding that sustained engagement between traditional institutions could deepen understanding of Nigeria’s diverse identities and shared heritage.

He also commended Mr Dokubo for what he described as the wisdom and maturity with which he had handled his affairs since ascending the throne, saying “traditional leadership required courage, prudence and commitment to the welfare of the people.”

As a mark of goodwill, Mr Ogunwusi presented Mr Dokubo with a bronze artwork, explaining that it symbolised the importance of the people to a leader.

World.title: Enugu socialite killed during police raid of birthday party
World.content:
Nigeria Police

By Anayo Okoli

A birthday celebration organised by a famous Enugu socialite, Nnaji Izuchukwu, popularly known as Stone, at a hotel in the Asata area of Enugu turned fatal, leading to his death.

Reports said the celebration turned chaotic after a misunderstanding among attendees, which allegedly led the hotel management to invite the police from the Anti-Cultism Section.

The celebrant, Izuchukwu Nnaji, allegedly died from gunshot injuries he sustained during the ensuing police operation.

The exact circumstances surrounding the shooting remained unclear. Still, it was said that in the ensuing confusion following the police raid, he allegedly attempted to escape through a window with another person before he sustained gunshot injuries.

The Enugu State Police Command has confirmed the death and ordered an investigation into the incident.

Enugu police orders thorough investigation into the death

A statement by the command’s spokesman, SP Daniel Ndukwe, said: “The Commissioner of Police, Enugu State Command, CP Mamman Bitrus Giwa, has ordered a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding the death of Nnaji Izuchukwu (male) during an intelligence-led operation by operatives of the Anti-Cultism Section of the Violent Crime Response Unit (VCRU).

“He has directed the Assistant Commissioner of Police in charge of the State Intelligence Department (SID) to establish the facts of the incident and determine whether the operation and use of firearms complied with established operational standards and extant laws.

“Preliminary findings indicate that operatives, acting on credible intelligence, raided Bull Hotel, Asata, Enugu, where Nworie Chidera Kelvin, a.k.a. “Akidi,” an alleged notorious drug peddler and Vikings Confraternity member, was lodged with associates. Akidi is allegedly linked to multiple cases involving unlawful firearm possession and cultism, including one in which he was charged in absentia. He was also suspected of keeping the gang’s firearms and other criminal tools.

“The operation led to the arrest of Akidi and nine other suspects, comprising males and females aged 17–28.

“Quantities of dried weeds suspected to be “loud” cannabis, a weighing scale suspected to be used for measuring illicit drugs, and ₦43,400 in various denominations were recovered.

“During the operation, Nnaji and another suspect jumped through a window in an attempt to escape. While pursuing them, an operative was confronted by both suspects, who allegedly attempted to disarm him. In the ensuing struggle, the firearm discharged, leaving Nnaji with gunshot injuries, while the other suspect escaped.

“Nnaji was rushed to hospital, where he was later confirmed dead. His remains have been deposited in a mortuary for preservation and autopsy.

“CP Giwa has urged the deceased’s family, associates and other concerned persons to remain calm, assuring them that the circumstances surrounding the incident will be thoroughly investigated and that any officer found culpable will face appropriate disciplinary action.

“He reiterated that professionalism, ethical conduct and strict adherence to operational standards, particularly those governing the use of firearms, must never be compromised in any police operation.”

World.title: Chelsea vs Tottenham: Preview, team news, possible line-ups
World.content:
Chelsea’s English midfielder #17 Morgan Rogers (R) celebrates scoring the team’s first goal during the English Premier League football match between Arsenal and Chelsea at the Emirates Stadium in London on September 6, 2026. (Photo by Adrian Dennis / AFP) / RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE. No use with unauthorized audio, video, data, fixture lists, club/league logos or ‘live’ services. Online in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No video emulation. Social media in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No use in betting publications, games or single club/league/player publications. /

Chelsea will look to extend their winning run in the Premier League when they host Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge on Saturday in a London derby that could have significant implications for both sides.

Chelsea have won four, drawn one and lost two of their opening seven league matches, leaving them in the top four. Their recent results have also boosted confidence, with a 5-1 victory over Bournemouth followed by a 2-0 win away to Everton last weekend.

Pedro Neto scored twice against Everton as Chelsea ended a run of 22 Premier League matches without a clean sheet. The Blues will now attempt to record three consecutive league victories for the first time since February.

The West London club have won their last six league meetings with Tottenham. Another victory on Saturday would set a new club record for consecutive league wins against their London rivals.

Tottenham, meanwhile, ended a six-game winless start to the league campaign with a 3-1 victory over Coventry. James Maddison, Omar Marmoush and Ben Davies scored to give Roberto De Zerbi’s side a much-needed result.

The win was Tottenham’s fourth Premier League victory in 2026 and the first time in 36 top-flight matches that they had scored more than twice.

Despite the result, Spurs remain 16th in the table, although they are only three points behind the top nine. They will need to improve their away record against Chelsea to secure another positive result.

Tottenham have won only once in their last 34 Premier League visits to Stamford Bridge, recording 11 draws and 24 defeats. Their most recent victory there came in the 2017-18 season, when Mauricio Pochettino guided them to a 3-1 win.

Spurs have also lost their last six London derbies in the league and will be keen to avoid extending that run.

Team news

Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez is set to miss the match after undergoing surgery for a fractured jaw sustained during the win over Everton.

He joins Reece James, Jamie Gittens, Pep Chavarria and Emmanuel Emegha on the injury list. Malo Gusto, however, is available again after recovering from illness.

Mike Penders is expected to start in goal in Martinez’s absence. The 21-year-old could become Chelsea’s youngest goalkeeper to start a Premier League match.

For Tottenham, Rodrigo Bentancur remains suspended and will serve the second match of his three-game ban. Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall and Destiny Udogie are also sidelined with knee injuries, while Savio is unavailable because of a muscle problem.

Mykhaylo Mudryk, who is on loan from Chelsea, is ineligible to face his parent club and is also recovering from an ankle injury.

Tosin Adarabioyo is a doubt with a calf problem, but Pedro Porro, Omar Marmoush and Andrew Robertson have been passed fit to play.

Possible line-ups

Chelsea: Penders; Acheampong, Lacroix, Colwill; Neto, Caicedo, Henderson, Hato; Palmer, Rogers; Pedro.

Tottenham Hotspur: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Gallagher, Tonali, Maddison; Kudus and other attacking options to be confirmed.

World.title: Keyamo accuses Atiku of fearing APC’s Northern support
World.content:
The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, has accused former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar of being apprehensive about the All Progressives Congress (APC)’s support base in northern Nigeria ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

Keyamo, a senior advocate of Nigeria, made the allegation in a statement titled, “Why Atiku Abubakar Is Particularly Jittery About the Kaduna Flag-off,” in which he criticised the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate’s reported online attacks against the APC ahead of the party’s campaign rally in Kaduna State.

He alleged that some videos circulating online showing the removal of President Bola Tinubu’s campaign posters were staged to create the impression that the President had lost support in the North.

Keyamo also dismissed as fake a purported letter alleging that N2.3 trillion had been earmarked for the Kaduna rally, describing it as an attempt to portray the APC as relying on financial inducements to attract supporters.

The minister, however, did not provide evidence in the statement to substantiate his allegations about the videos or the purported letter.

He argued that Atiku’s political calculations ahead of the 2027 election had been based largely on securing northern votes, adding that the former vice-president faced challenges in gaining support in the South.

Keyamo cited the 2023 presidential election, claiming that Atiku lost across the North-Central states and all Southern states except Osun State.

He alleged that Atiku had initially expected Tinubu to have limited electoral appeal in the North but was now concerned about the APC’s political structures in the region.

According to Keyamo, the APC’s presence in northern Nigeria could undermine Atiku’s strategy of relying on the region to secure victory in the next presidential election.

The minister further argued that even a strong showing by Atiku in parts of the North might not be sufficient to secure victory if he failed to make significant gains in the Middle Belt and Southern states.

Keyamo also drew a comparison between Atiku and former President Muhammadu Buhari, who secured substantial northern support in the 2015 presidential election.

He argued that Atiku’s political background differed from Buhari’s, while making corruption-related allegations against the former vice-president without presenting supporting evidence in the statement.

The comments come amid intensifying political activity ahead of the 2027 general elections, with parties and their presidential contenders seeking to consolidate support across the country’s geopolitical zones.

World.title: 2027: Basiru urges ex-Assembly speakers to back Tinubu
World.content:
The National Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Senator Ajibola Basiru, has urged former presiding officers of State Houses of Assembly across the country to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election in 2027 and promote the administration’s economic reforms.

Basiru made the call at a programme organised by the Kaduna State chapter of the Former Presiding Officers of State Houses of Assembly in Nigeria, themed, “Kaduna 2026: United Voices of Experience, All Together for Tinubu 2027.”

He described the former legislative leaders as experienced political actors whose electoral and public service backgrounds could help the ruling party strengthen its grassroots presence ahead of the 2027 general elections.

According to him, their experience would be useful in explaining the rationale behind the Tinubu administration’s economic policies, responding to opposition criticism and engaging voters on the government’s performance.

Basiru said Tinubu inherited severe fiscal pressures upon assuming office, which, he noted, necessitated difficult policy decisions, including the removal of petrol subsidy and the adoption of a more market-driven foreign exchange regime.

He argued that the reforms, despite the initial difficulties they caused, had improved the financial capacity of state governments, enabling them to meet salary and pension obligations and invest in development projects.

The APC national secretary urged political stakeholders to explain the objectives of the reforms to Nigerians, including the challenges associated with their implementation and their expected long-term effects.

He also challenged opposition leaders who had previously occupied influential positions in government to account for their records in office before criticising the current administration.

Basiru specifically questioned former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s economic proposals, citing his participation in previous administrations and raising concerns over the privatisation and sale of national assets during that period.

He cautioned voters against what he described as unrealistic promises and politically motivated narratives by opposition figures seeking support ahead of the 2027 elections.

The APC chieftain urged the former presiding officers to intensify public enlightenment, engage communities and encourage voters to assess political parties and candidates based on their records, policies and performance.

He said sustained mobilisation, strategic communication and unity among party stakeholders would be necessary for the APC’s campaign ahead of the elections.

Basiru reaffirmed his call for party members and political stakeholders to take the administration’s message to the grassroots and mobilise support for Tinubu’s re-election bid.

World.title: Police fire tear gas as new French demonstrations kick off
World.content:
Protesters march along the Avenue Jean Zay during a demonstration “against racism, fascism and imperialism” on the sidelines of the Congress of the Far-right party Rassemblement National (RN) in Orleans, central France on October 24, 2026. Amid another Saturday of protests under tight security across France, Orleans is hosting the National congress of the Far-right party Rassemblement National and preparing for a record-breaking demonstration, on the eve of their first major campaign rally. (Photo by SIMON WOHLFAHRT / AFP)

French police started firing tear gas at protesters Saturday as they stepped up security in major cities aiming to prevent a repeat of rioting a week ago, on a day of fresh nationwide demonstrations over the high cost of living.

Police in the southeast city of Lyon fired tear gas to disperse some 150 protesters near the city centre — where demonstrations had been banned — when they briefly tried to block a road, an AFP journalist saw.

Elsewhere, authorities and rattled shopkeepers geared up for potential new street violence.

Near Paris’s Bastille neighbourhood, a clothing store had removed all its merchandise from shelves ahead of the demonstrations, while a nearby restaurant was boarded up with signs insisting it was “still open”. Many other retailers in the capital also had wooden boards covering their windows.

The Louvre and the Musee d’Orsay museums were closed.

Police were seen readying riot gear in zones that bore the brunt of last weekend’s clashes and looting.

They were among 70,000 security personnel the interior ministry said were mobilised to counter the “high” threat of violence.

“We will not tolerate any unrest,” Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on Friday, adding that calls had been circulating on social media calling for violence and looting.

– Protest against far-right party –

Adding to tensions, far-right leader Marine Le Pen’s National Rally (RN) party was holding a weekend congress in the central city of Orleans to kick off her campaign for elections in six months to choose President Emmanuel Macron’s successor.

Thousands of people yelling anti-fascist slogans marched on Saturday against Le Pen, and also against Macron, a pro-business centrist leader. “Macron resign. Le Pen in prison,” the crowd yelled.

The violence last weekend and the heightened tensions over this weekend’s demonstrations highlighted the febrile atmosphere in France ahead of that vote, which Le Pen is best-placed, according to surveys, to win.

Last weekend saw rioters on the margins of the nationwide demonstrations clash with police, vandalise public buildings and loot hundreds of stores. Some 2,700 people were arrested and the retail sector said shopowners were left with damage and stolen stock totalling hundreds of millions of euros.

Macron attributed the worst of the violence to “ultra-left” groups that he said “want to bring down the republic”.

Groups organising Saturday’s renewed demonstrations have accused Macron and his government of ignoring widespread public anger over rising costs, and over classroom conditions for students.

Inflation in France, as elsewhere, has been sent surging by the Middle East war, started in February by US President Donald Trump and Israel.

Protests have also been taking place in Italy, Belgium, Spain and Portugal over different issues, yet with some overlap on inflation and education problems. Italy has sent 500 troops to try to quell street violence in Milan.

– Boarded-up shops –

In Paris, streets on Saturday were unusually quiet, with many shop windows boarded up, and some of the bigger retailers sent messages to customers warning that they were closed for the day.

The capital’s police at the last minute ordered a union-organised march in the city be moved from Bastille, in the centre-east, to the more remote eastern Porte d’Italie on the southern rim of the capital.

Unions said they reluctantly would go along with that. But the Yellow Vest movement — a loosely organised grouping that staged disruptive street protests against Macron eight years ago — indicated it would not comply.

Macron and his government have sought to draw a line between the legitimate demands of protesters and the looting, burning and ransacking that erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations last Saturday.

Courts have already sent 217 people, half of them first-time offenders, to prison over the events on Saturday, officials said.

Macron has said authorities would accept only union-led demonstrations and would counter any others they deemed “illegitimate”.

Authorities in Marseille had banned all protests but announced Friday that a union-organised demonstration would be allowed on an “exceptional basis”.

The restrictions, including outright bans on protests in some cities, have drawn criticism.

Amnesty International denounced what it called “a slide toward authoritarian practice”, saying the measures were “jeopardising the right to demonstrate peacefully”.

“Police have a responsibility both to ensure that protests can take place peacefully and safely and to protect the public from violent disorder,” said Eva Cosse, senior Europe researcher at Human Rights Watch.

World.title: 2027: Arewa‘ll return Tinubu to Aso Rock – Musa Kwankwaso
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu

A member of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Dr Musa Kwankwaso, says the North-West will return President Bola Tinubu to Aso Rock by voting for him massively in the 2027 general elections.

Kwankwaso spoke against the backdrop of the massive turnout and endorsement of Tinubu at the formal kick-off of the APC Presidential Campaign on Saturday in Kaduna.

Kwankwaso described the gathering as a decisive demonstration of Northern support for Tinubu ahead of the 2027 polls.

The APC campaign council member said the Kaduna rally had effectively dispelled lingering doubts over where the North stood in the unfolding presidential contest.

“Today, we of the North-West geopolitical zone have spoken loud and clear on who we stand for. Our choice of Tinubu remains our commitment to a better Nigeria and national cohesion,” he said.

Kwankwaso said that the significance of the Kaduna gathering extended beyond the immediate political mobilisation.

He argued that the North had sent a strong message to other geopolitical zones on the need to consolidate around Tinubu for the sake of national progress.

According to him, the president’s administration represents an opportunity to deepen equitable development and ensure that the country’s resources are distributed fairly across the six geopolitical zones.

“Tinubu’s presidency stands for fair and equitable distribution of resources to all zones, and his return will be a blessing to the greater Nigeria of our dream.”

He also dismissed any suggestion that the North’s support for Tinubu was merely transactional, saying the region had a responsibility to honour its political commitment and remain united behind the President as the 2027 election approaches.

“Asiwaju is the northern candidate, and he will not promote anything outside his ambition because we are trustworthy people, and we shall deliver him come 2027,” he said.

He urged Nigerians, particularly political stakeholders across the geopolitical zones to view the emerging support for Tinubu through the prism of national unity and collective progress, rather than narrow political interests.

He emphasised that the Kaduna mobilisation had demonstrated that the North had already made its choice. (NAN)

World.title: Kaduna ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​govt debunks N2.3trn APC campaign spending claim, cites forgery
World.content:
Governor Uba Sani of Kaduna State.

The Kaduna State Government has dismissed as fabricated a viral letter alleging that Gov. Uba Sani approved and released N2.3 trillion for the APC presidential campaign flag-off.

The government described the purported letter as fraudulent and misleading, accusing its authors of attempting to damage the governor’s reputation for fiscal discipline and responsible governance.

The Commissioner for Information and Culture, Malam Ahmed Maiyaki, stated this in a statement on Saturday in Kaduna.

Maiyaki said the letter, dated Oct. 18, 2026, and titled “Notification for Preparations for the Grand Rally Flag Off”, contained inconsistencies that questioned its authenticity.

He said the purported letter, allegedly addressed to Sen. Abdulazeez Yari, Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, falsely claimed that N2.3 trillion was released for the campaign flag-off.

The commissioner noted that Kaduna’s 2026 budget stood at N985.92 billion, making the alleged expenditure more than twice the state’s annual budget.

He said the claim was financially implausible and unsupported by any authentic appropriation, approval or expenditure records.

Maiyaki also identified irregularities, including the misspelling of the governor’s surname as “Uba Sai” and the apparent unauthorised reproduction of his signature.

“The Kaduna State Government categorically disowns this document. Gov. Uba Sani neither authored nor authorised the purported letter, and no N2.3 trillion was budgeted, approved or released,” he said.

He described the allegation as fictitious and a deliberate attempt to mislead the public.

Maiyaki said that since assuming office on May 29, 2023, Sani had prioritised fiscal discipline, transparency, accountability and prudent management of public resources.

He listed investments in security, infrastructure, education, healthcare, agriculture and social protection among the administration’s priorities.

The commissioner expressed concern over what he described as coordinated misinformation aimed at discrediting the governor and his administration ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He warned that fabricating official correspondence and circulating false financial claims could constitute criminal offences.

“Political competition must be conducted within the bounds of truth, decency and the law,” Maiyaki said, urging critics to rely on credible evidence when questioning government expenditure.

He disclosed that steps were being taken to establish the origin of the purported letter.

Maiyaki also called on security and investigative agencies to examine the document and ensure that anyone found culpable faced appropriate legal action.

He urged media organisations and members of the public to verify documents before circulating or publishing allegations concerning public expenditure.

The commissioner reaffirmed the administration’s commitment to peace, institutional strengthening, infrastructure development, citizens’ welfare and sustainable governance.

He said the government would remain focused on prudent financial management and would not be distracted by what it described as deliberate misinformation. (NAN)

World.title: It’s unfair to compare us to Barca – Real Madrid’s Mourinho
World.content:
Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho said it was unfair to compare his side to Spanish champions Barcelona ahead of Sunday’s La Liga Clasico.

Hansi Flick’s Barca have won back-to-back La Liga titles and lead the top flight, in which they are unbeaten, while Mourinho arrived this summer after Madrid went two seasons without a major trophy.

The panorama has changed slightly, after Barca suffered their first defeat of the season at Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday, while Madrid have won their last four matches.

Madrid are third in La Liga, trailing Barca by six points before Sunday’s meeting at Camp Nou.

“I think the people that thought a week ago Barca would thrash us will keep thinking the same thing,” Mourinho told reporters on Saturday.

“I don’t think just for the Paris game, or Madrid’s (4-1 win against) Leipzig, they will change their way of thinking.”

Mourinho highlighted that he has only been at the helm a few months, in comparison to Flick, who arrived at Barca in 2024.

“People look at us like a finished product, but finished products in football are difficult because they are never finished… but they look at us like we’re in an advanced phase of the process,” continued Mourinho.

“We’ve been working for three months, out of that you can take pre-season when the players were arriving (back from the World Cup), and the recent international break, then we’ve been together a month-and-a-half, two months…

“This is the start of a product, we’re in an initial phase where the coach is learning, analysing, bit by bit defining paths, the players are learning about the coach… comparing a team in this state (to more established sides), I think is unfair.”

Mourinho said form did not matter when it comes to the Clasico.

“We’ve been in a good dynamic, winning games, playing well, scoring goals, but in the Clasico it doesn’t matter what you did before, it has no influence,” said Mourinho.

“The Clasico is unique, normally the football world stops to watch it. Hopefully it’s a great game. And we win.”

Mourinho said he would not change his plans to try and stop Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal.

The 19-year-old Spain international is in sublime form and hopes to win the Ballon d’Or award on Monday.

“He’s a great player and great players you respect,” added Mourinho.

“One thing is respecting, another thing is to change plans, structures, forgetting your own essence. That we will not do, neither for him or any other player of great quality we face.”

AFP

World.title: A Misguided Narrative: The Dangerous Implications Of Punch’s Editorial
World.content:
Biodun Ajiboye

The Punch Editorial Board’s October 16, 2026 piece on the political participation of chief executives of federal parastatals is far worse than merely flawed. It is an ill-fated, ill-informed overreach. It stands as a textbook example of journalism attempting to dictate law without basic comprehension.

The editorial’s central argument collapses under an elementary error in political science: conflating the civil service with the public service.
