World.title: Sharks, Springboks suffer major injury blow
World.content:
The Sharks’ hard-fought 36-21 United Rugby Championship victory over Cardiff on Friday night came at a heavy price after captain Andre Esterhuizen was forced off the field during the early stages of the match.

Esterhuizen landed awkwardly on his ankle during an aerial duel from the opening kick off, with the injury reigniting the intense debate surrounding player safety on artificial 4G surfaces.

The utility player – who has become one of the most effective members of the Springboks’ ‘bomb squad’ – limped off to join a growing injury list, while leaving Springbok coach Rassie Erasmus sweating over his availability for the upcoming November internationals.



Sharks star Andre Esterhuizen likely to miss Springbok tour

After the match Esterhuizen could be seen in a moon boot, and all the early signs suggest he looks set to be sidelined for a lengthy period of time.

Just prior to the clash, Sharks lock Stephan Lewies voiced widespread player reluctance toward 4G pitches, citing high injury rates and the extra physical toll synthetic turf exacts on athletes.

Critics have long pointed to increased friction, joint stress, and non-contact lower-limb injuries as major risks of playing professional rugby on artificial grass.

Player safety in question

In recent seasons, Stormers director of rugby John Dobson also highlighted several issues related to playing on 4G surfaces.

“Whether it is at maul time or ball carrying, it took time to get used to how the surface affects momentum. It is an incredibly unforgiving surface,” Dobson previously commented.

“I would prefer them not to exist, quite frankly, from a player safety and lottery of the game perspective.



“If you are on grass and there is a contact then the foot almost skids back, but on a 4G if they get their studs in they can actually cannon forward off it because their studs are not going to give. It makes it almost impossible to defend in those situations. It is dangerous too, because your legs can twist. We have done injuries like that on that kind of surface.”

World.title: Zimbabwean man arrested after two sable antelopes killed in Limpopo
World.content:
Zimbabwean man arrested after police discover meat linked to two dead sable antelopes. Image: SAPS

A 34-year-old Zimbabwean man has been arrested in Limpopo after two sable antelopes worth R44 000 were allegedly killed in a suspected illegal hunting incident.

Gift Duba was arrested on Wednesday, 22 October 2026, during an intelligence-driven police operation in the Sekhukhune District.

He faces charges of illegal hunting, possession of game meat and contravening South Africa’s Immigration Act.



According to the South African Police Service (SAPS), the arrest followed information about alleged illegal hunting at a farm along Vaalfontein Road in the Groblersdal policing area.

Zimbabwean man arrested after sable antelopes killed

Police from the Sekhukhune Tactical and Investigation Team acted on the information and proceeded to Bloompoort village, where they searched a homestead in Monageng.

During the search, officers discovered meat in a refrigerator that they suspected was linked to the alleged killing of two sable antelopes on Tuesday, 21 October.

Further investigations led police to the farm, where they found two dead sable antelopes, described as old bucks, valued at R44 000.

Police also discovered portions of meat that had been cut into strips and hung on trees to dry for the production of biltong.

Investigators reportedly established that the dried meat was intended to be collected once it had lost moisture, making it lighter and easier to transport.



Zimbabwean national faces immigration charge

Duba was arrested on charges of illegal hunting, possession of game meat and contravening the Immigration Act.

He appeared before the Groblersdal Magistrate’s Court on Friday, 23 October 2026.

The case was postponed to Monday, 26 October, for a bail application and further police investigations.

He was remanded in police custody pending his next court appearance.

The Limpopo Provincial Commissioner of Police, Lieutenant General Jan Scheepers, commended the Sekhukhune Tactical and Investigation Team for its swift response.

Police investigations are continuing.

World.title: Matric pupil BARRED: Principal suspended
World.content:
A Free State school principal has been suspended after a matric learner was allegedly prevented from writing an exam over unpaid school fees. Image: X

A Free State school principal has been suspended after allegedly barring a matric learner from writing an examination over unpaid school fees.

The Grade 12 pupil at Selelekela Secondary School in QwaQwa missed her English First Additional Language Paper 3 examination on Thursday, 15 October.

The Free State Department of Education confirmed the principal’s suspension on Friday, 23 October, pending an investigation.



PRINCIPAL SUSPENDED OVER MATRIC EXAM INCIDENT

The principal, who also served as the school’s chief invigilator, allegedly refused to allow the learner into the examination room because of outstanding fees.

The department has since appointed the deputy principal as chief invigilator for the remainder of the 2026 National Senior Certificate (NSC) examinations.

Officials have also provided the learner with psychosocial support. She has continued writing her remaining papers.

However, the department must still resolve the examination she missed.

WILL MATRIC LEARNER HAVE TO REWRITE?

Education officials are preparing an application to quality assurance body Umalusi, through the Department of Basic Education, requesting a concession for the missed English paper.

“The Department is finalising all reports and supporting documentation for submission to Umalusi through the Department of Basic Education (DBE), to request a concession in respect of English FAL P3,” it said.



The department hopes to secure the concession rather than have the learner rewrite the paper in June 2027.

Umalusi has yet to make a decision.

SCHOOLS WARNED OVER UNPAID FEES

The incident has prompted the department to hold an urgent virtual meeting with chief invigilators across public and independent schools.

Officials reminded schools that examination regulations prohibit them from excluding eligible learners over unpaid fees.

“School fee disputes must never compromise a candidate’s opportunity to write,” the department warned.

It also cautioned that schools failing to comply with examination instructions could face disciplinary action.

Under the South African Schools Act, public schools cannot deny learners access to education because their parents have failed to pay school fees.

The department has not indicated when it expects to conclude its investigation.

World.title: DA's final stretch ahead of November polls
World.content:
EKURHULENI - The DA is setting its sights on an outright win in the Ekurhuleni metro.

This is a challenge set by Deputy Federal Chairperson Siviwe Gwarube.

She was speaking at the DA's rally in Ekurhuleni, saying the party wants a clear majority so it can govern the metro alone.

At the same time, she's not ruling out coalition talks if they fail to get the desired majority.

"You don't go into an election with the view to go into a coalition. You go into an election solely with the purpose of winning. And we are putting everything and throwing everything in the kitchen sink here.

"As much as we are working with the ANC at a national level and the GNU, the truth of the matter is we're still the Democratic Alliance and we still have to sell our unique selling proposition to the people of Ekurhuleni and everywhere else around the country. To say they must give us a solid majority so we can govern alone. We've seen what we can do in the City of Cape Town when we don't have to share power, when we have actually changed the lives of people.

"So it's not to say we are ruling out any coalition arrangements, but what we are saying is that we're not going to this election wanting to coalesce. We are wanting to say to the people of Ekurhuleni they can give us a solid mandate and we can win outright."

At the same time, the DA also raised concerns about the safety of women in communities.

Gwarube wants to see more being done to ensure these crimes lead to successful convictions.

The DA is calling for closer cooperation between SAPS and metro police.

"The SAPS needs to be capacitated with greater investigating powers, but also more capacity to be able to investigate these crimes. The worst thing that a woman can ever experience is being one, either killed or number two, seeing their perpetrator walking the streets way after they've reported the matter. This happens way too often in our country.

"Therefore, the SAPS needs to be capacitated enough so that they are able to lead to successful convictions."

World.title: Lower inflation doesn’t mean lower prices - expert
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A new IPSOS survey across 33 countries shows that people expect inflation to keep rising, with wars and global conflict pushing up living costs.

IPSOS South Africa CEO Natalie Otte said South Africans are still struggling with the cost of food, electricity and transport, while unemployment and interest rates add to uncertainty.

"A people perspective, lower inflation doesn't mean that prices are going to go down. It simply means prices stop rising as quickly. And for many South Africans, the increases we've seen in food, electricity, transport and other essentials, they've started getting used to it. They've started building it into their budgets or trying to adapt to it, but people still feel very uncertain about the future.

"What's driving people's sort of uncertainty. And this rising cost of living in their perception is also the state of the global economy, but also policies of my own national government, right? And then especially in South Africa, that's a big one. The interest rate levels in my own country, as well as I said, unemployment is also a big thing, taxes and interest rates. So it isn't just the wars, but that is the main. Main thing coming through at the moment."

World.title: The cost of unemployment tallied
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Finding a job can come at a cost, from printing CVs to travelling to interviews.

JOBJACK co-founder Heine Bellingan said employers can make hiring easier, by removing unnecessary barriers, especially for entry-level positions.

Simple changes could help more job seekers access opportunities.

"There's lots of things that need to come together, but from what we've seen specifically, especially with the change in technology in the world, there's some easy things employers can do that would make a big difference. And the first thing is just not to hire from a box of paper CVs anymore. I mean, it's 2026. That's not necessary. And hiring from a box of paper CVs is a big barrier for job seekers. The cost of printing, the cost of transport to go drop a CV. So that's just an easy starting point.

"The second thing, just to lessen the burden on the job seekers, is in a store level role not to have two rounds of interviews. That instantly doubles the cost and the barrier job seeker faces.

"Then lastly, if you think about a head office, you know, white collar role, businesses invest so much in finding the right person because the wrong person in your business, in your head office is expensive. But that same thought process and investment should go into your store level roles because it's as important to find the right cashier.

"The cashier is your customer facing person in the business, it's the person driving the revenue, it's person driving sales. And if you're not investing and finding the right person, you're actually often bringing people to an interview that would never stand a chance to succeed in this role, wasting their time, incurring costs for them because they now need to travel to an interview they will just not be successful at.

World.title: Mayor needs to go - political expert over Bronkhorstspruit water crisis
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Political analyst Brutus Malada said the Bronkhorstspruit water crisis points to a serious failure of governance.

The water treatment plant ran out of chlorine while dealing with contamination linked to sewage spills upstream.

More than 400 people fell ill.

Malada said officials should have seen the crisis coming and acted sooner.

"How did they not foresee that they are going to run short of chlorine? Yeah, it says that there are no monitoring systems. There are no early warning systems or the mayor was just clueless.

"What experts are telling us that there are standard operating procedures that say at this level. That's when you must be very worried and start replenishing. Why didn't they ask for an emergency procurement to avoid the crisis that we find ourselves in? The mayor should have resigned."

World.title: Six killed in Eastern Cape
World.content:
ABERDEEN - Six people have been killed and six others seriously injured following a head-on collision between a minibus taxi and a truck on the R61.

The crash happened about 30 kilometres just outside Aberdeen towards Beaufort West.

Six female passengers in the minibus taxi died at the scene, while the injured were taken to Graaff-Reinet Provincial Hospital.

Fatigue is among the suspected contributing factors.

Police are investigating a case of culpable homicide.

World.title: North Korea's Kim calls for training world's 'strongest' military
World.content:
PYONGYANG - North Korean leader Kim Jong Un urged his military to train to become the strongest in the world at a two-day meeting of company commanders in Pyongyang, state media said Saturday.

Kim's call for what he dubbed a "Korean-style military revolution" came the same week Seoul's military proposed talks to clarify the border after an explosion inside the heavily fortified Demilitarised Zone (DMZ) further strained inter-Korean ties.

Seoul and Pyongyang remain technically at war as the 1950-53 Korean War ended in a truce, not a peace treaty.

The Pyongyang event, held Thursday and Friday, was aimed at developing a plan "to train the strongest armed forces in the world," Kim said, according to the official Korea Central News Agency (KCNA).

He also called for "all the companies" of the North's army to be "turned into a strong elite unit in military and technical aspects and consolidated into perfect combat forces".

KCNA said it was the first gathering of "the entire army" since a February party congress where Kim had called for stronger conventional forces and reaffirmed plans to develop nuclear weapons and missiles.

North Korea has also tested a slew of weapons recently, including a "new-type" precision-guided torpedo system and an intermediate-range hypersonic missile, both of which were said to use AI technology.

Despite long-running UN sanctions, North Korea has enshrined its status as a nuclear-armed state in law, with its regime repeatedly declaring its atomic arsenal permanent and irreversible.

The North has also become a key Russian ally since it launched its invasion of Ukraine in 2022, sending troops to support Moscow's war effort in return for economic benefits and military technology.

South Korea proposed on Friday military talks with North Korea to clarify their border and restore communication channels, after Seoul blamed the DMZ blast that injured South Korean soldiers on North Korean landmines, a claim Pyongyang strongly rejected.

Pyongyang, which also previously rejected Seoul's demand for an apology over the explosion, has not responded to Friday's proposal.

World.title: Typhoon Champi knocks out power to thousands in Taiwan
World.content:
TAIPEI - Emergency crews scrambled on Saturday to restore power to tens of thousands of homes in Taiwan after Typhoon Champi's fierce winds battered the island, with the storm moving towards China and Japan.

Authorities evacuated more than 5,000 people from their homes ahead of the storm, which toppled trees, brought down power lines, and triggered brief flooding.

One person has been killed and more than 500 injured since Thursday, when the government began issuing warnings about the approaching typhoon.

Around 56,000 households are still without power as Champi continues to buffet the island, with nearly 24 centimetres (9.4 inches) of rain recorded in the western county of Miaoli on Saturday.

Most shops across northern and central Taiwan were closed for a second day, as the typhoon gradually moves away from the island's northeast and heads north towards China and Japan.

"Although the period of the typhoon's most severe impact has passed, we would like to remind everyone that winds and waves in the waters around Taiwan remain strong as the typhoon moves northwards," the Central Weather Administration's Wuu Woan-hwa said at a briefing.

Champi is the latest in a busy Pacific storm season turbocharged by the El Nino weather phenomenon that has caused unprecedented warming in the equatorial Pacific.

The storm was briefly a super typhoon as it crossed the ocean in recent days, with reported maximum sustained wind speeds of nearly 300 kilometres (186 miles) per hour.

It was packing wind speeds of 120 kph on Saturday, according to the latest update from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center.

The storm's intensity weakened overnight as it made a loop off Taiwan's northeastern county of Yilan, where it has dumped 65 cm of rain since Thursday, the forecaster said.

Martha Wang said she was afraid of being "blown away" by the wind as she rode her scooter across a bridge in New Taipei City on Saturday morning.

"I was really scared because I was on the bridge. My scooter was shaking," the 55-year-old secretary told AFP.

William Yu, however, was unfazed by the storm, saying it "wasn't any stronger than other typhoons."

"I went to the convenience store to eat yesterday (evening) and everything was fine," the 55-year-old librarian said.

- 'Strong winds and heavy rain' -

Authorities in China warned of "strong winds and heavy rain" as Champi approaches the country's east coast, state-controlled broadcaster CCTV said.

Some train services have been suspended and tens of thousands evacuated from their homes in Shanghai.

"Some areas of Jiangsu, Shanghai, Zhejiang, and other regions are expected to experience heavy to torrential rainfall," it said.

Dozens of flights have been cancelled in the region, including in Japan's southernmost prefecture of Okinawa where the government said two people were injured in the typhoon.

Tourists on Ishigaki island waited for flights to resume so they could return home.

"We hope it's our last day," Eva Malek, 49, from Poland told AFP.

"It's not easy to have information. We were not aware of the situation and didn't expect something like this to happen. When the typhoon arrived we didn't think it would be that strong."

The United Nations said Wednesday that the El Nino system gripping the planet is heading off the charts and that countries should take urgent action to prepare for the worst.

El Nino is expected to peak in December, but the human impact is set to last into 2027 and beyond.

The warming phase of a natural climate cycle, El Nino temporarily raises sea temperatures in the tropical Pacific, triggering changes in weather that can increase the risk of drought and flooding and exacerbate human-caused global warming.

By Joy Chiang With Celia Cazale In Ishigaki

World.title: Ebola vaccine trial begins in DR Congo
World.content:
BERN - The first clinical trial of an Ebola vaccine in the outbreak gripping the Democratic Republic of Congo began Friday, the head of the World Health Organization said.

The DR Congo's worst-ever Ebola outbreak has passed the 9,700-case mark, with the number of deaths exceeding 4,600.

Among the many challenges facing the response is the lack of any approved vaccines or treatments for the Bundibugyo species of Ebola behind the epidemic.

Ervebo, a vaccine approved for use against the more common Zaire strain of Ebola, will be put through a full-scale human trial in the DRC to see if it offers any cross-protection against Bundibugyo.

The trial began with the first shot of Ervebo being administered in Bunia, the capital of the DRC's northeastern Ituri province, which is the epicentre of the outbreak.

"Science gives us hope. Today, in Bunia DRC, the first participants were vaccinated in a new Ebola vaccine trial called Tumaini, which means 'hope' in Swahili," WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on X.

"This trial will help us understand whether any of the vaccine candidates designed for Bundibugyo virus work," he said, adding that in the meantime, the existing Ervebo vaccine would be tested.

"WHO is supporting this DRC-led effort to find answers and save lives."

- Two vaccines in the pipeline -

The so-called Tumaini trial is a single trial framework that can test the safety, efficacy and immunogenicity of multiple vaccines.

The trial will use a ring vaccination approach: immunising contacts deemed to be at high risk of infection.

It is gearing up to incorporate two Bundibugyo-specific candidate vaccines, which are currently advancing through earlier-stage, smaller-scale clinical trials.

One is a ChAdOx1 adenoviral vector jab being developed by the University of Oxford; the other, by the US-based Moderna group, uses mRNA technology.

Both have received funding from the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations, and are expected to enter the trial "shortly", CEPI said in a statement.

"Tumaini will work closely with affected communities, health authorities and outbreak response partners to generate robust evidence on vaccine performance that could contribute to curtailing the epidemic, saving lives, and strengthening preparedness for future Bundibugyo outbreaks," said CEPI.

The trial will include pregnant women and children aged 12 years and older, generating evidence for populations that are often excluded from clinical trials.

- 'Important step' -

WHO emergencies director Chikwe Ihekweazu said the trial was set up to generate the rigorous evidence needed to determine whether the participating vaccines could protect people at risk.

"If successful, this would be the first time we have clear evidence of vaccine efficacy against Bundibugyo virus, a major advance that could transform how we respond to this outbreak and prepare for future outbreaks and help save lives," he said.

Ebola, which spreads through contact with bodily fluids and causes a haemorrhagic fever, has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the past 50 years.

"Bringing this trial into the Ebola response is an important step towards addressing the urgent needs of affected communities," said Steve Ahuka-Mundeke, the DRC Ebola response incident manager.

The DRC declared its 17th outbreak of Ebola on May 15, and the WHO two days later triggered a public health emergency of international concern, its second-highest alert level.

By Robin Millard

World.title: Several feared trapped in Eastleigh building collapse
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

What was supposed to be a usually busy Friday afternoon in Eastleigh's 9th Street turned chaotic after an 18-floor building that was under construction came down, tumbling.

By Friday evening, rescue operations were still ongoing, with cries from people believed to have been trapped being heard from a distance as bulldozers and rescuers continued the search operation.

Two victims, a man and a woman, who were injured in the building had been rescued and rushed to hospital as the search continued.

Asha Jilo, one of the witnesses, said the building collapsed around 1:09 pm just after the afternoon prayers.

"Immediately after the building collapsed, we started contacting some people we know who work there, one of them was still available on the phone until around 3 pm, when his phone went offline," Jilo shared

On Fridays, Eastleigh is usually a hive of activities, being the main market day, but all the businesses were shut as police were battling rowdy youths, some of them believed to be opportunists.

The building, whose height was said to be about 15 floors, had not been cleared for occupation as required, raising questions about why the investors had allowed it to be taken.

It is said that the ground and first floors were already occupied by businesses, raising fears that the number of victims could be high. Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

At the time of the collapse, it is said that some construction workers were busy on the upper floors.

Governor Johnson Sakaja, who visited the scene after the collapse, was still gathering information about the building. The first priority was about saving lives.

“The building that collapsed is around 16 floors, and we have got information about the building, but what is more concerned right now is for us to save lives,” said Sakaja

Adding, “Equipment has already been mobilized, excavators and breakers, so we can be able to remove the big debris and save lives,’

The Governor said some developers engage qualified professionals to secure construction approvals before dismissing them and disregarding approved plans and safety standards.

He urged professional bodies to strengthen oversight, investigate such cases and take appropriate disciplinary action, stressing that developers must comply with approved designs, engage qualified personnel and obtain occupation certificates after safety inspections.

Rescue efforts at the collapsed storey building in Eastleigh 9th street in Nairobi County. [Benard Orwongo Standard]

Nairobi Regional Police Commander Issa Mohamud, who was at the scene, said that, according to reliable information, several people were trapped inside the debris, inside the big boulders, and the rescue effort is ongoing.

The city police boss said investigations will be carried out to ascertain who is responsible for any negligence.

“If there will be any death, that is negligence by murder. Whoever is the owner, whoever authorized the building, all of them will be charged properly. But that will come after thorough investigation is done,” he warned

Adding, “We will not excuse anybody on this matter. This has become now and then, and we will make sure that people face the law accordingly for any criminal negligence,”

World.title: Ruto hands over COMESA chairmanship, pushes for levy to fund regional programmes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President Ruto and Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa during the handover of the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa chairmanship at the bloc’s 25th Summit of Heads of State and Government in Harare, Zimbabwe, on Thursday, October 22, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has handed over the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA) chairmanship to Zimbabwean President Emmerson Mnangagwa.

Ruto took over the one-year chairmanship from Burundi’s President Évariste Ndayishimiye at the 24th COMESA Summit in Nairobi on October 9, 2025.

His tenure focused on using digital technology to deepen regional integration, expand trade and promote inclusive growth.

He handed over the role on Thursday, October 22, during the 25th Comesa Summit of Heads of State and Government in Harare, Zimbabwe, where he urged the regional bloc to fast-track a market levy to finance its programmes and institutions.

“We cannot be ambitious in our plans and timid in our financing. Every programme we agree upon must be matched by the resources to deliver it. Otherwise, our communiqués will promise what our budgets cannot pay for,” Ruto said.

He urged the Comesa Secretariat to fast-track Article 168 of the COMESA Treaty, which provides for the Comesa Market Levy, as the organisation seeks sustainable and predictable financing.

The treaty establishes the levy to generate resources for financing the bloc’s activities.

Ruto said officials from finance ministries, central banks and other relevant agencies would meet to consider a draft COMESA Resource Mobilisation Strategy aimed at strengthening member states’ ownership of regional programmes and finding new ways to raise funds.

He called on member states to make financing central to their discussions, warning that the bloc’s institutions and integration agenda would depend on their ability to fund agreed commitments.

“Can we finance what we commit, and deliver what we finance?” he asked.

Ruto also urged African countries to channel more of their domestic financial resources into African institutions rather than leaving funds in foreign accounts while development projects lack capital.

He said Africa holds more than $4 trillion in domestic financial assets, arguing that regional financial institutions could mobilise more of these resources to support trade, infrastructure and development.

Ruto named the Trade and Development Bank (TDB), the African Trade and Investment Development Insurance (ATIDI) and ZEP-RE among the institutions that could mobilise capital for regional priorities.

He urged African governments to place more reserves with these institutions, finance more projects through them and support their bonds and guarantees.

The outgoing Comesa chairperson said the bloc needed stronger regional value chains and more trade among member states as global supply chains faced disruption and protectionism returned.

“Regional integration is no longer a dream we discuss. It is an economic and strategic necessity,” he noted.

Ruto said Comesa’s economic growth rose from 5.6 per cent in 2024 to 6.4 per cent in 2025, while inflation fell from 31 per cent to 13.2 per cent.

Exports among member states increased by 10.5 per cent to $14.7 billion, their highest level between 2020 and 2025, while exports to global markets rose by 6 per cent to $212 billion, he said.

He argued that African countries needed to process more raw materials locally instead of exporting them and importing finished products.

“To every partner who seeks our minerals, our markets and our young workforce, our offer is clear: invest with us, process with us, build with us,” Ruto added.

He called for partnerships based on mutual benefit and equal treatment, saying African countries should have a greater role in determining how their resources and markets contribute to economic development.

World.title: Judge certifies fresh bid to jail Sakaja, Charles Kerich over Sh76.7m debt as urgent
World.content:
Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja. [File, Standard]

The High Court has certified as urgent a fresh application seeking to have Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja, former Finance Executive Charles Kerich and two other county officials jailed over an alleged breach of a court-approved payment plan in a Sh106.7 million legal fees dispute.

Justice Francis Gikonyo certified the application by Kwengu & Company Advocates seeking to reinstate a three-month jail sentence previously imposed on Kerich and hold Sakaja, current Finance County Executive Committee Member Ibrahim Auma Nyangoya and Chief Officer for Finance Asha Abdi accountable for the alleged failure to pay Sh76.7 million.

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.

World.title: Industry Minister: Egypt Forum 2026 to address manufacturing challenges, boost investment
World.content:
Minister of Industry Khaled Hashem said Egypt Forum 2026 would help strengthen the industrial sector by addressing challenges facing manufacturers and fostering dialogue between the government and industry stakeholders to promote growth, attract investment and support domestic production.

In an interview with Extra News on Friday, October 23, 2026, Hashem said holding the forum at this time reflects the government’s commitment to listening to manufacturers, removing obstacles to their operations and developing practical solutions to the challenges they face.

These efforts, he added, would help create more opportunities for young people and support Egypt’s broader economic development.

The minister noted that the government is working to simplify industrial licensing procedures and accelerate the approval process through clear, streamlined mechanisms.

He also highlighted the role of universities in contributing ideas and proposals at the forum, saying their participation could help address challenges facing the industrial sector in the coming period.

Hashem further announced the implementation of new measures to simplify the procedures factories must follow to obtain insurance documents through the Ten-Year Insurance Pool (Al-Mogamaa Al-Ashariya).

The measures are intended to reduce the financial and administrative burdens on industrial investors, speed up project implementation and facilitate the start of production.

He reaffirmed the government’s commitment to reviewing and streamlining administrative procedures and expanding their digitization to improve the business environment and encourage industrial investment.

World.title: PM’s remarks on electricity load shedding taken out of context
World.content:
The Cabinet’s Media Center denied reports attributed to Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly suggesting that electricity load-shedding cuts could last between six and eight hours daily.

In a statement issued Thursday, October 22, 2026, the Media Center said the remarks were taken out of context and did not reflect any actual decision to implement load shedding.

Madbouly made the comments during a session titled “Egypt’s Energy Journey: National Achievements and Future Prospects,” while discussing possible scenarios for addressing rising energy prices.

The Prime Minister outlined three options: passing the full increase in energy costs on to citizens, having the state absorb the entire increase, or keeping the budget allocations and purchasing petroleum products at the new prices within available resources.

He explained that the third option could cover only 50–60% of citizens’ needs, potentially forcing the government to consider more difficult measures, including electricity load-shedding cuts for six to eight hours a day.

World.title: Egypt completes detailed urban plans for two North Sinai cities
World.content:
Minister of Local Development and Environment Manal Awad announced the completion of detailed urban plans for the cities of Nakhl and Al-Hasana in North Sinai Governorate, aimed at regulating urban expansion, optimizing land use and identifying future needs for roads and public services.

The move comes as part of the state’s efforts to improve public services and advance comprehensive development across the Sinai Peninsula, in line with directives from President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi.

Awad received a report from Said Helmy Abdel Khaleq, head of the Local Planning and Integrated Local Development Sector, outlining the completed plans and their role in regulating urban growth, guiding land use and establishing a framework for development in the coming years.

According to the report, the area designated for Nakhl is set to expand from 369 feddans to 1,251 feddans by 2037, providing a planning framework to accommodate projected urban and population growth and identify locations for activities and services needed to meet residents’ future requirements.

The detailed urban plan for Al-Hasana covers 403 feddans and defines land uses, traffic circulation routes and road networks to guide urban development and support orderly expansion.

Awad said completing the plans marked an important step toward improving urban planning in both cities by clarifying land-use designations and identifying requirements for roads and public services.

These measures, she added, would help improve living standards and create a more organized urban environment for residents.

She affirmed that the ministry would continue coordinating with relevant authorities and North Sinai Governorate to advance local planning and development, taking environmental and urban planning standards into account while supporting essential services and infrastructure, promoting economic development and creating job opportunities for local residents.

The minister explained that detailed urban plans are essential tools for managing urban growth, as they designate residential, commercial, service and industrial uses and establish main and secondary road networks. Such plans help curb unplanned expansion and unauthorized construction while ensuring that development takes into account residents’ current and future needs.

For his part, Abdel Khaleq stressed that the plans would help set priorities for urban expansion, identify infrastructure and service needs, improve land-use efficiency and guide development and investment in accordance with designated land uses and applicable planning regulations.

World.title: We are not at war with the Houthis, Egypt’s parliament assures
World.content:
The Chairman of the Foreign Affairs Committee of the Egyptian House of Representatives, Sameh Shoukry affirmed that Egypt’s mandate to take measures to defend Saudi Arabia is not intended to launch offensive military operations inside Yemen.

During an interview with the Egyptian al-Nahar TV channel on Friday, Shoukry said that Egypt’s position “is not linked to any form of aggression.”

He explained that the statements made by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi on this matter are clear and consistent with both Egypt’s diplomatic policy and the doctrine of its armed forces.

He stressed that Egypt is not at war with the Houthis or any other party, and that Cairo is working to avoid war and military operations.

Shoukry emphasized that the mandate granted by the House of Representatives to the President of the Republic relates specifically to the defense of Saudi Arabia and the implementation of necessary measures to protect it and safeguard Arab national security.

He emphasized that Arab national security is an integral part of Egyptian national security, and that the security of Egypt and Saudi Arabia are closely linked—a reality that necessitates working within a comprehensive Arab framework to confront threats.

Aiding Saudi Arabia

Shoukry’s remarks follow statements by President Sisi, in which he requested a mandate from the House of Representatives to authorize the necessary measures to provide military support to Saudi Arabia, should the need arise.

Sisi on October 17 affirmed Egypt’s readiness to take the necessary steps to defend Saudi Arabia, should Riyadh request it.

Subsequently, on October 21, he clarified that any Egyptian military action would be strictly limited to defending Saudi Arabia’s territory and borders, and would not extend to launching an offensive into Yemen.

World.title: Fuel prices on Saturday following decision of Automatic Pricing Committee for Petroleum Products
World.content:
Egyptian citizens have grown increasingly concerned over gasoline and diesel prices following decisions by the Automatic Pricing Committee for Petroleum Products, as these prices directly impact transportation costs and the pricing of goods and services.

In an official statement issued in the middle of October, the Committee announced that prices for petroleum products would remain unchanged.

This decision followed a review of various local and global factors that influence pricing, including international oil prices and the exchange rate of the Egyptian pound against foreign currencies.

Committee’s Decision

The decision to maintain current petroleum product prices follows the resumption of the Automatic Pricing Committee’s operations, as ordered by the Cabinet.

The Committee reviewed both domestic and global economic variables—such as international oil price trends and pricing measures implemented over the preceding period—that influence fuel pricing.

This review encompassed the parameters of the pricing mechanism for the July to September quarter, compared to the previous quarter, ultimately resulting in the decision to keep existing prices unchanged.

Fuel Prices

According to the prices stipulated in the decision, the prices for gasoline, diesel, and kerosene per lite—as of, Saturday—are as follows:

92-octane gasoline: LE 22.25.

95-octane gasoline: LE 24.00.

Diesel: LE 20.50.

Kerosene: LE 20.50.

Prices for butane gas cylinders on Saturday:

12.5 kg domestic butane gas cylinder: LE 275.

25 kg commercial butane gas cylinder: LE 550.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Melania Trump says she secured one-city ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine for humanitarian aid
World.content:
First lady Melania Trump announced on Friday that she helped secure a localized ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the city of Oleshky to facilitate the humane evacuation of elderly residents.

Trump worked directly with Ukrainian and Russian leadership as the “exclusive intermediary,” according to a press release from the first lady’s office, and initiated discussions to secure the terms of the ceasefire agreement. The Russian Ministry of Defense said in a statement it would implement the ceasefire in the region beginning at 4 a.m. Moscow time on October 27, and Ukraine officials said it would do the same at three am Kyiv time on the same day.

Both Russian and Ukrainian officials on Friday confirmed the limited ceasefire. Ukrainian authorities said around 1,700 civilians remain in the city and supply routes for food and medicine have been blocked.

“Oleshky’s remaining population is comprised primarily of elderly residents who urgently need medical attention, medicine, food, and clean water,” Trump said in a statement. “The people of Oleshky have limited electricity, live amid mined roads, and endure regular military attacks. It was abundantly clear that without my intervention, the possibility to bring humanitarian aid into the city and to evacuate the elderly would be impossible.”

“Non-military, civilian leaders from both countries will work together to visit Oleshky residents in their homes and determine the level of assistance they require. Residents who wish to evacuate will receive coordinated support and transportation to their preferred destination. I anticipate some will want to go to Russia, and some to Ukraine,” she added.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov credited Trump for her “significant contribution.” He said Russian leader Vladimir Putin and President Donald Trump discussed the topic in a recent call, as CNN has previously reported.

“The military is working to coordinate a ceasefire in that area to facilitate this humanitarian mission. Those who wish to leave the settlement will be able to do so. Naturally, this requires extensive and complex preparation, involving a wide range of different representatives,” Peskov said.

Peskov declined to provide specifics on the evacuation routes or how long the ceasefire would last, only saying the operation would “certainly take at least a few days.” Dmytro Lubinets, the Ukrainian Parliament commissioner for human rights and a leader in negotiations, said the “operation will take place gradually; it is extremely complex to carry out.”

Davyd Arakhamia, a member of the Ukrainian parliament and part of the negotiations, said he would “like to highlight the roles played by the Pope and US First Lady Melania Trump.”

CNN previously reported that Pope Leo discussed the humanitarian crisis in Oleshky on a phone call with Putin last Friday while in the hospital recovering from lung cancer surgery, according to the Vatican. The Kremlin said that Putin “supported” the Vatican’s intention to help alleviate the conditions.

“An operation to lift the blockade of the town of Oleshky and its surrounding areas will begin shortly. Its goal is to establish permanent humanitarian corridors for the safe evacuation of civilians and the delivery of aid,” Arakhamia said in a statement.

“To achieve this goal, a ceasefire will be established in the near future, as announced by U.S. First Lady Melania Trump,” he continued.

Donald Trump praised his wife’s efforts on Friday, saying “they contacted both sides, and both sides wanted to do it.” He said that her focus remains on helping the children impacted by the war.

“What she wants to do is save children,” the president said. “That’s her focus. Both sides are cooperating with her, so doing a very good job.”

Asked if the first lady would be part of potential trilateral talks with Russia and Ukraine, Trump said: “No, but that’s not the worst idea I’ve ever heard.”

The first lady’s office said that the circumstances of Oleshky came to her attention during a private discussion at the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York.

Communication lines were already opened, given Trump has been involved with the reunification of children that have been separated from their families due to Russia’s war against Ukraine.

Melania Trump said Friday she “secured an impartial American media organization to accompany and document Russian and Ukrainian teams on the ground throughout the process.” The right-wing network Newsmax subsequently said that it was “granted exclusive television access to accompany a delegation of Russian and Ukrainian observers entering Oleshky on Oct. 29.”

Concerns about the poor humanitarian conditions in Oleshky were raised during a briefing hosted by the Ukrainian and Norwegian embassies in Washington, DC, earlier this week.

Denys Sienik, the top Ukrainian diplomat in Washington, said that Russia has not allowed the Red Cross to deliver desperately needed food, clothing and medicine to the people there, many of whom are elderly.

Oleksandra Matviichuk, a Ukrainian whose organization won the Nobel Peace Prize, said that “because of constant hostilities, landmines, and manned-drone attacks, people can’t leave the city.”

“People are eating grass,” she said, noting that the last official food delivery was in May.

Matviichuk added that under international law, Russia, as an occupying force, has an obligation to provide food, medicine and drinking water to the population under its control.

Lack of power is an issue too. Residents are freezing to death because the generators have run out of power, according to Zarina Zabrisky, an independent journalist based in Kherson.

“I had multiple reports of bodies left to rot in the roads. And since there were a lot of abandoned animals there, including dogs, there are packs of wild dogs consuming the human remains,” she said.

This story has been updated with additional information.

World.title: Israel begins demolitions in West Bank city after two soldiers killed in shooting attack
World.content:
Israel began demolishing buildings and forcing residents to evacuate a neighborhood in the occupied West Bank on Friday, hours after two Palestinian gunmen opened fire on an Israeli military checkpoint, killing two soldiers.

Three more soldiers were lightly wounded in the attack in the city of Hebron, according to the Israel Defense Forces (IDF).

The attack came just four days before Israel holds elections for the first time since the Hamas-led attack on October 7, 2023, in a crucial test for Netanyahu, who has sought to portray himself as a security hardliner.

The IDF said after the attack it was imposing “a full siege” on the city of Hebron and Netanyahu said he had ordered a full closure of the West Bank starting Friday.

Hours later, Netanyahu appeared to scale back plans for a full closure of the territory, saying he would consider “a cordon” around the cities of Hebron and Halhul that may extend to other areas.

Netanyahu also said the military would forcefully evacuate the area of the attack and “transform it completely,” employing the plan used in the Jenin, Tulkarm, Nur Shams, and Al-Far’a refugee camps in early 2025, which led to the displacement of thousands of Palestinians and the evacuation of entire neighborhoods.

Israeli authorities launched a several-days-long counterterrorism operation in the Hebron area, the military and Israeli Security Agency (ISA) said in a joint announcement.

“The forces have begun conducting precise, targeted and thorough searches throughout the area to locate and dismantle terrorist infrastructure and weapons, while questioning suspects,” the statement said, adding that the operation is confined to the area from where the gunmen operated.

The IDF and ISA said residents living in the area will be able to leave through three designated exit points and will be subject to questioning and security screening. Those who “raise suspicion” will be referred to security forces for further questioning.

The military and ISA added that the operation is a continuation of counterterrorism measures being taken since the morning, including “mapping the terrorists’ residences, imposing a cordon on the areas of Hebron and Halhul, establishing roadblocks, and conducting counterterrorism activities in areas throughout the sector.”

The statement also said “illegal structures that could pose a security threat” in the area are being demolished.

Israeli human rights organization B’Tselem condemned the plan to “forcibly displace Palestinian residents” from the Hebron neighborhood.

“Israel is announcing its next crimes in advance,” the group’s executive director Yuli Novak said. “Netanyahu and (Israeli defense minister, Israel) Katz have declared their intention to empty a Palestinian neighborhood in Hebron and repeat the mass displacement and destruction inflicted on the northern West Bank refugee camps.”

By Friday afternoon, Israeli forces had started demolitions in the Farsh al-Hawa area of Hebron. In video obtained by CNN, an Israeli soldier tells residents of a housing complex: “You have five minutes to evacuate.”

“That is exactly what we will do here, in a neighborhood in Hebron from which the terrorists came. We will evacuate the residents, go house to house, remove weapons found there, and address and destroy all terrorist infrastructure,” Netanyahu said.

Forces continued searches across the area for anyone else who may be connected to the attack. Both gunmen were shot and killed earlier Friday, the IDF said.

Videos from the scene depict a firefight between the Palestinian gunmen and Israeli forces that lasted at least several minutes with repeated bursts of gunfire ringing out. In one Reuters video, an Israeli responder yells that the shooting has been going on for at least 20 minutes and they were struggling to remove the wounded from the scene.

The IDF said it located a vehicle used by the gunmen to carry out the attack, which was filled with “a large quantity” of ammunition. “This was a serious terror attack,” said IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir following a situation assessment. “The fighters’ rapid action prevented an even more serious attack and further harm to civilians and security forces.” He said the ammunition in the car was intended to be used “to carry out an attack on a much larger scale.”

Zamir said the IDF would also carry out further arrests of suspects and increase intelligence operations in the area.

“We will pursue Hamas terrorists and those who sent them, wherever they are and at all times,” Netanyahu said in a statement.

A police officer walks with bagged evidence at the scene of the shooting. Ammar Awad/Reuters

Hamas praised the attack in a statement but did not claim responsibility.

“Together with all the people of Israel, I pray for the full and speedy recovery of those wounded in the attack,” said Netanyahu’s main rival, former IDF Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot, said in a statement on X.

This story has been updated with the latest developments.

World.title: Liberia: Judge Cites Evidence in Finding NSA Staff Peter Bon Jallah Guilty of Statutory Rape, Kidnapping
World.content:
Criminal Court E Acquits Him of Gang Rape; Orders Pre-Sentence Report Before Sentencing

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh

Monrovia — Assigned Circuit Judge Wesseh Alphonsus Wesseh Sr. has found 63-year-old Peter Bon Jallah, a staff member of the National Security Agency (NSA), guilty of statutory rape and kidnapping, but not guilty of gang rape in a case involving a 16-year-old boy.



In a verdict delivered Friday, October 23, Judge Wesseh said he had reviewed the evidence presented by both parties and considered the arguments advanced during the trial before determining that the prosecution had established sufficient grounds to convict Jallah on two of the three charges.

The judge framed his decision around three central questions: whether the prosecution’s evidence justified a conviction for gang rape, statutory rape and kidnapping.

He answered the first question in the negative, acquitting Jallah of gang rape, but answered the other two in the affirmative, finding him guilty of statutory rape and kidnapping.

Following the verdict, Judge Wesseh ordered Jallah remanded at Monrovia Central Prison pending the submission of a pre-sentence and behavioral report by the Bureau of Probation Services at the Ministry of Justice.

The judge directed the clerk of court to communicate with the probation authorities to ensure that the report is made available as soon as possible to assist the court in determining the appropriate sentence.

Judge Identifies Three Decisive Questions

In his ruling, Judge Wesseh said the court had examined the facts and circumstances contained in the evidence presented at trial before identifying three issues that were decisive to the case.

On the gang rape charge, the judge concluded that the prosecution’s evidence did not provide sufficient and reasonable grounds to convict Jallah. He consequently declared the defendant not guilty and acquitted him of that charge.

However, on statutory rape, the judge found that the evidence presented by the prosecution provided sufficient grounds for conviction.

He reached a similar conclusion on the kidnapping charge, finding Jallah guilty on that count as well.

The ruling represents a split decision in a case that involved allegations of repeated sexual abuse of a minor and the alleged confinement of the complainant for several days.

Indictment Details Alleged Repeated Abuse

According to the indictment summarized in the court’s verdict, Jallah and two unidentified men were indicted by the Montserrado County Grand Jury during the February 2026 Term of Court for gang rape, statutory rape and kidnapping.

The indictment alleged that Jallah and the two other men acted individually and jointly in sexually abusing the complainant on multiple occasions.

It further stated that the complainant, who was 16 at the time of the alleged incidents, lived in the Airfield Shark Community in Monrovia and regularly visited Jallah’s residence to perform domestic work for which he received compensation.

The indictment alleged that on November 29 and December 24, 2025, Jallah lured the boy to his residence in the Sharks Community of Airfield Sinkor, where he allegedly sexually assaulted him.

The most serious allegations concerned an incident said to have occurred on January 1, 2026, after the boy participated in a community football league at the Kpelle Town football field.

According to the indictment, the boy encountered Jallah near his residence after the game. Jallah allegedly offered to purchase football boots for him and instructed him to return home to bathe before accompanying him.

The indictment alleged that the two subsequently travelled by car to a building in the Camp Johnson Road area of downtown Monrovia, where the boy was allegedly held for three days and sexually abused by Jallah and the two unidentified men.

It further alleged that on January 3, 2026, at about 10 p.m., the boy was concealed at the back of Jallah’s vehicle and abandoned along 15th Street in Sinkor.

The complainant was reportedly rescued by private security guards, who alerted his parents. His mother and other relatives subsequently took him to the John F. Kennedy Medical Center for medical examinations.

These details formed part of the allegations contained in the indictment and should not be interpreted as separate findings by the court unless expressly established in the judge’s ruling.

Case Faced Procedural Delays

The court’s verdict also outlined the procedural history of the case, which experienced several delays before proceeding to a full trial.

The case was initially before Criminal Assizes Court “A” for Montserrado County before being transferred to Criminal Court “E” for evidentiary proceedings and a full trial.

Jallah was arraigned on June 18, 2026, and pleaded not guilty to the indictment. He subsequently elected to be tried by a judge without a jury.

The trial was delayed after the prosecution filed a motion seeking a change of venue. Following the denial of that motion, the prosecution petitioned the Chamber Justice for a writ of certiorari, but the petition was denied and the case was ordered to proceed.

The proceedings encountered another setback when the judge previously presiding over the matter could not continue taking evidence after the regular sitting of the court expired.

On August 5, 2026, the case was reassigned for trial.

According to the written verdict, the prosecution presented 13 regular witnesses and six rebuttal witnesses, while the defense called eight regular witnesses and three subpoenaed witnesses from the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection, Orange GSM and the John F. Kennedy Medical Center.

The prosecution’s witnesses included the complainant, police investigators, medical personnel and Rwandan forensic examiner Pascal Bavugirije.

The defense witnesses included Jallah himself and several other individuals who testified on his behalf.

The number of witnesses listed in the written verdict differs from earlier accounts that referred to 12 prosecution witnesses, making the court’s official record the appropriate reference for the final tally.

DNA and Medical Evidence Featured at Trial

The prosecution relied in part on forensic findings linking Jallah’s DNA profile to biological material recovered from four clothing exhibits.

However, testimony attributed to the forensic examiner indicated that the findings could not establish precisely when or how the biological material was deposited.

The defense challenged the prosecution’s interpretation of the evidence, pointing to alleged inconsistencies in the complainant’s account and limitations in the medical and forensic findings.

Medical evidence also featured prominently in the proceedings. Earlier accounts of the trial referenced a John F. Kennedy Medical Center report that reportedly found no visible signs of anal trauma, while the parties disputed the significance of the medical and forensic findings.

The precise weight the court assigned to each item of evidence should be established from the complete written ruling and trial record. The verdict provided identifies the court’s conclusions on the three charges but does not detail its assessment of every witness or exhibit.

Prosecution and Defense Clash in Final Arguments

During final arguments on Thursday, October 22, prosecution lawyer Cllr. Calvin H. Momolu urged Judge Wesseh to convict Jallah, maintaining that the evidence presented during the trial supported the charges.

Defense lawyer Cllr. Wilfred Sayeh argued that the prosecution had failed to prove its case to the required legal standard. The defense questioned the police investigation and challenged the interpretation of the medical, forensic and testimonial evidence.

The judge adjourned the proceedings until Friday morning to review the evidence and arguments before delivering the verdict.

In reaching his decision, Judge Wesseh found the prosecution’s evidence sufficient to convict Jallah of statutory rape and kidnapping, while concluding that it did not warrant a conviction for gang rape.

The two other men named in the indictment were not brought under the court’s jurisdiction and were not tried alongside Jallah in these proceedings.

Defense Plans Appeal

Following the verdict, defense lawyer Cllr. Sayeh announced plans to appeal the ruling to the Supreme Court of Liberia.

The planned appeal would give the defense an opportunity to challenge the lower court’s decision before the country’s highest court.

In the meantime, Jallah remains ordered remanded at Monrovia Central Prison while the Bureau of Probation Services prepares the report requested by Judge Wesseh.

The report is intended to assist the court in determining the sentence to be imposed following the guilty verdicts.

The case now enters the sentencing stage before the anticipated appeal, with the court having found Jallah guilty of statutory rape and kidnapping but acquitted him of gang rape.

World.title: Liberia: Court Finds Peter Bon Jallah Guilty Of Statutory Rape, Kidnapping
World.content:
Jallah had pleaded not guilty to all charges, while his defense challenged the prosecution’s evidence, citing alleged inconsistencies in the complainant’s account and limitations in the medical and forensic findings.

— Acquits NSA Staff of Gang Rape; Defense Announces Supreme Court Appeal

MONROVIA, Liberia — Criminal Court “E” at the Temple of Justice has found 63-year-old Peter Bon Jallah, a staff member of the National Security Agency (NSA), guilty of statutory rape and kidnapping but not guilty of gang rape in a case involving a 16-year-old boy.

By Victoria Wesseh



The verdict was handed down Friday, October 23, 2026, by Assigned Circuit Judge Wesseh Alphonso Wesseh Sr., following final arguments by the prosecution and defense on Thursday.

Following the verdict, Judge Wesseh ordered Jallah’s remand at Monrovia Central Prison. However, the court had not announced the sentence at the time of reporting.

Defense lawyer Cllr. Wilfred Sayeh has announced plans to appeal the ruling to the Supreme Court of Liberia, setting the stage for another legal battle over the verdict.

The court acquitted Jallah of gang rape. The two other individuals allegedly involved in the incident on Camp Johnson Road were not presented during the trial.

Prosecution Presented 12 Witnesses

During the trial, prosecutors presented 12 witnesses, including the complainant, police investigators, medical personnel, and Rwandan forensic examiner Pascal Bavugirije.

The prosecution also relied on DNA findings that linked Jallah’s DNA profile to biological material recovered from four clothing exhibits.

However, the forensic examiner reportedly testified that the findings could not establish when or how the biological material was deposited.

Jallah had pleaded not guilty to all charges, while his defense challenged the prosecution’s evidence, citing alleged inconsistencies in the complainant’s account and limitations in the medical and forensic findings.

Defense Challenges Evidence, Plans Appeal

During Thursday’s final arguments, prosecution lawyer Cllr. Calvin H. Momolu urged the court to convict Jallah, arguing that the evidence presented during the trial supported a guilty verdict.

Defense lawyer Cllr. Sayeh countered that the prosecution had failed to establish the allegations beyond a reasonable doubt. The defense questioned the interpretation of medical and forensic findings, as well as aspects of the police investigation.

The competing arguments centered on witness testimony, medical findings, forensic evidence, and whether the prosecution had sufficiently established the elements of the charged offenses.

With the guilty verdict on two charges and the defense’s announced intention to appeal, the case is expected to proceed to the Supreme Court, where Jallah’s lawyers will seek a review of the lower court’s decision.

This news is breaking. More details to follow.

World.title: Liberia Poised to Surpass 2026 Intellectual Property Registration Target
World.content:
The Government of Liberia, through the Liberia Intellectual Property Office (LIPO), has announced that it is on track to surpass its annual intellectual property registration target after recording 526 registrations by the end of the third quarter of 2026.

Speaking at the Ministry of Information’s regular press briefing on Thursday, LIPO Director General Hon. Garmai Koboi noted that the Office had achieved 95.6 percent of its annual target of 550 registrations — expressing confidence that the current pace of registrations would push the year-end figure beyond the projected benchmark.

According to Hon. Koboi, trademarks accounted for the overwhelming majority of registrations, with 483 recorded during the period, followed by 40 copyright registrations and three industrial designs.

Of the total, Hon. Koboi further disclosed that 174 of the registrations were by Liberian-owned businesses and foreign nationals with established business operations in the country.



“With 526 applications recorded against an annual target of 550, we have achieved 95.6 percent of our FY2026 intellectual property registration target, leaving an outstanding balance of just 24 applications, representing 4.4 percent of the annual target,” Hon. Koboi added. “This performance reflects the work we are doing to strengthen intellectual property awareness and engagement among businesses, entrepreneurs, and other key stakeholders through targeted outreach, capacity-building initiatives, and stakeholder collaboration.”

According to Hon. Koboi, the uptake in registration is down to LIPO’s ongoing efforts to make intellectual property services more accessible, particularly to entrepreneurs, creators, and small businesses seeking to protect and commercialize their innovations, brands, and creative works.

“These achievements reflect the progress we are making toward building a stronger and more inclusive intellectual property ecosystem in Liberia,” the Director General said. “By supporting enterprise development, promoting creativity and innovation, strengthening intellectual property protection, and expanding access to IP services for SMEs and creators, we are seeing a lot of uptake in our registration and use of the IP system.”

Highlighting LIPO’s other achievements, Hon. Koboi pointed to the implementation of the Business and Intellectual Property Management Clinic (BIPMC), undertaken in partnership with the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) through its GROW-2 Project.

The initiative, according to LIPO and UNIDO, reached 142 entrepreneurs across Lofa, Bong, Nimba and Margibi counties, providing practical training, business advisory support and technical guidance on intellectual property identification, registration and management.

At the closure of the clinic, 90 intellectual property applications were filed for the first time by enterprises in these counties, of which 39 resulted in the issuance of intellectual property registration certificates to applicants who satisfied the legal and regulatory requirements under the Liberia Intellectual Property Act of 2016.

The project, according to Hon. Koboi, forms part of a broader national effort by the Government to integrate intellectual property protection into business development, particularly in agriculture, food processing, fashion, manufacturing and other sectors where entrepreneurs increasingly rely on brands, creative designs and product differentiation to compete in the marketplace.

Speaking also, Hon. Koboi noted that LIPO, in collaboration with the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), has expanded the 2nd edition of the Intellectual Property Management Clinic (IPMC) to 40 SMEs in four counties, providing specialized one-on-one mentorship support to 40 small and medium-sized enterprises across Montserrado, Nimba, Bong and Lofa counties.

The initiative provides training and technical advisory support to participating businesses in order to help them strengthen their intellectual property management practices, minimize infringement risks and identify opportunities for business growth and market expansion.

“These projects support the government’s commitment under the ARREST Agenda to its 2029 vision of developing a robust intellectual property ecosystem, as they expand access to intellectual property protection services for businesses and creators while equipping them with the knowledge and practical guidance needed to understand, protect, and effectively manage their intellectual property assets,” Hon. Koboi noted.

Meanwhile, Hon. Koboi has noted that one of the greatest achievements for the office this year has been the successful completion of the national stakeholder validation of Liberia’s National Intellectual Property Policy and Strategy (NIPPS), describing the exercise as an important step toward establishing a coordinated framework for intellectual property development.

The document is intended to strengthen coordination among public institutions and other stakeholders while positioning intellectual property as a tool for innovation, enterprise development, creativity and economic diversification.

The completion of the validation exercise represents a key milestone in Liberia’s efforts to establish a more structured national approach to intellectual property development, although further steps will be required before the framework becomes fully operational.

The LIPO Director General has also disclosed that the institution is preparing to digitize its intellectual property registration services through the Intellectual Property Administration System (IPAS), with technical assistance from WIPO. The planned introduction of the system is expected to modernize the administration of intellectual property applications, streamline registration procedures, and improve the efficiency of service delivery.

In a separate development, the LIPO Director General has appealed to the Liberian Senate to give attention to outstanding international instruments submitted by the President for ratification, emphasizing their potential importance to the country’s agriculture, tourism and creative sectors.

Hon. Koboi noted that the ratification of relevant instruments could strengthen Liberia’s ability to benefit from international intellectual property protection frameworks, particularly in areas involving geographical indications and the protection of products associated with specific geographical origins.

“We also want to appeal to the Senate to look at all outstanding instruments submitted by the President for ratification,” Hon. Koboi noted. “These instruments are very cardinal to our agriculture sector, for example, looking at our potential geographical indications, including our Liberian coffee, the tourism sector, our local government and the creative industries.”

Geographical indications are intellectual property protections used to identify products whose qualities, reputation or other characteristics are linked to a particular geographical origin.
