World.title: Justice chancellor: Income Tax Act could lead to unfair treatment of heirs
World.content:
The Office of the Chancellor of Justice has asked the Ministry of Finance to explain why heirs may face income tax on the sale of inherited property even when the proceeds are used to repay the deceased's debts.

A person who purchased a property jointly with their spouse, with each owning half as separate property, contacted the chancellor of justice after their spouse died and they inherited the deceased spouse's share together with their minor child.

An inventory of the estate revealed that its liabilities exceeded the value of its assets by approximately €57,000. The person who contacted the chancellor of justice had also pledged their separately owned home, where they live with their child, as additional collateral for the loan. However, when they sought to sell the inherited property quickly to repay the loan, they discovered that the deceased spouse's acquisition cost of their share of the property could not be transferred to the heirs.

The Estonian Tax and Customs Board (MTA) also failed to take into account that the heir had already been making loan payments while their spouse was still alive but in a coma. According to an illustrative calculation by the MTA, selling the property would leave the heir liable for approximately €15,000 in income tax.

"The petitioner believes that they are required to pay income tax in this situation even though using the proceeds from the sale to meet the inherited loan obligations would leave them with no financial gain," explained Evelin Lopman, an adviser to the chancellor of justice and head of the business environment department.

According to the Office of the Chancellor of Justice, assessing the situation requires determining whether the exclusion of the deceased's property acquisition cost is consistent with the constitutional right to property, the principle of proportionality in taxation and the requirement of equal treatment.

To resolve the matter, the office is seeking an explanation from the Ministry of Finance as to whether the objective could be achieved in a way that places a smaller burden on the heir. It also wants to know what justifies the restriction in cases where an estate's liabilities exceed the value of its assets, the obligation to repay a loan taken out to purchase the property passes to the heir and the property is sold to meet the deceased's obligations.

"Would it be justified to establish a legal exception for such situations, based on the heir providing additional documentary evidence?" Lopman asked the Ministry of Finance.

"When assessing the proportionality of the restriction, do you consider it relevant to take into account situations where the heir's own home serves as collateral for the inherited obligation and failure to meet that obligation could result in the sale of the home?" Lopman added.

Lopman also highlighted the fact that when a surviving spouse sells securities that were part of the spouses' joint marital property, they can deduct 100 percent of the acquisition cost, as provided for in the tax authority's guidelines. She questioned why the sale of inherited real estate is treated differently.

Lopman is seeking clarification from the Ministry of Finance on whether it considers changes to the regulations necessary. The ministry has just over a month to respond.

World.title: Iraqi PM adviser accuses Iran of severe border violations and smuggling
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A senior adviser to Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi has openly accused Iran of orchestrating deliberate security breaches, widespread drug smuggling, and illicit financial flows across the border, marking a rare and pointed public rebuke from within Baghdad’s executive circle as Iraq shuttered key commercial crossing points.

Speaking to domestic media, prime ministerial adviser Abdelamir Taiban stated that Tehran has actively undermined Iraqi internal stability by allowing unauthorized, affiliated networks to bypass border protocols, inciting borderland disorder.

Taiban noted that Iraqi nationals have faced abductions after entering Iranian territory, identifying the areas surrounding the Shalamcheh terminal in Basra and the Al-Sheeb terminal in Maysan as high-risk corridors. He urged the federal government to aggressively scale electronic monitoring and comprehensive automation across every operational terminal along the shared 1,599-kilometer frontier.

The adviser characterized the inbound traffic of narcotics and counterfeit currency as the most damaging economic threat facing the nation, asserting that the resulting market sabotage has inflicted financial disruption outpacing the economic fallout previously caused by ISIS.

The remarks follow the indefinite closure of the Al-Sheeb port of entry in Maysan governorate to both travelers and commercial cargo—a measure following the precautionary shutdown of Shalamcheh in September amid regional drone incidents—which prompted demonstrations by local transport operators and cross-border truckers concerned over disrupted trade in fresh produce and construction materials.

In response, Prime Minister Al-Zaidi convened the Ministerial Council for National Security, ordering security units to safeguard peaceful assemblies while maintaining stringent checks to intercept illicit trafficking channels.

World.title: US dollar dips to 168,500 IQD following Zaidi’s remarks on cash inflows
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar retreated by approximately 1,000 dinars per $100 across parallel market trading desks on Saturday, October 24, 2026.

The softening followed public statements delivered on Friday by Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi, in which he disclosed that Washington will dispatch $1 billion in physical cash shipments to Iraq and assured the public that parallel rates will soon decline toward 155,000 dinars per $100.

The remarks stemmed upward momentum that had pushed dollar transactions across domestic exchange bureaus to 169,500 dinars on Thursday and Friday, driving the prevailing market benchmark down to 168,500 dinars.

Across major trading hubs in Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra, foreign exchange desks and licensed counters posted identical rates on Saturday morning, listing cash selling quotes at 169,000 dinars against buying bids of 168,500 dinars per $100.

Despite the temporary retreat, parallel figures continue to maintain a notable spread over the Central Bank of Iraq’s official statutory cash peg, which remains set at 152,000 dinars per $100.

The divergence highlights persistent liquidity dynamics and demand pressures outside central electronic settlement channels, even as executive assurances of incoming dollar consignments aim to stabilize market sentiment and curb speculative price premiums.

World.title: US State Department reissues Level 4 ‘Do Not Travel’ advisory for Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The U.S. Department of State issued a renewed travel advisory on Saturday, October 24, 2026, maintaining its highest “Level 4: Do Not Travel” warning for Iraq and urging American citizens to avoid travel to the country under any circumstances.

According to the advisory, Washington cited the inability of Iraqi authorities to guarantee the safety of foreign nationals in the event of sudden armed conflict or localized violence, while emphasizing the U.S. government’s severely constrained capacity to execute emergency evacuations or consular relief operations inside Iraqi territory.

The State Department warned of acute security and public health vulnerabilities, citing risks from terrorism, kidnappings, civil unrest, and frequent asymmetric strikes. It specified recurring hazards from improvised explosive devices (IEDs), unmanned aerial systems, and indirect rocket fire conducted by Iran-aligned armed groups and remnants of ISIS against U.S. personnel, diplomatic compounds, commercial companies, energy installations, and commercial airports.

The advisory also drew attention to regional escalation vectors—including cross-border hostilities conducted by the Houthi movement—as well as widespread unmarked minefields and UXO hazards, aviation restrictions implemented under Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) notices, and severe structural shortages across Iraq’s trauma and emergency medical infrastructure.

In response to sustained security threats, strict operating restrictions remain enforced on U.S. diplomatic personnel, requiring special authorization for in-country travel and residency within heavily fortified protocols.

For private American citizens currently residing in Iraq, the State Department urged immediate contingency planning independent of U.S. governmental assistance, including enrolling in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP), drafting emergency wills and power-of-attorney designations, leaving DNA reference samples with family medical providers, securing private medical and emergency evacuation insurance, and developing comprehensive personal departure protocols.

World.title: Iraqi FM Fuad Hussein condemns deadly church attack in Jordan’s Karak
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein held a telephone conversation on Friday, October 23, 2026, with Jordan’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates, Ayman Safadi, strongly condemning the deadly armed attack that targeted mourners at a church in Jordan’s southern Karak Governorate.

During the call, Hussein conveyed Iraq’s full solidarity with the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan in confronting terrorism and violent extremism.

The Iraqi foreign minister extended the government and people of Iraq’s heartfelt condolences to the leadership, government, and citizens of Jordan, as well as to the families of the victims, while wishing a swift recovery to those injured.

The diplomatic outreach followed a shooting incident earlier on Friday, in which unidentified gunmen opened fire during a funeral service at a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hmoud, located in Karak Governorate approximately 180 kilometers south of Amman.

The attack left at least seven people dead and dozens wounded, prompting heightened security deployments and an active manhunt by Jordanian security agencies.

World.title: Ukraine says two soldiers died after arrested girl sent Russian poison
World.content:
Kyiv – Ukrainian police said Friday they had detained a 17-year-old girl suspected of helping Russia’s security services to poison Ukrainian soldiers and that two had died.

Ukraine and Russia have throughout their war since 2022 accused each other of recruiting minors for sabotage acts including poisoning.

The girl, who was not named, is suspected of having packaged deadly drugs and sending them to Ukrainian soldiers she contacted by Telegram, said a police statement.

She was arrested by police in Zhytomyr, west of Kyiv, after allegedly following instructions from a Russian handler in exchange for at least 5,000 hryvnias ($111), they said.

After receiving packages with “free drugs”, the soldiers were “instructed to take them on camera”, the statement said.

“The recipients did not know that the capsules contained a lethal dose of methadone,” it said, adding that “two soldiers died from poisoning in the Zhytomyr region.”

Police said they had identified other recipients of the packages, which “prevented four more murders” across the country.

“The young woman was notified that she is suspected of aiding and abetting the premeditated murder of two people as part of a prior conspiracy,” the police statement said.

She was also suspected of “shipping drugs and psychotropic substances for the purpose of distribution”, it said, adding that she faced up to 15 years in jail if found guilty.

Police cautioned that Russia aims “to kill our people and destabilise the situation within the country”.

“Do not accept medication or other substances, as well as food or drinks of dubious origin, from people you do not know well,” police cautioned.

Since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, Ukrainian authorities say they have opened thousands of investigations into collaboration with the enemy, and frequently arrest individuals accused of working for Moscow.

In 2023, Ukraine accused Russia of poisoning the wife of Kyrylo Budanov, who was then head of Ukraine’s military intelligence and is now a presidential advisor.

World.title: Volvo Cars shares plunge on losses, job cuts
World.content:
Stockholm – Shares in Swedish carmaker Volvo Cars plunged Friday after it said US tariffs and strong competition from local brands in China pushed it into a third-quarter loss.

The company also said it would cut about 2,500 jobs worldwide.

Volvo Cars, controlled by Chinese group Geely, reported revenue of 66.9 billion kronor ($6.7 billion) for the third quarter, down nearly 23 percent from the same period last year.

It swung to a net loss of 5.7 billion kronor for the quarter from a net profit of 4.5 billion kronor a year earlier.

Shortly after 0800 GMT, Volvo Cars shares were down almost 30 percent.

“We continue to operate in a very tough environment with strong external challenges: de-globalisation, hypercompetition and climate change,” chief executive Hakan Samuelsson said in a statement.

In response, the company announced a new five-billion-kronor savings plan it said would lead to about 2,000 job cuts in Sweden and 500 more globally, “through natural attrition and by targeted exit packages to employees”.

The company, which had bet heavily on electric vehicles, said the removal of consumer incentives for EVs in the United States under President Donald Trump had also hit its margins.

In 2024, Volvo Cars dropped a plan to transition to exclusively EV sales by the end of the decade.

“We are convinced that we have the right long-term strategy addressing these challenges,” Samuelsson said.

“However, in the short term, with severely challenged volumes, we need to reinforce our turnaround plan with additional decisive actions, lowering our break-even point and improving cash flows to make us more resilient.”

Struggling along with other European auto companies in the face of a difficult global landscape, Volvo Cars last year announced an 18-billion-kronor cost-cutting plan.

The company said in September that Samuelsson would resign when his contract ends, with Skoda Auto CEO Klaus Zellmer set to replace him “no later” than October next year.

World.title: France braces for new protests as Macron seeks to restore order
World.content:
Paris – France was on Friday bracing for a weekend of new protests after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago, as President Emmanuel Macron sought to reclaim the initiative and restore order.

Macron, who on Thursday announced that only union demonstrations would be authorised this weekend, was to hold a meeting of his defence council of top ministers and officials and also meet security forces.

He was also set to host for the first time representatives of high school pupils, whose protests over conditions at their schools sparked a movement that has broadened nationwide into a show of anger against the government at the rising cost of living.

The protests have come at a critical moment for France six months ahead of elections to replace Macron, with a new poll underlining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is the frontrunner and showing her position has been strengthened by the latest events.

Adding to tensions, Le Pen is at the weekend due to host her National Rally (RN) party congress in Orleans, with thousands of supporters expected but local authorities fearing clashes as opponents head to the city.

Macron is due to announce “additional decisions” after hosting the meeting of his defence council, on top of the limited curfews already announced, his office said.

At the meeting with students, “we will present our demands to him — which remain the same: the state of school infrastructure and an overhaul of the Parcoursup (university admissions) system,” Nathanael Combary, president of Renouveau Lyceen (High School Renewal) told AFP.

Pierre Sourzat, who heads the organisation Les Lyceens (The High School Students), was sceptical: “He’ll listen to us, pretend he’s understood us, and then nothing will come of it.”

Macron’s government has sought to draw a line between the legitimate demands of protesters and the looting, burning and ransacking that erupted on the sidelines of protests last Saturday.

In a judicial response of unprecedented firmness, courts have already sent 217 people, half of them first-time offenders, to prison over the events on Saturday, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said.

On Thursday, Macron called for “the utmost severity” against “acts of delinquency”, accusing “ultra-left” groups of having sought to “bring down the republic” last weekend.

– ‘Police have a responsibility’ –

Demonstrations in Marseille in the south and Lyon in the southeast have been banned at the weekend, while in Paris protesters will only be allowed to march a limited route between Bastille and Nation squares.

Marseille authorities however reversed a decision to halt all public transport in the city on Saturday. But in the capital, leading museums including the Louvre will be closed on Saturday while the Art Basel art fair is being cut short.

Some 20 percent more members of the security forces will be deployed this weekend after heavy criticism of the anticipation and intelligence gathering of police last week.

“In a country governed by the rule of law, the police have a responsibility both to ensure that protests can take place peacefully and safely and to protect the public from violent disorder,” said Eva Cosse, senior Europe researcher at Human Rights Watch, expressing alarm over reports of children being severely injured by crowd-control weapons.

The violence has tarnished the image of France ahead of elections that could be a turning point in its modern history, with the government’s debt pile also troubling investors.

A new poll by Harris Interactive for M6/RTL made after the violence showed Le Pen soaring ahead on 33-35 percent in the first round of voting for the presidential elections.

It predicted that hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon was on course to face her in the run-off where Le Pen would emerge as an easy winner on some 70 percent of the vote.

World.title: Kering shares tumble as Gucci fails to reassure investors
World.content:
Paris – Kering shares were down more than 10 percent in Paris Friday after the French luxury group published results that failed to reassure investors about a turnaround at its key Gucci brand.

At 0730 GMT, Kering shares were down 10.8 percent at 190.40 euros, their lowest since June 2025. The market’s CAC40 index was down 0.3 percent.

Kering reported late Thursday that third-quarter sales were flat at 3.34 billion euros ($3.75 billion).

Sales at Gucci, by far the group’s largest single brand, fell by four percent to 1.29 billion euros, worse than the three-percent decline registered in the second quarter.

“Gucci has not shown convincing signs of stabilisation,” Deutsche Bank analysts said in a note.

Italy-based Gucci is key to Kering’s fortunes, but has been in freefall since 2023 as the brand lost its luxury cachet.

World.title: 'Insult to Uttarakhand': Akhilesh Yadav's 'infiltrator' jibe draws sharp response from CM Dhami
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

on Saturday hit back at

(SP) president

Akhilesh Yadav

over his âghuspaithiyaâ (infiltrator) remark targeting a person from the hill state.

In a video shared by news agency IANS, the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister is seen saying, âWho is the biggest infiltrator in Uttar Pradesh? He is from Uttarakhand.â

The remarks appeared to be directed at Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath, who was born in Pauri Garhwal district when it was part of undivided Uttar Pradesh. The region is now in Uttarakhand, which was carved out of Uttar Pradesh in 2000.

In response, Dhami accused Akhilesh Yadav of âinsultingâ the people of Uttarakhand. He also invoked the 1994 Rampur Tiraha firing incident, in which Uttar Pradesh Police opened fire on activists campaigning for a separate Uttarakhand state.

Akhilesh Yadavâs father, Mulayam Singh Yadav, was the Uttar Pradesh chief minister at the time.

"Uttarakhand is both the Devbhoomi (land of Gods) and Veerbhoomi (land of the brave). This sacred soil has given the nation numerous saints, soldiers, and individuals devoted to national service. Shri Akhilesh Yadav ji, calling the people of Uttarakhand infiltrators, is an insult to the pride of the Devbhoomi and to our struggles," Dhami posted on X.





"The people of Uttarakhand also have not forgotten that when Akhilesh Yadav ji's father, Mulayam Singh Yadav, was the chief minister of Uttar Pradesh, bullets were fired at the agitators demanding a separate Uttarakhand state at Rampur Tiraha in Muzaffarnagar. Bullets were fired at Uttarakhand's agitators during the father's regime, and today the son is calling the people of Uttarakhand infiltrators! The people of Uttarakhand can never forget their struggles and sacrifices," he added.

World.title: ‘No hesitation in detaining youth’: Congress targets government over US national VanDyke’s release in Myanmar arms case
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress on Saturday questioned the decision to allow US national Matthew VanDyke, an accused in the Myanmar arms training case, to return to his home country, asking why a foreign national accused of terrorism was being granted such liberty while young activists protesting against alleged âvote choriâ were being detained.

Congress general secretary in charge of communications Jairam Ramesh raised the issue in a post on X, referring to VanDyke's release and the extension of permission for him and six Ukrainian nationals to remain outside India until February 24 next year.

âUS national Matthew VanDyke, arrested for conspiring to carry out terrorist activities against India, was released yesterday and allowed to return home for 4 months.

Why has such liberty been extended to a foreign national accused of terrorism?â Ramesh asked.

He also criticised the government's handling of protests against alleged electoral irregularities.

âThis even as the government has shown no hesitation in detaining and arresting youth activists and peaceful protesters during the anti-vote chori protests this past month,â he said.

Ramesh further pointed to the issue being raised during US secretary of state

's visit to India in May, noting that the American official had visited again this week.





Congress raises questions over US intervention

Ramesh had previously accused Prime Minister

of being a âcompromised PMâ following VanDyke's release in September.

The Congress leader had claimed that Rubio raised the matter during his May visit to India and that US ambassador to India Sergio Gor also took it up with foreign secretary Vikram Misri.

On September 8, Ramesh claimed that charges under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) had been dropped against VanDyke.

He alleged that this contrasted with what he described as the widespread misuse of the law against Indian citizens and delays in such cases.

After VanDyke was released on September 24, Ramesh alleged that the prime minister had âfailedâ to protect India's elections, institutions and national security.

Court allows seven accused to remain abroad till February 24

A Delhi court on Friday extended until February 24, 2027, the permission granted to VanDyke and six Ukrainian nationals to remain outside India while the National Investigation Agency (NIA) continues its probe into the Myanmar arms training case.

Special Judge Prashant Sharma passed the order after hearing applications filed by the seven accused. The proceedings were held in-camera.

The NIA sought additional time to investigate several aspects of the case, with its counsel Rahul Tyagi making submissions to that effect. The agency told the court that further investigation was needed to verify alleged offences under the UAPA in connection with the import and recovery of large quantities of drones and accessories through India.

VanDyke appeared in person before the court on Friday and was permitted to return to the US.

The other six accused attended the hearing through video conferencing, citing health issues.

The seven foreign nationals had earlier been permitted to stay in their home countries until October 23 after seeking six weeks to meet their families.

NIA alleges training of armed groups in Myanmar

The NIA has alleged that VanDyke and the six Ukrainian nationals entered India on tourist visas, travelled to the northeastern region without the required permits and crossed from Mizoram into Myanmar, where they allegedly trained ethnic armed organisations.

The accused were arrested on March 13 over allegations of training insurgent-linked groups in Myanmar.

The agency had initially invoked provisions of the UAPA, including those relating to conspiracy.

However, its chargesheet did not include the UAPA provisions and instead invoked Sections 21 and 23 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act. These provisions cover offences that can be compounded before the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO).

The NIA had previously indicated that its investigation into the alleged terror-related aspects was continuing and that further allegations could be included in a supplementary chargesheet.

World.title: Why do some women become the strongest defenders of patriarchy
World.content:
âSir, let me say that I am not a feminist. I consider myself as a human being. As a human being we feel that it is our duty to help women, minorities, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, OBCs, and also the neglected class.â Mamata Banerjee in Lok Sabha on Womenâs Day, 2008.

Oxford dictionary defines

feminism

as 'the belief and aim that women should have the same rights and opportunities as men or the struggle to achieve this aim.'

Then why is it that some of us distance ourselves from this term? And why is it that some women uphold the very patriarchy that restricts them?

Why do some women keep patriarchy alive

A group called the NCMIndia Council for Men Affairs recently took out a 'Long Live Patriarchy' march that went viral on social media.

The group also had women holding the banner. "In the name of equality, these girls don't want to do jhaadu-pocha, clean utensils or raise kids.

They just want freedom, money and debauchery," one of the women at the march said. "Equality does not mean freedom to drink, smoke, roam around at night. Women are misusing their independence.

Azaadi

does not mean shaming men."

TOI spoke to Dolly Kumari, who is also a member of the group that actively raises men's issues, and asked her what patriarchy meant to her.

"Patriarchy cannot be understood simply as a system created by men to oppress women. When a woman speaks about men's issues, some people may find it surprising because they expect her to speak only from a particular gender-based perspective. But I do not believe empathy should have a gender. Supporting men who experience injustice does not mean denying the difficulties women face," she said.

"My objection is to the idea that everything traditional must be condemned as patriarchal and, therefore, bad. If a man wants to protect and provide for his family, and a woman willingly chooses to trust him in that role, why should society automatically call that oppression or brainwashed women?"

Oxford dictionary defines patriarchy as 'âa society, system or country that is ruled or controlled by men.'





It would appear, then, that women supporting patriarchy would be an anomaly. However, Dolly said that the purpose of their 'Long Live Patriarchy' initiative was to raise awareness of men's rights, which "we have been organising on Gandhi Jayanti for nearly a decade."

"Equality should not become a competition between men and women. Women deserve justice, and so do men. We need a society where both can express their pain, seek support, and live with dignity without being judged by gender stereotypes," said Dolly.

"In the traditional Indian family, men were often expected to provide, protect and take responsibility for their families while women traditionally took on many responsibilities related to the home and children. These roles evolved within the social and economic realities of their time although it resulted in unequal rights and restrictions. Our history is not simply a story of oppression and therefore patriarchy should prevail.

"

Is the 'aurat hi aurat ki dushman' concept real?

Does different treatment of a son from daughter and parenting play a role in keeping misogyny alive? Or is this 'aurat hi aurat ki dushman hoti hai' syndrome.

Devika Anand, a psychologist at Rise and Mind, believes that the answer lies partly in the way gender roles are normalised within families and communities.

"I think one way to understand this is that we don't always question the systems we grow up in, particularly when those systems are presented to us as normal, moral, or necessary.

When a woman grows up learning that a good woman is one who sacrifices, adjusts, tolerates, or puts others before herself, these expectations can become deeply embedded in her understanding of what it means to be a woman," she said.

Over time, these expectations may stop feeling like restrictions and start being seen as values. A woman may even derive a sense of identity or self-worth from having lived up to them, sometimes at considerable personal cost.

"When younger women choose differently, it can challenge not just her beliefs but also the meaning she has attached to her own sacrifices," Devika explained.

This explains why some women who have experienced restrictions themselves may go on to impose similar expectations on younger women. Having spent years adjusting to restrictive norms, they may come to regard them as an inevitable part of life rather than something that can be challenged.

"There can also be a need to make sense of one's own experiences. If someone has made significant sacrifices because she believed there was no alternative, acknowledging that those sacrifices were unnecessary or unfair can be painful. It may bring up feelings of anger, grief, or regret. Believing that younger women must make similar sacrifices can sometimes help preserve the sense that those sacrifices had a purpose," Devika said.

When certain expectations are repeatedly reinforced within families and communities, they can become the default way of relating to others. A woman may reproduce the same expectations she experienced, not necessarily because she wants younger women to suffer, but because she has learned to see those expectations as responsible or appropriate behaviour.

From 'mere sar mei dard hai, iska karan marrd hai' to 'ek sutta, 2 chai, marrd jaat haye haye', the protest saw viral slogans. (PTI image)

Can patriarchy give women a sense of power?

"Power doesn't always mean having equal power within a system.

Sometimes, it means having more power than someone else within that system," Devika said.

In a patriarchal family, a woman may have limited autonomy in relation to men but still hold considerable authority over younger women, daughters-in-law or other women in the household. She may have little influence over the rules themselves but gain status by enforcing them.

"This can give her a sense of belonging, security, or control in an environment where her own power is otherwise limited," Devika explained.

There can also be a psychological incentive to conform. If a woman receives approval, respect or recognition for upholding family traditions, questioning those traditions may threaten not only her beliefs but also her position within the family or community.

When tradition becomes a question of freedom

Calling kindness, compassion, empathy and nurture 'qualities' that women should have, Dolly said, "I feel that relationships are increasingly being discussed in terms of personal freedom, sometimes without equal emphasis on duties, compromise, commitment, and mutual accountability."

Dolly believes that a woman does not have to reject tradition to prove that she is empowered. "I come from a traditional, patriarchal family, yet my father always encouraged me to participate in activities that people might traditionally associate with boys. I played sports, learned to ride a bike, built a career in technology, and today have a beautiful family of my own. Growing up with two brothers also gave me a personal experience of sharing opportunities and responsibilities across gender lines.

That experience is one of the reasons I believe that having a traditional father or growing up in a strict household does not automatically mean being oppressed. Tradition and discipline are not inherently oppressive," she said.

Devika, too, cautions against labelling every woman who holds a traditional belief as a victim of internalised misogyny, which may include judging women more harshly than men, policing other women's behaviour, or believing that women are inherently less capable or less deserving of autonomy," she said.

When women challenge the rules they grew up with

A 65-year old influencer from Haryana called Tai Savitri, who recently went viral over her commentary on society and patriarchy, told TOI that even though her experiences have been bitter, it was her educated children that taught her to become a feminist. "I was less educated. My kids got good education so I learnt a few things from them. It was also a feeling that I should do something for the women," she told TOI.

She recalled facing criticism in her village, even though her family did not offer much resistance to her views.

"Yes, I have also heard that aurat hi aurat ki dushman hoti hai but I think it is more because of lack of education that pitied one woman against the other, a system wherein one woman was the slave of another. This created a scenario where women did not want other women to succeed in life," she said.

In one of her viral videos, Savitri compared women who restrict other women to dogs that have become accustomed to living on a leash.

"You must have seen dog owners taking their pets out. Even if they let go of this leash, by mistake or deliberately, you will notice that the dog itself will hold the leash in his mouth and give it back to his owner. Because the dog has now developed a habit of living like a slave and it has accepted its fate.

It is the same with women who try to show other women in poor light. It is the same slave mentality. My only message to women is

kutta nahi sher bano

(don't be a dog, be a tiger). Whoever tries to put a leash on you or make you a slave, rip them to shreds," she said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Patriarchy gives some women a sense of belonging

There is a distinction between having a choice and the freedom to make that choice. Holding a traditional belief is not the same as denying another woman the right to choose differently. The consequences of that belief, and the degree to which it is imposed on others, matter.

Women who defend patriarchal expectations are not necessarily motivated by a single cause. Their views may be shaped by the values they grew up with, the sacrifices they have made, the security they derive from their place within a family or community, or a genuine belief that traditional arrangements offer stability.

The question, then, is not simply why some women become flagbearers of patriarchy. It is also why a system that can restrict women's choices sometimes offers them identity, belonging or authority in returnâand what it would take for women to feel secure enough to question it.

Perhaps the more useful question is not whether women are their own enemies, but whether a society that teaches women to measure their worth through sacrifice, obedience and conformity gives them enough room to imagine a different way of living.

World.title: MEA condemns deadly church attack in Jordan that killed eight
World.content:
India on Saturday condemned a deadly attack on a Greek Orthodox church in Jordan that killed eight people and injured several others, expressing solidarity with the Jordanian government and people.

In a statement, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "India unequivocally condemns the heinous attack at a Church in Karak, Jordan on 23rd October 2026, which resulted in the tragic loss of several innocent lives and injuries to many others. We extend our heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and wish a swift recovery to those injured in this cowardly attack. India stands firmly with the Government and the friendly people of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan in this difficult hour.

We also reaffirm our strong commitment to the fight against terrorism in all its forms and manifestations."

External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar also condemned the attack and expressed condolences to the victims' families.

The attack took place on Friday at a church in the village of Hammoud in the Karak governorate, where gunmen opened fire on a funeral procession. The death toll rose to eight on Saturday after one of the injured victims, who was in critical condition, died, Health Minister Ibrahim al-Bdour told AFP.





Another 26 people remain hospitalised, including one in critical condition, the minister said.

Jordan vows action after attack

Jordanian Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya described the shooting as a terrorist attack and said security forces were working to track down those responsible.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"A terrorist group has carried out a horrific act, one that is condemned in every respect, and the security services are working round the clock to track them down," he told a press conference.

King Abdullah II, who visited the wounded at a hospital in Karak, also condemned the attack and said on X that the shooting "will be met with the harshest retaliation".

Prime Minister Jafar Hassan ordered three days of national mourning beginning Friday, with flags to be flown at half-mast over government and public institutions.

Karak is home to a significant Christian community in Jordan, a Muslim-majority country where Christians account for between two and three per cent of the population.

World.title: Ashoke Sen: Indian Physicist honoured with 2026 Oskar Klein Medal for string theory work
World.content:
Physicist Ashoke Sen has been awarded the 2026 Oskar Klein Medal, becoming the first physicist from India to receive this honour.

Sen, who holds the ICTS-infosys Madhava chair professorship at the International centre for theoretical sciences (ICTS), tata institute of fundamental research (TIFR), Bengaluru, is widely recognised for his pioneering contributions to modern string theory.

String theory proposes that the fundamental building blocks of matter are tiny, one-dimensional strings rather than point-like particles. The theory seeks to provide a unified framework for understanding matter and the forces governing interactions between its constituents.

Established in 1988, the Oskar Klein Medal is named after Swedish theoretical physicist Oskar Klein. It is awarded annually by stockholm university and the nobel committee for physics of the royal swedish academy of sciences.

As part of the oskar klein memorial lectures, a distinguished researcher is invited each year to deliver a lecture in klein's memory and receive the medal.

Sen delivered his memorial lecture, titled âgravity from strings and strings from gravityâ, on October 22 at the AlbaNova university centre in Stockholm.

His presentation explored how string theory can provide a consistent quantum description of gravity and help address unresolved questions surrounding the quantum physics of black holes.





Contributions to modern string theory

A recipient of the Padma Shri in 2001 and the Padma Bhushan in 2013, Sen has made several influential theoretical contributions that have helped shape the field of string theory.

His work was recognised with the breakthrough prize in fundamental physics in 2012. The research helped establish the idea that different string theories could be understood as distinct limits of a single underlying theory.

In a statement, ICTS highlighted Sen's internationally recognised contributions to S-duality, the precise counting of black-hole entropy and string field theory, describing them as key areas of work that have helped shape modern string theory.

World.title: 'Rubbing salt into wounds': BJP targets Rahul over Nov 1 rally, recalls 1984 anti-Sikh riots
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party on Saturday upped the ante against Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, accusing him of rubbing salt into the wounds of the Sikh community by holding an INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1 - the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots in Delhi following the assassination of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.Addressing a press conference, senior BJP leader Ravi Shankar Prasad questioned the Congress leader's insistence on holding the rally on the date."Why is Rahul Gandhi so adamant about holding his rally in Delhi on November 1? This issue is being raised very seriously by our party. November 1 is a day that holds deep emotional significance for the Sikh community, as they remember the 1984 massacre with profound sorrow," Prasad said."So, by creating a storm at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, what kind of salt does Rahul Gandhi want to rub into their wounds?" he asked.The BJP leader also said that many members of the opposition alliance were not satisfied with the decision to hold the rally on November 1."We have heard that many members of their alliance were also not satisfied with this decision. We have also received information that a virtual meeting was convened on October 22 to discuss this issue.However, since many allies did not attend, the meeting was postponed," he said."We have also learnt that several allies were unhappy with the November 1 date and had suggested that the rally be postponed to a later date. This reflects Rahul Gandhi's true face. When he insists on something, he refuses to listen to anyone. If he is determined to have his way, he will go ahead, even if it means cruelly mocking the sentiments of the Sikh community," the BJP leader said.The opposition rally aims to ramp up pressure on the government over the "vote chori" issue and demand Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.On October 12, protests over the "vote theft" charge reached the Supreme Court's doorstep, with opposition leaders, activists and civil society members participating in a 'March for Democracy' along a heavily barricaded route in Delhi and filing a joint petition against the SIR.Rahul hosted INDIA bloc leaders for tea at his home on October 13. After the meeting, the opposition bloc vowed to continue resisting and take the "vote chori" fight to its logical conclusion.

World.title: When Sonia met Rajiv: Congress leader narrates her 1st meeting with husband in X debut
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson

made her debut on social media platform X on Saturday, sharing a video in which she recalled her first meeting with former Prime Minister

and offered a glimpse of her upcoming book, Belonging: A Journey of Love.

The book, Sonia Gandhi's first, is scheduled to be launched on November 10. It recounts her personal journey, including her memories with Rajiv Gandhi and experiences from her younger days to the present.

In the nearly two-minute video accompanying her first post on X, Sonia Gandhi recalled meeting Rajiv Gandhi at the Varsity Restaurant, a Greek eatery in Cambridge, England, where they were students.

The video featured photographs of the couple and the restaurant where they first met.

"In a small Greek restaurant in Cambridge, my journey of love began. Rajiv and I created a world filled with love, laughter and memories. On 10th November, I share that world with you," she wrote in her post.

Sonia Gandhi recalls meeting Rajiv Gandhi in Cambridge

Speaking in the video, the Congress MP recalled looking for Italian food while living in England, where she said the food available at the time did not suit her preferences.

"Food in England in those days was awful. In those days, you didn't have so many restaurants, you know, like you have today," she said.





She explained that she was looking for a place serving food closer to what she was accustomed to, particularly Italian cuisine, when she discovered the Greek restaurant.

"And then, we discovered this place (Varsity Restaurant). It was a Greek restaurant where many European students, but also Indian students, used to go for their meals. And that is then where I met Rajiv in that very restaurant," she said.

Recalling her first impression of Rajiv Gandhi, she said she felt almost immediately that he was someone she would want to spend her life with.

"When I first met him, I felt almost immediately that you know he was someone I would really love to be with. And, of course, I learned that it was the same for him," she said.

Sonia Gandhi also recalled that a common friend introduced them. The two subsequently became friends and began attending parties with other students and visiting places together.

"I remember when I first met him, a friend, a common friend, introduced us.

Then, you know, we became friends. Then going to parties with friends, or going to see sights, orâ¦ We went to a Valentine party where there were lots of students," she said.

Describing what stood out to her about Rajiv Gandhi, she said his gentle nature had left a lasting impression.

"He was a very gentle-looking person. Of course, he was very good-looking. But that gentleness came through. So that was something which really touched me and struck me.

So that, of course, I'll never forget when I first met him," she said.

Sonia married Rajiv Gandhi on February 25, 1968.

Upcoming memoir traces her personal journey

World.title: 'Will not sign': AISA chief Neha Bora defies Delhi police peace bond notice after HC setback
World.content:
NEW DELHI: All India Students' Association president Neha Bora on Saturday said she would not sign a bond to "keep peace" before a special executive magistrate, a day after the

dismissed her plea challenging the police notice directing her to furnish a Rs 10,000 bond with a surety.

"We don't have any conditions. We are not going to sign the bond," Bora said.

Bora had moved the high court, arguing that the notice was vague, factually incorrect and unsupported by material establishing the likelihood of a breach of peace.

She alleged that the proceedings were a "colourable exercise of preventive powers to suppress peaceful dissent, in violation of Articles 19(1)(a), 19(1)(b) and 21 of Constitution".

During Thursday's hearing, Bora's counsel argued that citizens did not need permission to hoist the national flag, referring to the police notice alleging that she had hoisted it without valid permission.

The notice, issued on October 17 under Section 126 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), directed Bora to appear before the magistrate on October 19 and explain why she should not execute a personal bond of Rs 10,000 with one surety "for keeping peace for a period of enquiry".





Bora was taken into preventive detention on October 16 while on her way to participate in the Cockroach Janata Party's (CJP) 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march at Central Park in Connaught Place. She was released the following day.

According to her petition, the police initiated proceedings over alleged sloganeering at Mandi House on October 16, repeated protests around Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS, and allegations that she had instigated people to join a demonstration at Connaught Place that day.

The petitioner's call and the incident alleged were different. The petitioner called for a peaceful gathering at Mandi House at 5.00 pm on Oct 16, and it is a matter of record that she was detained from Mandi House," Bora's petition stated.

World.title: India unequivocally condemns attack on church in Jordan’s Hamoud
World.content:
India on Saturday (October 24, 2026) unequivocally condemned an attack on a church in Jordan's Karak governorate that left at least seven people dead and 34 wounded. New Delhi said it stands "firmly" with the government and the "friendly people" of Jordan in "this difficult hour".

“Seven people were killed and 34 others sustained injuries when gunmen opened fire at a funeral in the church in Hamoud locality of Karak governorate on Friday (October 23, 2026),” according to authorities in Jordan.

"India unequivocally condemns the heinous attack at a Church in Karak, Jordan on October 23 which resulted in the tragic loss of several innocent lives and injuries to many others," the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said.

"We extend our heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and wish a swift recovery to those injured in this cowardly attack," it said in a statement.

"We also reaffirm our strong commitment to the fight against terrorism in all its forms and manifestations," the MEA added. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar too expressed anguish over the attack.

"Deeply shocked at the heinous attack at a Church in Karak, Jordan," he said on social media. "Our heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families and wish a swift recovery to those injured," he said.

World.title: Jamia protest: University shifts classes online to ensure ‘safety, security’ of students
World.content:
Jamia Millia Islamia university in Delhi on Saturday (October 24, 2026) announced that classes of all its courses have been shifted to online mode until further notice to ensure the “safety and security” of its students amid an ongoing protest demanding restoration of elected student representation on campus.

In an official notice, the university said this is a precautionary measure taken to safeguard students’ academic interests and to ensure “continuity in the teaching-learning process without any undue disruption”.

Several students have been staging a hunger strike since October 12 demanding the restoration of student union elections that were last held in 2006. JMI has not held student union elections since they were dissolved following campus violence.

Earlier in the week, Jamia constituted a committee to draft the constitution of its students’ union, which was dissolved in 2006. The five-member committee will be chaired by Zubair Meenai, Dean of the Faculty of Social Sciences.

The committee will examine the circumstances that led to the dissolution of the students’ union in 2006, relevant court rulings, and the recommendations of the Lyngdoh Committee (2007). It has been asked to consult all stakeholders, including students, and submit a draft by December 20.

The development followed the constitution of a high-level committee on October 18 to engage with protesting students and examine their demands. According to the university administration, the panel members held discussions with student representatives on October 19 and 20, but the students did not agree to sign the minutes of the discussions.

Rejecting the notifications, student representatives said the measures failed to address their three key demands: the immediate announcement of a schedule for the 2026-27 students’ union elections, revocation of disciplinary action against protesters, and removal of the Chief Proctor and the Security Advisor.

They alleged that the decision to constitute another committee to draft the union’s constitution by December 20 was a delaying tactic. The students said their indefinite hunger strike would continue until the university released the JMISU election notification and schedule.

With PTI inputs

World.title: Top news of the day: SC panel to hear pellet gun, harassment claims during NEET protests; Haryana gangsters detained in U.S.; and more
World.content:
Delhi NEET protest: SC panel to hear evidence on pellet gun use, harassment claims on Oct 29, 30

The Supreme Court-appointed High-Powered Enquiry Committee (HPEC), probing the alleged violence during the July Jantar Mantar protests, will hold a two-day sitting in New Delhi on October 29 and 30 to hear affected persons and record evidence on the alleged use of pellet guns and harassment of female protesters, officials said on Saturday (October 24, 2026).

Haryana gangsters Himanshu Bhau, Neeraj Faridpuria detained in U.S.

Gangsters Himanshu Bhau and Neeraj Faridpuria, wanted in several cases of murder, extortion and high-profile shootings, have been detained by U.S. authorities in Las Vegas following a tip-off from the Haryana Special Task Force (STF). Confirming the development, Haryana STF Inspector General Simardeep Singh told The Hindu that both gangsters had been detained in Las Vegas.

Neha Bora refuses to sign peace bond, questions curbs on dissent

All India Students’ Association president Neha Bora will not sign a peace bond before a Special Executive Magistrate, the student leader said on Saturday (October 24, 2026), a day after the Delhi High Court dismissed the plea challenging a police notice directing Neha Bora to provide a personal bond of ₹10,000 with one surety.

Delhi court orders trial of Yasin Malik, Engineer Rashid, five others in money laundering case

A court in New Delhi has ordered the trial of jailed separatist leader Yasin Malik, Baramulla MP Sheikh Abdul Rashid, alias Engineer Rashid, and five others in a money laundering case linked to alleged funding from Pakistan through hawala channels for secessionist activities in Jammu and Kashmir.

Odisha moves Supreme Court against Andhra Pradesh over rural poll notice in Kotia area

The Odisha Government has filed a contempt of court petition against the Andhra Pradesh Government in the Supreme Court, challenging its notification to conduct panchayat elections in the disputed Kotia region in the state’s Koraput district. Odisha’s Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari said the petition was filed through the district collector of Koraput after the Andhra Pradesh Government issued a notification on October 10 to conduct Zilla Parishad and Panchayat Samiti elections in the Kotia cluster of villages in Odisha territory.

CBI arrests proclaimed offender in fodder scam case

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested proclaimed offender Satyendra Kumar on Friday (October 23, 2026) in connection with a fodder scam case. According to the press statement issued by the CBI, after the filing of the charge sheet in the case in 2001, the accused Satyendra Kumar absconded, and the CBI was on the lookout for him for over 25 years. As he failed to appear before the court to face trial, a permanent warrant of arrest was issued against him by the Court.

J&K Cabinet reshuffle next week, list finalised: Omar Abdullah

Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Saturday (October 24, 2026) said his council of ministers would be expanded and reshuffled in the first two to three days of next week and urged party colleagues and MLAs not to seek ministerial berths as the list has already been finalised.

Israel launches major West Bank operation after soldiers killed

Israel’s military launched an operation in the occupied West Bank on Friday (October 23, 2026) it said would last several days and include searches and building demolitions, after gunmen killed two soldiers days ahead of Israeli elections in which security has been a key focus.

France to deploy 70,000 police for fresh weekend protests

France will deploy about 70,000 police nationwide as it braces for new protests on Saturday (October 24, 2026) after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago. Protests by high school students over learning conditions sparked a movement that has since spread nationwide, fuelled by broader anger over the rising cost of living.

Trump lifts some Canada tariffs ahead of midterms

U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration lifted some tariffs on Canadian imports on Friday (October 23, 2026), two weeks ahead of midterm elections, after a vulnerable Republican candidate said she’d lobbied for the change. The easing of tariffs will apply to products including “plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment,” the White House said in a statement.

England’s Bodhana Sivanandan becomes International Master at age of 11, breaks 38-year-old record

Indian-origin English chess player Bodhana Sivanandan has become the youngest female International Master (IM) at the age of 11, breaking a 38-year-old record set by Judit Polgar. Sivanandan, who hails from Harrow in north London, needed only a few rating points to qualify for the open IM title and break Polgar’s record, while also securing a place among the 10 youngest IMs of all time.

World.content:
A 60-year-old fisherman was found dead after murdering his wife and son following a domestic dispute at their residence near Sirkazhi in Mayiladuthurai district on Friday night.

According to police, K. Jalendran lived with his wife, Malarselvi, 55, and son, Athigugan, 23, at Thirumullaivasal. Following a domestic dispute on Friday night, Jalendran allegedly attacked his wife and son with an iron rod, killing them on the spot. He subsequently ended his life.

As the house remained locked for a prolonged period, neighbours grew suspicious and checked on the family, after which the incident came to light. They informed the Sirkazhi police, who recovered the bodies and sent them to the Sirkazhi Government Hospital for post-mortem examination.

Further investigation into the incident is under way.

World.title: INDIA bloc to hold rally in Tripura on Oct 30, seeks CEC's removal
World.content:
INDIA bloc's Tripura unit will organise a rally in Agartala on October 30, 2026, pressing for a five-point charter of demands, including the removal of CECGyanesh Kumar and the inclusion of voters excluded from electoral rolls through the SIR, two senior leaders said.

Also read | The need to preserve the shine of Indian elections

Addressing a press conference, Leader of the Opposition in the Tripura Assembly Jitendra Chaudhury said the country was heading towards a national crisis as citizens' voting rights were allegedly being curtailed in the name of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.

"Over 13 crore electors have so far been disenfranchised through SIR across the country. The CEC has been acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah to ensure BJP victories in electoral battles," Mr. Chaudhury claimed.

The CPI(M) state secretary alleged that the SIR exercise in West Bengal and Bihar was aimed at ensuring the BJP's victory in the two states' Assembly elections.

"We have learnt that around 2.50 lakh voters may be deleted from the electoral rolls through SIR in our state. The move to disenfranchise valid voters is aimed at giving political mileage to the BJP in electoral battles. If this happens, we will strongly raise our voice," he said.

Mr. Chaudhury also criticised the Modi government over a law passed in the Lok Sabha that, he alleged, granted the CEC immunity from legal action for acts performed in office.

"Lifetime immunity has been given to the CEC to protect him from facing any legal action for his wrongdoings in the future. Even the President of India, the Prime Minister and chief ministers do not enjoy such immunity," he said.

Tripura Pradesh Congress Committee (TPCC) president Asish Kumar Saha said the INDIA bloc has been fighting for people's voting rights nationwide.

"To intensify the movement in Tripura, we will organise a massive rally on October 30 with a five-point charter of demands, including the removal of Gyanesh Kumar and the inclusion of names deleted from electoral rolls through SIR," Saha said.

He added that if security forces attempted to stop the proposed rally, the INDIA bloc would stage a demonstration outside the office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO).

Mr. Saha also appealed to people to set aside their political beliefs and join the movement, saying the issue concerned the country's larger interests and the universal franchise guaranteed by the Constitution.
