World.title: Georgia opposition party ban case: Day two of court proceedings
World.content:
On 22 October, Georgia’s Constitutional Court continued hearing a lawsuit filed by the ruling Georgian Dream party in Batumi, seeking to ban (declare unconstitutional) five opposition parties: the United National Movement, Coalition for Change, Lelo – Strong Georgia, Gakharia for Georgia and the Federalists.

Below are the key developments from the second day of hearings. The proceedings remained at the preliminary motions stage, with none of the opposition’s motions granted.

The hearings continue today, 23 October, and are being broadcast live by the Georgian Public Broadcaster.

The court has until 24 June 2027 to issue its final ruling, meaning it still has plenty of time.

Unprecedented case

The main issue raised by the opposition on the second day of hearings was that the lawsuit sought to ban all five parties in one go.

Lelo leader Badri Japaridze told the court that the case was unprecedented, as the parties had no links to one another. He argued that this was particularly true of Lelo, which was founded in late 2019.

Badri Japaridze described a statement by a Georgian Dream leader that the parties would be dissolved within days as disrespectful to the court. He argued that this meant the “verdict had already been delivered”. Presiding judge Revaz Nadaraya responded that the court could not comment on statements made by politicians and that no-one would be able to exert any influence over it.

Georgian Dream MP Archil Gorduladze partially agreed with Japaridze’s argument. He acknowledged that there was indeed no precedent for dissolving five parties in a single proceeding, but argued that there was equally no precedent for five closely linked parties jointly violating Article 23 of the Constitution, which prohibits parties aiming to forcibly change the constitutional order.

Venice Commission

The Lelo party asked the court to invite three experts from the Venice Commission to the hearing to assess whether banning the parties would comply with European democratic standards. Other opposition parties supported the motion, while Georgian Dream opposed it.

However, Revaz Nadaraya dismissed the motion as unfounded, saying that the European legal experts could be heard elsewhere. Nika Gvaramia, co-chair of the Coalition for Change, argued that the Venice Commission was an association of European constitutional courts and that the right to consult it was enshrined in the Organic Law.

The court’s full bench then held consultations and rejected the motion.

The court also rejected another motion by Lelo, requesting that its lawsuit No. 1907, filed on 28 October 2025, be admitted for consideration on its merits. The lawsuit challenges provisions of the Organic Law on Political Associations of Citizens which, according to the party, restrict freedom of association, freedom of expression and political pluralism.

“Lack of trust is not enough reasoning”

Another Lelo representative, Giorgi Sioridze, requested that the Constitutional Court seek an advisory opinion from the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) on five questions: the criteria under which a political party may be banned, the evidence required, whether a party’s stated objectives or its actual actions should carry greater weight, whether less restrictive measures are available, and what standards should apply when examining a case involving several parties simultaneously.

One of the arguments put forward in support of the motion was a lack of trust in the Constitutional Court. Revaz Nadaraya dismissed this argument as unfounded. He said that although the case was important and unprecedented, this was not sufficient grounds for seeking an advisory opinion from the ECtHR. Nadaraya also added that a national court should not have to ask the European Court whether five parties could be named as co-defendants in the same proceedings.

Evidence and one month to review case materials

The Coalition for Change, meanwhile, requested that evidence be obtained from the Ministry of Justice, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Government Administration, that witnesses be identified and that consideration of the case on its merits be postponed.

The coalition also requested that the defendants be given one month to review the case materials. The court’s full bench unanimously rejected the motion. Nadaraya explained that, at this stage, the court was not convinced of the need to obtain additional evidence, as the requested materials relied on the same opinion already included in the case file.

Georgian Dream representatives accused the opposition of attempting to delay the proceedings. According to Archil Gorduladze, the defendants were filing motions that had no legal basis or relevance to the case. Tornike Cheishvili argued that the parties were expressing the same arguments using different terminology and that their motions were virtually identical.

Meanwhile, outside the courtroom…

– Georgia’s Public Defender (ombudsman) has yet to submit a legal opinion (amicus curiae) to the Constitutional Court, despite Lelo calling on him to do so on 19 October. According to First Deputy Public Defender Tamar Gvaramadze, the ombudsman’s office is holding internal discussions and no decision has yet been made.

– Georgian Dream MP Irakli Kadagishvili said it was unacceptable for international actors to make statements intended to put pressure on the court. He argued that such statements served harmful political purposes.

Reactions after the hearing

Berdia Sichinava, a representative of the Gakharia for Georgia party, compared the proceedings to Franz Kafka’s novel The Trial, saying that no-one really knew who was being accused of what. Badri Japaridze also said that, by the end of the second day of hearings, none of the parties understood exactly what Georgian Dream was accusing them of.

Ana Tsitlidze, a representative of the United National Movement, accused the judges of behaving like Georgian Dream activists. According to Lelo representative Irakli Kupradze, the proposed ban would affect not only the parties but also nearly a million Georgian voters.

Ana Buchukuri, a representative of Gakharia for Georgia, suggested that the third day of hearings would also begin with procedural motions. She argued that the court’s refusal to grant any of the motions indicated that a decision had already been made.

World.title: Should state have right to ban political parties? Tbilisi street poll – Video
World.content:
Ban on Georgian opposition

Should the state have the right to ban political parties? Tbilisi residents answered reporters’ questions.

Context

The Constitutional Court of Georgia began examining a lawsuit filed by the ruling Georgian Dream party on 21 October, seeking to ban five opposition parties.

The lawsuit was signed by 88 Georgian Dream MPs, who claim that the parties violated Article 23 of the Constitution, which prohibits the establishment and activities of political parties aiming to overthrow or forcibly change the country’s constitutional order.

The proposed ban on opposition parties is no ordinary constitutional case. The court’s ruling could determine what kind of country Georgia ultimately becomes. The case has therefore attracted widespread attention.

How respondents reacted to the question

Most Tbilisi residents interviewed by reporters said that banning political parties was unacceptable in a country that claims to be a democracy. They stressed the importance of a multiparty system and people’s right to choose.

Many said the current developments reminded them of a slide towards dictatorship, drawing comparisons with Russia, North Korea and even the Soviet Union.

One respondent echoed claims made on Georgian pro-government propaganda channels that the opposition had attempted to set fire to parliament and stage a coup, and should therefore be banned.

Another respondent said that banning political parties could be open to discussion, but only if the process was fair and transparent.

Many passers-by declined to comment and tried to avoid appearing on camera. This was hardly surprising, given that people approached on the street generally tend to avoid politically sensitive questions.

World.title: Vanity Fair: Trump son-in-law received $750m from Azerbaijani bank
World.content:
Kushner’s links to Azerbaijani bank

Reports have emerged of hundreds of millions of dollars being transferred through Azerbaijan to a secret bank account that Jared Kushner, the son-in-law and former senior adviser to US President Donald Trump, allegedly had access to.

However, no evidence has been presented that the money belonged to the Azerbaijani state or that Azerbaijani authorities were involved in arranging these transactions.

The name of the Azerbaijani bank through which the transfers were allegedly made has also not been disclosed.

According to an investigation published in Vanity Fair, Dutch intelligence, while monitoring Kushner’s phone, discovered that a large sum of money had been transferred from an Azerbaijani bank to an account in the United Arab Emirates.

The claims were detailed in an article by American investigative journalist Matthew Cole, published on 22 October. The article is an excerpt from his new book, Princes and Thieves.

The investigation refers to a bank account holding approximately $750m, as well as an additional $1bn allegedly transferred to Israel through Azerbaijan. The author links these financial transactions to unofficial diplomatic negotiations involving the United States, Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Israel.

How did Dutch intelligence gain access to Kushner’s phone?

According to Matthew Cole’s investigation, the Netherlands’ Military Intelligence and Security Service (MIVD) gained access to data from Kushner’s phone in late 2017 through a hacker linked to Russian military intelligence.

Dutch intelligence officers initially discovered screenshots from Kushner’s iPhone on Russian military intelligence servers. Then, exploiting the same technical vulnerability, they were able to monitor activity on his phone screen in early 2018.

The intelligence officers’ attention was drawn to Kushner’s use of a bank account in the UAE. According to the investigation, hundreds of millions of dollars had previously been transferred to this account from an Azerbaijani bank.

Dutch intelligence initially suspected that the bank account from which the funds originated might have been linked to the Azerbaijani government. However, the article does not provide any banking documents confirming this connection.

$750m and possible intermediary role of Azerbaijani bank

The account, referred to in the investigation as Alpha, was held at First Abu Dhabi Bank, one of the UAE’s largest banks.

According to the author, the Saudi and UAE leadership transferred around $750m into the account from 2017 onwards. The funds were allegedly intended to finance unofficial foreign policy initiatives.

The account did not legally belong to Kushner. It was held by Watani Al Emarat, a charitable organisation funded by the UAE government. However, according to the investigation, Kushner had signing authority over the account, allowing him to carry out certain banking transactions.

The section of the investigation concerning Azerbaijan focuses particularly on the mechanism used to transfer the funds.

According to Cole, all the funds deposited into the account monitored by Dutch intelligence arrived in US dollars from an Azerbaijani bank.

The author claims that some Azerbaijani banks acted as intermediaries in transferring large sums of money abroad. They accepted funds in Saudi riyals and UAE dirhams before transferring the equivalent amounts overseas in US dollars, charging a commission of 6–7%.

Under the arrangement described, a client would transfer funds in local currency to an Azerbaijani bank, which would then send the equivalent amount in US dollars to a recipient abroad from a separate internal account. The author notes that such transactions could make it more difficult to trace the original source of the funds.

Additional $1bn allegedly transferred to Israel

The investigation also describes a second major financial transaction allegedly carried out through Azerbaijan.

According to the author’s sources, by spring 2018, UAE leader Mohammed bin Zayed had transferred around $1bn to Israel through Azerbaijan, allegedly intended for Kushner.

The second account, referred to by Cole as Beta, was reportedly held at the Bank of Israel.

The article claims that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was to be informed of any potential transfers from this account. According to the author, former US ambassador to Israel David Friedman acted as an intermediary between Kushner and Netanyahu.

Friedman categorically denied these allegations. Kushner’s lawyer also stated that his client was unaware of the accounts in question, had no involvement with them and had not broken any laws.

Kushner’s financial ties have previously come under scrutiny

The new allegations come amid ongoing debate in the US over Kushner’s business ties with Gulf states.

In March 2026, US Senator Ron Wyden and House Representative Robert Garcia launched an investigation into Kushner’s continued efforts to raise funds from foreign governments for his investment firm while simultaneously engaging in diplomatic activities.

The members of Congress sought to establish whether investments received by Kushner’s firm, Affinity Partners, from Middle Eastern governments could have influenced his involvement in US foreign policy.

An investigation published by The New Yorker in September reported that Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund had invested $2bn in Kushner’s firm in 2021. The UAE and Qatar also invested in Affinity Partners.

These were separate financial arrangements, not directly linked to the alleged secret banking transactions of 2017–2018 described in the Vanity Fair article.

In addition, on 1 October, CNN published an investigation into investments made by Kushner’s firm in Israeli financial group Phoenix Financial. According to CNN’s analysis, Phoenix Financial had invested in at least nine companies supplying equipment to the Israeli military.

However, CNN said it had found no evidence that Kushner’s diplomatic decisions had directly influenced these investments. Kushner’s lawyer also stated that his client had not been involved in the companies’ investment decisions.

On 8 October, Kushner published a detailed response on his website to the earlier New Yorker article, rejecting allegations that he had used his diplomatic activities for personal financial gain.

Which previous investigations have implicated Azerbaijani banks?

Azerbaijan’s role in international financial transactions has previously been the subject of journalistic investigations.

In 2017, the Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (OCCRP), together with its partners, published a major investigation titled The Azerbaijani Laundromat.

The investigation documented financial transactions totalling around $2.9bn, carried out between 2012 and 2014 through various companies and bank accounts.

According to OCCRP, around $1.4bn of this amount was transferred through Baktelekom LLC, a company that held an account at the International Bank of Azerbaijan.

The investigation highlighted the role of Azerbaijan-linked financial entities in international money transfers. However, there is no confirmed link between this scheme and the recently reported accounts allegedly connected to Kushner.

Meanwhile, in January 2026, the Council of Europe’s Committee of Experts on the Evaluation of Anti-Money Laundering Measures and the Financing of Terrorism (MONEYVAL) reported progress by Azerbaijan in this area.

The committee upgraded Azerbaijan’s compliance ratings against international standards in seven areas, including money transfer controls, identification of the ultimate beneficial owners of legal entities and banking supervision.

However, the country remained subject to enhanced monitoring.

World.title: Deer born at Tbilisi Zoo continue to return to wild – video
World.content:
Nine red deer born at Tbilisi Zoo have returned to the wild — or, more precisely, to a semi-wild environment. They have moved to Algeti National Park, near Tbilisi.

Life at the Tbilisi Zoo: video

Deer born at Tbilisi Zoo were first moved to Algeti National Park in the summer of 2025. It was the first attempt to reintroduce the species into the wild in Georgia.

The process will continue in the coming years until the park has enough deer to restore the population.

The idea of restoring Georgia’s deer population emerged in the 1990s, when their numbers in the country fell sharply. Poaching and uncontrolled hunting contributed to the decline. Today, the red deer features on Georgia’s Red List of threatened species. In 2023, at the initiative of the Ministry of Environmental Protection and with funding from the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency, authorities drew up a national plan to restore endangered species.

Zurab Gurielidze, a professor at Ilia State University and director of Tbilisi Zoo, led the development of the plan. As part of the project, authorities established an enclosed area of around 60 hectares in Algeti National Park, providing the deer with a suitable habitat and the conditions they need.

The process will take time and require continuous monitoring, adequate protection and cooperation between various agencies. Once the deer population in the park reaches a sufficient level, authorities will release the animals fully into the wild, where they will be able to live independently.

World.title: Turkmenistan, Austria explore expanded agricultural commodity trading
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 24. Turkmenistan’s State Commodity and Raw Materials Exchange and the Vienna Agricultural Exchange have explored opportunities to expand commodity trading, strengthen agricultural trade and develop new business ties during meetings in Vienna on October 22–23, the Embassy of Turkmenistan in Austria said.

The Turkmen delegation was led by Batyr Volsahatov, chairman of the State Commodity and Raw Materials Exchange of Turkmenistan (SCRMET).

During the visit, the delegation met with Ernst Haas, president of the Vienna Agricultural Exchange, and Karl Schneider, the exchange’s secretary. The Turkmen officials also held talks with Dražen Maloča, head of regional management and regional director for Southeast Europe and Eastern Europe/Central Asia at the Austrian Federal Economic Chamber (WKÖ).

The discussions focused on strengthening institutional and commercial cooperation between the two countries, promoting exchange-based commodity trading and expanding trade in agricultural products.

The parties also explored opportunities to establish new channels for mutually beneficial economic cooperation between Turkmenistan and Austria.

According to the Turkmen embassy, the meetings provided a platform for exchanging views on potential areas of cooperation and identifying ways to deepen business ties between the two countries.

Turkmenistan operates a state commodity exchange that facilitates domestic and international trade in a range of goods, including petroleum products, chemicals, textiles and agricultural commodities. The exchange plays a role in connecting Turkmen producers with foreign buyers and supporting the country’s export activities.

Austria, meanwhile, provides access to European commercial networks and agricultural trading expertise. Closer engagement between the exchanges could create opportunities to strengthen commercial contacts, improve market access for agricultural products and broaden cooperation in commodity trading.

World.title: Uzbekistan, Germany discuss plans to deepen ties in 2027
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 24. Uzbekistan and Germany have discussed expanding political, trade, economic and investment cooperation, as well as preparations for joint events in 2027, during a meeting between Uzbekistan’s Deputy Foreign Minister Muzaffar Madrakhimov and German Ambassador Matthias Follert in Tashkent on October 23.

According to Uzbekistan’s Foreign Ministry, the sides reviewed current issues on the bilateral agenda and emphasized the importance of further strengthening cooperation across multiple areas.

The officials also discussed plans for joint events in 2027 and agreed to maintain active engagement across all areas of bilateral cooperation.

Uzbekistan and Germany have maintained diplomatic relations since 1992. Germany is Uzbekistan’s largest trading partner within the European Union, with bilateral trade reaching approximately $1.43 billion in 2025, a 13.2% increase from the previous year.

Economic cooperation spans industry, energy, agriculture, transport, vocational education and sustainable development. German companies also contribute to Uzbekistan’s industrial modernization and infrastructure development, while German development institutions support projects in areas including energy efficiency, public administration and climate resilience.

The two countries have also expanded political dialogue through bilateral consultations and the Central Asia–Germany cooperation framework. In June 2026, Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening political ties, expanding trade and investment, and advancing cooperation in energy, transport, mining, education and healthcare. The meeting also highlighted new trade and investment agreements worth more than $1 billion signed following business events in Tashkent in May.

World.title: Uzbekistan, EU seek to advance ties through upcoming high-level talks
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 24. Uzbekistan and the European Union have discussed preparations for upcoming high-level meetings and joint events, with a focus on translating diplomatic engagement into practical results, at a meeting on October 23 in Tashkent.

This was reflected in the statement by Uzbekistan’s Foreign Ministry, following a meeting between Uzbekistan’s Deputy Foreign Minister Muzaffar Madrakhimov and EU Ambassador to Uzbekistan Toivo Klaar.

The sides emphasized the importance of making effective use of existing cooperation mechanisms, maintaining consistent political dialogue and strengthening ties in trade, the economy and other priority areas.

Following the meeting, the parties agreed to continue efforts to expand mutually beneficial cooperation.

The meeting comes as Uzbekistan and the EU work to deepen their partnership under the Enhanced Partnership and Cooperation Agreement (EPCA), signed on October 24, 2025, and provisionally applied since March 1, 2026. The agreement expands the framework for cooperation in trade, investment and other areas of mutual interest.

The EU and Uzbekistan have maintained formal bilateral relations since Uzbekistan gained independence in 1991, with their cooperation initially governed by a Partnership and Cooperation Agreement that took effect in 1999. The EU is one of Uzbekistan’s key trading partners, accounting for 10.4% of the country’s total foreign trade in 2024.

World.title: Siemens Energy explores tech support for Green Energy Corridor project
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 24. Siemens Energy is exploring opportunities to provide solutions for converter substations based on high-voltage direct current (HVDC) technology within the framework of the Caspian–Black Sea–Europe Green Energy Corridor project.

This was announced by the company’s Vice President for Türkiye, Central Asia, and Western Europe, Maxim Zubov, in a video posted on the Azerbaijani Ministry of Energy’s social media accounts, in which he shared his views on the forum “Green Energy Corridor: From Feasibility Study to Implementation.”

He noted that the company is also prepared to assist in establishing connections with potential electricity buyers in Europe. According to Zubov, the company views the project as a significant international initiative that supports the development of renewable energy sources, contributes to the diversification of Europe's energy supply, and strengthens ties among the participating countries. He noted that the project could also contribute to strengthening Azerbaijan's electricity grid.

"As one of Europe's leading suppliers of high-voltage direct current (HVDC) technologies, we are exploring opportunities to provide technological solutions for the project's HVDC converter substations," Zubov said.

According to him, the company's technical team is holding discussions with the client, representatives of the Green Energy Corridor project, and the design institute to identify optimal solutions for the project.

Zubov added that the company could support the implementation of the project by leveraging its network of clients and partners in Europe.

"We have an extensive network of clients and partners in Europe. In this regard, we are prepared to assist in organizing discussions and establishing connections with potential electricity buyers. We believe that, by doing so, we can make an additional contribution to the successful implementation of the project," the company executive emphasized.

Siemens Energy is an international company operating in the fields of power generation, electrical grids, energy storage systems, and the electrification of industrial processes. According to the company, it possesses over 150 years of experience in energy technologies. Siemens Energy operates in 90 countries and has approximately 100,000 employees.

Investment prospects for project

At a forum held in Baku, the results of the feasibility study for the Caspian–Black Sea–Europe Green Energy Corridor project were presented for the first time to international investors, financial institutions, and business partners. The event covered the project's investment attractiveness, business model, financing opportunities, and the establishment of new partnerships, as well as preparations for reaching the Final Investment Decision (FID).

According to the project's feasibility study, investments in electricity transmission infrastructure are projected to amount to 14.3 billion euro. The document was finalized in July 2026 and approved by the governments of Azerbaijan, Georgia, Romania, and Hungary. The project is currently in the development phase.

The study indicates that the project will have a total transmission capacity of 3.9 gigawatts (GW), involving the construction of three power lines, each with a capacity of 1.3 GW. The project's internal rate of return (IRR) is estimated at 11.7%.

Projections suggest that, starting in 2032, the corridor will be capable of transmitting 8 terawatt-hours (TWh) of renewable electricity annually to the European Union. By 2040, the annual transmission volume is expected to reach 20 TWh.

The feasibility study forecasts that revenues generated from managing transmission constraints within the energy system will exceed 315 million euro per year, starting from 2032. It is also noted that the project will enable a reduction in carbon dioxide emissions by 3.6 million tons per year by 2040.

The annual economic benefit of the project is expected to increase as the power lines are commissioned in stages. It is projected that this figure will reach 860 million euro following the commissioning of the first line in 2032, and 1.8 billion euro after the second line becomes operational in 2036. With the commissioning of the third line in 2040, the annual economic benefit is expected to exceed 3 billion euro.

Speaking at the forum, Azerbaijan’s Minister of Energy, Parviz Shahbazov, stressed the strategic importance of the project in terms of strengthening regional energy security, diversifying energy supplies, and facilitating the green transition.

The minister noted that the project holds a special place in Azerbaijan’s strategy to become a regional hub for the production, transmission, and export of green energy. The reaffirmed political support for the project during the recent visit of European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen to Baku was also highlighted. Strengthening the project’s investment prospects through efforts to include the project in the draft TYNDP 2026 (Ten-Year Network Development Plan) for the European electricity grid, as well as the attainment of "Project of Mutual Interest" (PMI) status, was noted.

The Green Energy Corridor, envisioned to span approximately 3,000 kilometers, is planned to be commissioned in phases starting from 2032, with a target transmission capacity of 4 GW. According to the feasibility study, the project could facilitate the development of at least 8 GW of renewable energy generation capacity in the region, enable the transmission of approximately 20 billion kilowatt-hours of electricity to Europe annually from 2040 onwards, and contribute to a reduction in carbon emissions by up to 3.6 million tons.

One of the primary technical challenges of the project involves the planned installation of subsea power cables at depths of up to 2,200 meters in the Black Sea. Consequently, the necessity of employing advanced technological solutions to carry out operations at such depths has been emphasized.

The consideration of a hybrid business model combining regulated and commercial components to ensure the project’s commercial sustainability was pointed out. This model is intended to be based on long-term power purchase agreements, the participation of private capital, and the development of cross-border electricity trade.

Shahbazov said that the involvement of international financial institutions and private investors, a robust business model, and long-term commercial agreements are essential prerequisites for reaching a final investment decision.

"Our goal is to transform the Green Energy Corridor into a regional infrastructure project characterized by a clear business model, a sustainable financial structure, and attractive terms for investors. Azerbaijan’s strategic location, extensive experience in international energy projects, and reliable relationships with partner countries provide a solid foundation for achieving this objective," noted Shahbazov.

At the conclusion of the forum, the development of a partnership roadmap and the next steps toward reaching a Final Investment Decision (FID) for the Green Energy Corridor project were agreed upon.

Project participants

The Caspian–Black Sea–Europe Green Energy Corridor is a cross-border electricity transmission project involving Azerbaijan, Georgia, Romania, and Hungary. The initiative was established under a strategic partnership agreement signed in Bucharest on December 17, 2022, with the participation of the European Commission.

The development of the project is being handled by Green Energy Corridor Power Company (GECO), a joint venture registered in Bucharest. The company is owned by the national electricity grid operators of the four participating countries: AzerEnerji (Azerbaijan), Georgian State Electrosystem (Georgia), Transelectrica (Romania), and MVM (Hungary). Each participant holds a 25% stake in the company.

The project has been included in the Ten-Year Network Development Plan (TYNDP) 2026 of the European Network of Transmission System Operators for Electricity (ENTSO-E), under project numbers 1248 and 1244.

The next phase of the project involves the preparation of an implementation plan, the clarification of financing options, and the continuation of preparatory work for the final investment decision in 2029.

World.title: Turkmenistan approves participation in Poland’s Fast Textile 2026
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 24. Turkmenistan has approved a proposal for domestic textile companies to participate in the Fast Textile 2026 international exhibition in Zgierz, Poland, in November to expand the industry’s export potential.

According to the press service of the Turkmen government, the proposal was presented by Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers Nokerguly Ataguliyev at an online government meeting chaired by President Serdar Berdimuhamedov.

Turkmenistan plans to showcase export-oriented products manufactured by enterprises under the Ministry of Textile Industry and companies affiliated with the Union of Industrialists and Entrepreneurs.

The exhibition will also provide an opportunity for bilateral talks aimed at establishing business partnerships and expanding cooperation with international counterparts.

President Berdimuhamedov noted that Turkmenistan’s textile industry produces high-quality goods that are widely exported to foreign markets. He approved the proposal and instructed the deputy prime minister to take the necessary steps to organize the companies’ participation.

Fast Textile 2026 is an international B2B textile trade fair scheduled for 17–19 November 2026 at Ptak Expo (Ptak Wholesale Center) in Rzgów, near Łódź, Poland. Organized by Ptak S.A., the 12th autumn edition focuses on fabrics, knitwear, yarns, machinery, accessories, printing, embroidery and related technologies. It is expected to feature more than 600 exhibitors, over 14,500 trade visitors and approximately 20,000 m² of exhibition space, making it one of the largest textile sourcing events in Central and Eastern Europe.

Turkmenistan’s textile sector, managed by the Ministry of Textile Industry and private enterprises under the Union of Industrialists and Entrepreneurs, operates modern facilities that process domestic cotton into yarn, fabrics and finished goods. Up to 70% of production is exported, primarily cotton yarn (key counts such as Nm 27/1 and 34/1) to markets including Türkiye, the UAE, Kyrgyzstan, Azerbaijan and others in Europe and Asia. Participation in Fast Textile supports efforts to expand these export channels and form new partnerships.

World.title: Uzbekistan, Iran seek to expand trade and investment cooperation
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 24. Uzbekistan and Iran have discussed bilateral cooperation, upcoming diplomatic engagements and regional developments during a meeting between Uzbekistan’s First Deputy Foreign Minister Bakhromjon Aloyev and Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Islamic Republic of Iran to Uzbekistan Mohammad Ali Eskandari in Tashkent on October 23.

According to Uzbekistan’s Foreign Ministry, the officials reviewed the bilateral agenda, exchanged views on events planned for the near future and discussed current regional issues.

The meeting comes as the two countries seek to expand economic ties alongside regular political dialogue. In January–June 2026, bilateral trade increased by 37.5% year over year to $305 million, according to Uzbekistan’s Ministry of Investment, Industry and Trade. The two sides are also advancing 29 joint projects aimed at expanding investment and commercial cooperation.

Trade, investment and transport connectivity have emerged as key areas of cooperation. Uzbekistan and Iran have explored ways to improve transit links, strengthen logistics routes and expand business ties, while also developing cooperation in cultural and humanitarian affairs. Iran’s geographic position provides Uzbekistan with an additional route to regional and international markets.

The countries are preparing to hold the 17th meeting of their Joint Intergovernmental Commission and an Uzbekistan–Iran Business Forum in Tashkent on November 26–27. The events are expected to provide a platform for advancing joint projects and identifying further opportunities for trade and investment.

The latest meeting follows political consultations held in Tehran in August, when the two countries’ foreign ministries discussed strengthening political dialogue, expanding economic cooperation and addressing regional and international issues of mutual interest.

World.title: Turkmenistan prepares International Conference on Construction and Industry
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 24. Turkmenistan is preparing to hold an international exhibition and conference focused on the development of its construction, industrial, chemical and energy sectors.

According to the press service of the Turkmen government, the preparations were discussed at an online meeting of the Cabinet of Ministers chaired by President Serdar Berdimuhamedov.

Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers Baimyrat Annamammedov briefed the meeting on the events planned to mark Turkmenistan’s Day of Workers of the Construction and Industrial Sector.

The upcoming forum will bring together foreign companies, domestic private businesses, and representatives of Turkmenistan’s ministries and government agencies. Bilateral meetings between relevant government officials and representatives of foreign companies are also planned.

The exhibition and conference will provide a platform to explore modern international equipment and technologies for the construction, industrial, energy and chemical sectors, as well as road construction. Participants will also have an opportunity to exchange experience with international partners, strengthen existing business ties and establish new partnerships.

Annamammedov submitted a proposal on the preparations for the event for the president’s consideration.

President Berdimuhamedov stressed the importance of thorough preparations and ensuring that the international exhibition and conference are held to a high standard. He issued relevant instructions to the deputy prime minister.

CIET 2026 (International Conference & Exhibition “Development of the Construction, Industrial, Chemical and Energy Sectors of Turkmenistan”) is scheduled for 3–5 November 2026 at the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Turkmenistan in Ashgabat. Held under the theme “Innovation • Investment • Growth,” it coincides with the Day of Workers of the Construction and Industrial Complex (observed annually on 3 November). The event serves as a key platform linking government institutions, state enterprises, domestic private businesses and international participants to discuss investment opportunities, advanced technologies, public-private partnerships, digital solutions and project financing across construction, industry, chemicals, energy, infrastructure and related fields. Previous editions attracted more than 500 delegates from over 50 countries; the accompanying exhibition showcases equipment, materials and technologies, with pre-arranged B2G and B2B meetings. Sponsors and partners include companies such as Japan’s TOYO Engineering.

World.title: WA premier confronted by South Hedland community members
World.content:
South Hedland residents have confronted the West Australian Premier during a five-hour visit to the northern town — his first since the state government announced a coronial inquest into the deaths of three local children.

The renewed investigation into Margaret Hawke's 2022 killing of her 10-year-old daughter, seven-year-old son and four-month-old baby came after sustained political and media pressure over failures by WA's Department of Child Protection.

Child protection authorities are under fire after it was reported more than a dozen children were living alone in a house in South Hedland (ABC News: Alistair Bates)

Recent weeks have seen a steady stream of political drop-ins to South Hedland, more than 1,600 kilometres north of Perth, with the premier arriving on Saturday to declare a contractor had been selected to construct a long-promised $22 million MRI facility.

However, the spotlight remained on reports first appearing in The Australian newspaper that up to 15 children had been living unsupervised in a state-owned home until September.

The Premier was accompanied by Child Protection Minister Jessica Stojkovski — her fourth trip to South Hedland in nine weeks — for an agenda dominated by closed-door discussions with government agencies and their partners.

"You've gotta come back sit with us here, camp with us and roam the streets with us, so they can see for themselves what's actually happening," said Nyamal-Pitjikarli elder Doris Eaton, who spoke with the pair at a snap meeting during their visit.

" You can't see it from Perth, you can't do fly in and fly out. "

Doris Eaton (far left) met with the premier, alongside fellow elders Linda Doogiebee and Pat Mason. (ABC Pilbara: Kimberley Putland)

Departing talks with community organisation Hedland Aboriginal Strong Leaders, Mr Cook and Ms Stojkovski came under fire from a community member who identified herself as a former foster carer.

"When is the department going to be accountable and when are you going to speak to the community?" she said.

The ABC spoke with multiple other residents who expressed their frustration with the government response.

"I get confronted by people all the time. That's part of the job," Mr Cook said.

"But I fully appreciate that everyone wants to see things improve."

Progress being made, government says

There were no policy announcements about child protection during the premier's visit, nor did he meet with families impacted by the crisis.

Mr Cook said the emphasis was on consulting with the people "who are delivering the services in the community".

Dorothy Papertalk believes a coronial inquest would provide answers about what happened to her grandchildren. (ABC Pilbara: Alistair Bates)

The ABC understands Dorothy Papertalk, mother of Margaret Hawke and the children's grandmother, declined an invitation to meet with the premier.

Ms Papertalk led the campaign for an inquest, which was denied by the coroner in 2025. Ms Papertalk has requested privacy at this time.

"There are a range of families that are receiving good services, there's others that we can improve," Mr Cook said.

"The department's in a process of continuous improvement all the time."

Ms Stojkovski has ordered an assurance review of the department's handling of the Hawke murders. (ABC Pilbara: Kimberley Putland)

When questioned, Ms Stojkovski could not point to how many full-time equivalent staff positions had been filled since it was revealed in WA Parliament the Pilbara region had 11 child protection caseworker vacancies.

A relief team has been sent to South Hedland in response.

"Having those senior staff from the group, the relieving team, is really important and it's been very helpful for our staff here on the ground," Ms Stojkovski said.

The minister expects to be handed an assurance review of recommendations made in the wake of the Hawke murders by the end of the month.

'National shame': WA opposition

On Thursday, WA Commissioner for Children and Young People Jacqueline McGowan-Jones tabled a scathing assessment of the state's child protection system in parliament.

The report considered the experiences of 19 children who were placed into a secure care centre multiple times and made 56 recommendations.

"If children are brought into out-of-home care, it is because they are apparently at risk at home," Ms McGowan-Jones told the ABC.

" They were equally, if not more so, at risk, being brought into the state system. "

Jacqueline McGowan-Jones handed down her review on Thursday. (ABC News: Jasmine Hughes)

WA opposition leader Basil Zempilas said it was "insulting" that the premier was not visiting affected families.

"I am absolutely astounded after nine weeks of this being in the national spotlight, the premier has finally gone up — finally — but is not meeting with any families," he said.

"This is a shocking and ignorant lack of leadership."

World.title: Fire breaks out at Hitler's mountain retreat, suspect arrested
World.content:
German police say they have detained a suspect following a fire at Adolf Hitler's mountain retreat, known as the Eagle's Nest, in the state of Bavaria.

Around 200 firefighters were deployed to tackle the blaze at the Nazi dictator's remote and difficult-to-access Kehlsteinhaus residence, on the peak above Obersalzberg in southern Germany.

Firefighters saw flames rising high into the air as they approached the scene, only to find the building "completely ablaze", police said.

"A suspicious person was taken into temporary custody," they said in a later statement, adding that nobody was injured in the blaze.

Police spokeswoman Lisa Maier said firefighters struggled to tackle the fire due to its location at an altitude of 1,834 metres.

The building was only accessible with "heavy breathing apparatus", she said.

Emergency services were called to the fire on an icy cold night in Bavaria. (Reuters: Florian Scherer)

Authorities were alerted to the fire on Friday evening, when a smoke detector triggered a fire alarm at around 9:50pm local time, police said.

No reason for the fire was given, but German media reported that the investigators suspected it was the result of arson.

As snow fell on the Alpine peak, the Eagle's Nest was still engulfed in flames in the early hours of Saturday, a weather camera showed.

The fire appeared to have been doused by Saturday morning, although smoke continued to rise from the smouldering building.

Monument to Hitler

Officers blocked access to the road leading to the retreat.

The firefighters found no-one inside the building.

Adolf Hitler (right) used the resort 14 times during World War II. (Supplied)

Ms Maier said the investigation was still ongoing, with police planning a media conference later over the weekend.

German tabloid Bild reported that the authorities arrested a motorcyclist they came across on their way to the scene.

Built between 1937 and 1938, the Eagle's Nest forms part of the toxic legacy of Hitler's Third Reich, which was responsible for the deaths of millions of Jews along with Roma, LGBTQ people and communists in the Holocaust.

It was designed to serve as a monument to Hitler's rule, though the dictator himself only occasionally visited the complex, due to his fear of heights.

German police say a man is in custody with the fire thought to be deliberately lit. (Reuters: Markus Leitner)

Built of stone and granite, the residence offers an exceptional view of the picturesque Bavarian Alpine landscape.

It survived World War II undamaged and later gained notoriety through its use as a shooting location in many post-war Hollywood films.

Since 1952, it has hosted both an exhibition recounting the house's Nazi history and a restaurant.

The website says the Eagle's Nest "stands for the insanity of the regime and the world on the Obersalzberg, where plans for war and mass murder were formed".

Hitler visited the Eagle's Nest 14 times from 1938 until the end of World War II in1945.

He used the mountaintop teahouse strictly as a showpiece to welcome select foreign dignitaries, including French ambassador André François-Poncet, rather than host them at his official residences or at a military command centre.

Wires/ABC

World.title: Daughters joyful to 'breathe same air' as Donna Nelson returns to Perth
World.content:
Grandmother Donna Nelson was greeted with lots of hugs — and her favourite cappuccinos — on her return to Perth from Japan under an international prison transfer her daughters say has "lifted a weight" out of their lives.

The 60-year-old was arrested in January 2023 at Narita International Airport and charged with trying to import almost 2 kilograms of methamphetamine after she was tricked by a love scammer into carrying a bag filled with drugs.

Loading...

She was found guilty of drug smuggling and sentenced to six years in jail, three of which she has already served at a Japanese prison.

The former Greens candidate and Aboriginal health advocate is now being held at Bandyup Women's Prison in Perth, an outcome two of her five daughters say they and their mother could not be happier with.

Donna Nelson's daughters, Kristal Hilaire (left) and Ashlee Charles (right), are ecstatic that she is home. (ABC News)

"She's so happy, she's ecstatic. She's so happy to be able to have a cappuccino again," Ashlee Charles said of her mum.

"She's missed her cappuccinos. She was a regular cappuccino drinker… and she never had one all this time (in Japan)."

Ms Charles said in addition to indulging in her favourite coffee, her mother also enjoyed a lot of time with family and met her youngest grandchild for the first time.

"She hasn't had a hug this whole time," Ms Charles said.

"She got at least 10 hugs yesterday. She got so many hugs. We tried to make up as much as we could."

'Breathing the same air'

The prisoner transfer that brought Nelson home began last year after she abandoned her final avenue for appeal.

Nelson was duped by a love scammer into carrying drugs. (ABC News)

Daughter Kristal Hilaire, who had visited her mother in Japan, said the process of bringing her home had been stressful.

"It's been very secretive and we've had to put a lot of trust in our government and the Japanese government," she said. "That's been hard."

The love scammer who ruined Donna's life Grandmother Donna Nelson sits alone in a Japanese jail for 23 hours a day, far from the life she planned with her online boyfriend of two years. The court accepted the 59-year-old was love scammed, but sentenced her anyway.

The family said they only found out when their mother would return at the last minute, and could not stop crying with relief once she contacted them from Perth.

"It's like a weight was lifted that you'd forgotten was there, because it became normal to be wearing that weight and today you wake up and you're feeling renewed," Ms Hilaire said.

Nelson is now at Bandyup Women's Prison in Perth. (ABC News: Lauren Smith)

Ms Charles said she was looking forward to having her phone "blow up again" with calls from her mother, who used to call her daughters at least once a day but was unable to contact them on any regular basis from jail in Japan.

"It's weird to think that we are breathing the same air as her now and we literally can just drive past where she is," she said.

Nelson was unsuccessful in her appeal last year against drug trafficking charges, setting off the transfer deal. (ABC News: Yoshitaka Enomoto)

Nelson's family are uncertain about the future, but hopeful she could be up for parole in February.

For now, they are just grateful to the authorities for bringing her home.

World.title: Jillaroos hammer England 78-0 but superstar's World Cup ends in hospital
World.content:
The Jillaroos have continued a weekend of lopsided scores as they thumped England 78-0 at the Women's Rugby League World Cup, although the victory was soured by a tournament-ending broken wrist for gun centre Julia Robinson.

Eleven Australians crossed for tries in Perth, with Jaime Chapman, Jocelyn Kelleher, Isabelle Kelly and Abbi Church nabbing doubles in a 15-try rout.

Robinson also got on the board in the 16th minute, but her evening and tournament came to a painful end just a few minutes later when she got her arm trapped between teammate Shaylee Bent and England winger Amelia Brown in a tackle.

The Broncos superstar immediately came reeling out of the tackle holding her left wrist and was taken straight off the field before being taken to hospital.

Loading Instagram content

Despite missing their greatest try-scorer, the Jillaroos carried on unfazed to romp to an enormous victory that fell just short of the 90-4 win they enjoyed in their against England in Las Vegas in early 2025.

Australia entered the game second behind England in Pool A after both won their opening matches, but now tops the group as the only team with two wins and enjoying a massive 118-0 points differential.

The Australian women's win was the sixth straight drubbing in round two of the men's and women's tournaments, but fell short of being the biggest margin after the English men beat France 82-0 in the first game of the western double header.

Earlier on Saturday, Samoa thumped PNG 64-6 in the men's tournament, while Fiji's women rolled over the top of the Orchids 40-4 in Port Moresby.

Friday's games were no closer, with Fetu Samoa bagelling Wales 76-0, while the Tongan men beat Lebanon 36-0.

Looks back at all the action in our live blog below.

World.title: How a data centre united Australia's gaming community
World.content:
Before the Oceania data centre arrived, Australians sometimes found the online role-playing game Final Fantasy XIV a surprisingly lonely multiplayer experience.

On the Asia server, they'd struggle to find enough fellow English speakers to tackle the game's notorious super-bosses. Those visiting American servers would find the in-game Golden Saucer amusement park sparsely populated during another time zone's twilight hours.

And the few who chose the most distant Europe server struggled with "input lag" that perilously delayed gameplay actions, with the risk of failed quests and let-down teammates.

That changed in January 2022, 12 years after the game was released, when, encouraged by a pandemic boom in player numbers, developer Square Enix finally launched Oceania servers. It was a decision that united players in the region.

Lin, a Final Fantasy XIV community organiser from Melbourne, was shocked at the scale of the local player base.

"When they finally released a server where our ping [internet connection latency speed] was manageable, we were like, 'whoa, there's thousands of people here'," they tell ABC Arts.

"It took 30 minutes just to get into the queue. You no longer had to guess if we could speak the same language or understand the same lingo."

Final Fantasy's near-40-year legacy lured Pat, another community organiser from Melbourne, into online role-playing games.

"I love the Final Fantasy series. That's the one I grew up with," they say.

The Final Fantasy series has nabbed more than 212 million sales. (Supplied: Square Enix)

Massive offline multiplayer

By nature, Final Fantasy XIV's community primarily exists online. A community organisation called Limsa Extreme runs in-game award shows, theatre shows and musical productions throughout the year.

Local bar meet-ups are an infrequent occasion, but the annual Final Fantasy XIV community meet-up at PAX Australia, one of the country's biggest exhibitions of games and gaming culture, is the highlight on the calendar.

"The community is so tight-knit when they come together; but it's coming together, that's the hard part," Pat says.

This year's meet-up moved to a larger venue at the Melbourne Convention and Exhibition Centre. Even with the extra space it was standing room only.

Players attended from across Oceania, many cosplaying their game characters; one arrived in a costume of the series' cute cat-like Moogles, and several wore the green sprout headbands which indicate a new player.

The community has grown year on year, but 2026 had a special draw: the attendance of two popular Final Fantasy developers. Localiser Michael-Christopher Koji Fox and global community producer Toshio Murouchi, familiar faces to the global player base, dropped by the community event ahead of their panel.

Murouchi barely got to utter the single word "Hey" before being drowned out by enthusiastic cheers.

"I'm still a bit starstruck," says Mark Withers, a Newcastle-based streamer and event organiser.

"Many popular online games don't visit, or host dedicated servers, for Australian players.

"It's encouraging to be recognised and to be seen."

PAX Australia's Final Fantasy XIV community meet-up has grown since its inception in 2022. (Supplied: Limsa Extreme)

Australian impact on a global game

Koji Fox says a global team, including two longstanding Australian translators, is responsible for localising a game script that's now twice the length of the Bible.

But the Australian influence on the series goes even further back. Square Enix's localisation team, which produced English-language releases for landmark titles including Final Fantasy and Dragon Quest, was founded by Australian translator Richard Honeywood in the early 1990s.

Since then, Koji Fox, himself hired by Honeywood, says the medium's transition to spoken dialogue has reduced some overt Australian influences.

"The one thing that we don't let them do is do anything that requires rhyming, because Australian words don't rhyme [with the game's medieval style of British English]," Koji Fox says.

" One time they tried to rhyme 'hyper' and 'paper'; it was like 'hypa', 'paipa'. "

But Australia's presence has remained loud and clear at international Final Fantasy XIV fan festivals, which can attract 10,000 players at live events, even before they had their own servers.

"Since the beginning, we've had Australian fans spend the money, the time, the effort to get to these in America and Europe and even Japan," Koji Fox says.

"Now it's about giving back to this community by trying to increase the times we come to PAX Australia."

Koji Fox feels an Australian fan festival like the large-scale events held in Berlin and Tokyo is "not an if any more, I think it's just going to be a when".

"Everyone's just super-excited," he says, remembering the cheers that greeted Murouchi's speech.

"Imagine if [Final Fantasy XIV director] Yoshi-P was here; everyone would probably just drop dead!"

Geographic isolation as training weights

Perth's Ben Wu was one of many visitors to the Final Fantasy XIV Fan Festival in Berlin in July. As part of Team Fish, he took first place in a regional championship tournament, with a cash prize that was outmatched by the glee of meeting aforementioned director Yoshi-P.

Ben Wu (top row, second from right) from Australian Team Fish pictured along with Naoki Yoshida (top row, far right), known as Yoshi-P. (Supplied: Square Enix)

A retired competitive player in shooters like Counter-Strike, Valorant and Overwatch, Wu started playing Final Fantasy XIV during the pandemic, a period when the game's player count briefly overtook that of World of Warcraft.

Wu initially struggled to find other Australian players, participating in international tournaments with one local friend.

It wasn't until the Oceania server's arrival that he could marshal enough Australian players to field any team, let alone a winning one.

But its competitive scene still remains smaller than other regions.

Square Enix's unusual criteria means Oceania is grouped with Europe for fan festival tournaments. Wu found Australia's remoteness from other competitors, including the tightly interconnected network of European teams, gave Team Fish a surprising advantage against their rivals.

"We were able to hide our strategy from European teams by practising against North American and Japanese teams. We didn't only do that because we wanted to hide our strategy, it's almost impossible to practise with the Europeans," he says, explaining the high internet latency that makes executing rapid decisions impossible.

"We had to play on the North American and Japanese servers to get our practice.

" We weren't used to having low latency, so it felt like our training weights were removed when we played on stage. "

Final Fantasy XIV contains multitudes, accumulated over its 16-year existence. In-game there are the high-level competitions experienced by Wu, and the Limsa Extreme community's relaxed hangouts at the Aetheryte Plaza.

Outside it, there are real-life cosplay, sticker exchanges and entertaining spin-offs like the Taskmaster parody game show held at PAX Australia.

One player jokes it's not the gameplay that keeps them coming back; it's the community. Murouchi agrees Final Fantasy XIV's sense of player ownership is crucial.

"Players tend to feel Final Fantasy XIV as their own game. It's not an import from Japan: it's your game," Murouchi says.

"Because you don't need to visit Japanese servers or US servers, I believe people can feel Final Fantasy XIV is their home."

World.title: Two large earthquakes off coast of Vanuatu prompt tsunami warning
World.content:
A tsunami warning has been issued after two large earthquakes struck off the coast of Vanuatu.

A 6.9 magnitude earthquake struck first about 200 kilometres west of Sola at 12:31pm AEST on Saturday, according to the US Geological Survey (USGS).

It was followed shortly after by a 6.3 magnitude quake.

USGS recorded the quake at a depth of 10km.

The Pacific Tsunami Warning Centre said hazardous tsunami waves were possible for coastlines within 300km of the epicentre.

Its initial threat forecast identified Vanuatu as the area potentially affected.

"Persons located in threatened coastal areas should stay alert for information and follow instructions from national and local authorities," the warning centre said.

No threat is currently issued for Australia, according to the Bureau of Meteorology.

PTWC listed the initial magnitude of the larger quake as 7.2, but the USGS downgraded it to 6.9.

World.title: Years of conflict splits voters in former Netanyahu stronghold
World.content:
As lunchtime trade wanders through the door and with the smell of barbecued meat hanging in the air, kebab shop founder Amnon Oved smiles as he offers a rather blunt assessment of the state of Israel's leadership.

The popular businessman is a resident of Kiryat Shmona and, like many other Israelis, is preparing to vote in an election that will have a profound impact on the country after years of conflict and social upheaval.

In his mind, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, also known as Bibi, has reached his "best before" date.

"Bibi needs to go to America and sit there with [US President Donald] Trump, to smoke grass together and have a good life," he quips.

"Or he will sit here in prison, one of the two.

"Trump said to him, 'You're a liar.'

"That [was something] we knew before he said it!"

The October 27 election has essentially become a referendum on Mr Netanyahu's leadership and legacy.

An election poster for Benjamin Netanyahu that reads: "Never Surrender." (ABC News: Hamish Harty)

That includes his management of the multiple wars Israel is involved in, through to the personal corruption charges still hanging over him.

Current polling shows the longest-serving prime minister in Israel's history and his party, Likud, are facing a stiff challenge to hold on to power, with "change" candidates vying to topple him.

Israelis to vote in most seismic election in decades Here's a breakdown of Israel's upcoming general election and its complicated coalition structures.

Perhaps aware of the growing challenge against his ally, Mr Trump delivered a glowing endorsement of Mr Netanyahu as a "great warrior" ahead of the election.

Most data suggests Likud will be the second largest party in the next Knesset, behind one of Mr Netanyahu's main rivals, Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar.

But both men will still need to form coalitions post-election.

Israel heads to the polls after turmoil

Mr Oved's business is one of a handful that have consistently remained open in Kiryat Shmona, in far north Israel's Galilee region.

The view of Kiryat Shmona, with the Ramim Ridge in the background. (ABC News: Hamish Harty)

The city has been a Likud stronghold for decades and sits at the foot of the Ramim Ridge, where the border between Israel and Lebanon runs.

It was one of the Israeli cities targeted by Hezbollah's rocket and drone strikes after the Hamas-led October 7, 2023 attacks on Israel triggered the war in Gaza.

The 'straight' shooter looking to rule Israel Israel's upcoming election could be one of the most consequential in the country's history, with Benjamin Netanyahu's own former military chief firming as the favourite to oust the prime minister from office.

Israeli forces fired back over the border in response until an uneasy and, as some analysts described it, flawed ceasefire was struck in late 2024.

A fragile peace hung over the area until Hezbollah again opened fire earlier this year.

This time, the group acted in support of its backers in Tehran, days after the US and Israel launched a war on Iran.

The city came under attack once more, as Israeli forces pummelled Lebanese villages just a short distance away and launched a ground invasion.

"There have been wars since the world was created, and the wars will continue," Mr Oved said.

"It doesn't matter which leaders will be in power, good or bad. They are all crap in the end. They care about themselves."

At the November 2022 election, just over 49 per cent of the vote in Kiryat Shmona went to the Netanyahu-led party.

Trump endorses Netanyahu Donald Trump issues a glowing endorsement of Benjamin Netanyahu just months after an expletive-laden tirade against the Israeli prime minister.

The joint ticket led by far-right ultranationalist politicians Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich ranked second, with just under 14 per cent of the vote.

The two men would go on to become key members of the coalition government, which was later formed. They are running separately at this election.

Mr Ben-Gvir has been sanctioned by governments around the world, including Australia. But he and his Otzma Yehudit (Jewish Power) party is making the pitch that a strong Ben-Gvir means a strong Israel.

That message was on clear display at a public bomb shelter on the main road of Kiryat Shmona, which was covered in posters for his party.

Election posters for leader of the Otzma Yehudit (Jewish Power) party, Itamar Ben-Gvir, that read: "Ben-Gvir is strong, Israel is strong!" (ABC News: Hamish Harty)

In the background of the image are handcuffed Palestinian prisoners, highlighting his role as national security minister and his demands to become defence minister in a future government.

'People are hard to move'

Only about half of Kiryat Shmona's 25,000 residents have returned since fighting in southern Lebanon calmed.

The city's former deputy mayor Shimon Kamari believed many locals would still vote for Likud out of blind loyalty, even though he believed it had "abandoned" the city.

Shimon Kamari says his political views have changed over the years and he has become more right wing. (ABC News: Hamish Harty)

"Those who remained in the city are traditional people, religious people, people who the support for Likud flows in their blood, and it seems to me that it's very difficult to get it out of them," he said.

" It's very hard to get out of it because it comes from home, from the parents, it comes to them from grandparents, and these people are hard to move. "

Mr Kamari was born in the city to a family of Iranian Jews, and stayed in Kiryat Shmona during the war to continue running his food distribution business.

He said his political views had shifted over the years, and he had become more right wing in recent times.

For example, he was now of the view that things like a two-state solution could not and should not happen.

"If the government does not change … God forbid, it is a death sentence for Kiryat Shmona," he said.

Mr Kamari said he would be backing Gadi Eisenkot at the ballot box.

Israeli opposition leader and former military chief Gadi Eisenkot is campaigning ahead of Israel's upcoming general election. (Reuters: Amir Cohen)

"This culture that took root in the State of Israel, the culture of lies, we have to change it," he said.

"And I believe that the four parties of change, headed by Eisenkot, will be able to bring us back on track."

Some Israelis remain loyal to PM

Simmering anger against Mr Netanyahu in the city is countered by vocal support for the prime minister, who has argued he is the only person able to keep Israel and Israelis safe from the enemies who surround it.

Herzl Ben Asher, another former deputy mayor and current editor of the Galilee News, said some voters were misguided if they thought Mr Netanyahu's lengthy time in office was a reason to replace him.

Herzl Ben Asher says the time Benjamin Netanyanhu has been in power is not a reason to vote for someone else. (ABC News: Hamish Harty)

"Can you tell someone who has lived with his wife for 20 years, that 20 years is enough, and to replace her with someone else? No," he argued.

"He needs to maintain his achievements, and that's not easy.

"Getting to the summit is easier than staying at the summit — everyone knows that. He needs to complete his work."

Mr Ben Asher described Mr Netanyahu's achievements as "incomprehensible" in scale and significance, and pointed to the recent war with Iran, which is still not resolved, as evidence of how influential and powerful he can be.

Yoav Sabbag is preparing to vote in the Israeli election. (ABC News: Hamish Harty)

Another resident, Yoav Sabbag, lamented how empty Kiryat Shmona was but said Mr Netanyahu was the only person who could breathe life back into the city.

"We have to decide to take just Benjamin Netanyahu, because … maybe it is not [like he is] the 'Superman', but he [makes] me feel security in my country and in this area, five minutes from Lebanon."

World.title: Tasmanian football club coach charged with rape
World.content:
A former northern Tasmanian football coach has been charged with three counts of rape, leading to the resignation of the football club's president.

Police confirmed a 44-year-old man from northern Tasmania had been charged with the offences that were alleged to have occurred in April last year.

The man is believed to be former Bracknell football coach, Josh Adams.

He is scheduled to appear in the Launceston Magistrates Court early next year.

In a statement, Northern Tasmanian Football Association (NTFA) president Peter Gutwein said the association had recently been informed that a coach had been charged with "a serious criminal offence".

But he said the NTFA would not provide further comment as the matter was now before the courts.

News of charges being laid against Adams were first published by an independent media outlet.

Its reporting detailed private messages exchanged between Bracknell Football Club president Nicole Jones and the mother of Adams's alleged victim

Yesterday, Ms Jones announced via social media that she would be "standing down as president and all official club duties with immediate effect".

"I acknowledge that what I said [in the messages] was disrespectful, inappropriate and wrong, and I unreservedly apologise for these comments," she said.

In his statement, Mr Gutwein said the league was "deeply concerned" by the content of the private messages.

"The NTFA has referred the matter to the AFL for independent consideration and acknowledges that the President has unreservedly apologised for those comments and stood aside from all official club duties with immediate effect," he said.

"The NTFA recognises that individuals who report allegations of sexual violence must be treated with dignity, compassion and respect."

Adams had not re-committed to coaching Bracknell as of last month.

It is understood he has since been stood down from the role, and will be replaced.

World.title: ‘You’re gonna have to kill me’: Alleged MP attacker in earlier police stand-off
World.content:
Updated PoliticsFederalHaines attack ‘You’re gonna have to kill me’: Alleged MP attacker in earlier police stand-off Shelby Brooks and Isabel McMillan Updated October 24, 2026 — 9:20pm ,first published 11:01am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. New vision has emerged showing the moments before two police officers arrested Wangaratta man Brendan Nugent four years before he allegedly mowed down independent MP Helen Haines. The vision, obtained by Nine News, shows now 43-year-old Brendan Nugent in a previous altercation with police. Loading Captured in 2022, Nugent is seen in the video speaking with two police officers while holding a wooden garden stake. “Now you’re gonna have to shoot me,” he tells officers in the video.



“You’re gonna have to kill me.” As he becomes increasingly agitated, the officers spray him with capsicum spray before Tasering him. Brendan Nugent in a stand-off with police in 2022. Nine News Nugent, who was 39 at the time of the video, was taken to hospital for assessment, but no charges were laid following the incident. It comes after Haines’ condition was downgraded from critical to serious but stable, five days after she was struck by a car in an alleged intentional attack outside her office in north-east Victoria.



The Indi MP had been in a critical condition since she was injured on Monday afternoon, which ultimately resulted in surgeons amputating both her legs. She remains in The Alfred hospital in Melbourne, which confirmed on Saturday morning that her condition had improved. Helen Haines lost both her legs in the alleged attack. Jason Robins Phil Haines, her husband of 40 years, said on Wednesday that the road to recovery for the MP and her family would be long and difficult. “Her heart is huge – she is a very compassionate, caring, loving person, incredibly supportive of all around her,” Phil Haines said in his address. Helen Haines’ husband, Phil Haines, with Governor-General Sam Mostyn at The Alfred on Wednesday. Justin McManus



“And her mind – she has the sharpest intellect. She has always had the most intense desire to learn, to read, to synthesise and to understand what’s going on. Floral tributes outside Helen Haines’ office in Wangaratta this week. Jason Robins “We are grateful and thankful that, at this stage, both her heart and her mind are in good shape.” Helen Haines, 65, was allegedly struck multiple times by a white Toyota LandCruiser on Monday outside her office in Wangaratta about 3.35pm. Her husband was joined on Wednesday by Governor-General Sam Mostyn as he described his wife as a “fighter”.



“But we know she is a fighter. She is a determined person to do her best, with our support and love, to recover,” Phil Haines said. “And that is what we hope for.” Related Article Haines attack Haines pursues a political experiment – that decent people can disagree. Has this attack changed that? Helen Haines was retrieving items from the boot of her car on Murphy Street when witnesses saw a LandCruiser perform a sharp U-turn and ram Haines against her own vehicle. The LandCruiser then reversed and rammed her again. Brendan Nugent, 43, has been charged with dangerous driving causing injury, intentionally causing injury and a Commonwealth offence of causing harm to a Commonwealth public official. He appeared in Wangaratta Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday. Police allege the incident was targeted. Nugent, who remains in custody, has since been charged with additional counts for cultivating cannabis and possessing cannabis.

World.title: AFLW round 11: Bruising win for Geelong, top spot the reward; Lions maul St Kilda
World.content:
Geelong have secured an AFLW qualifying final at “our house” with a 30-point win that also put a massive hole in Fremantle’s top-eight hopes.

There could be major injury ramifications out of Saturday’s physical clash at GMHBA Stadium, which the Cats won 9.10 (64) to 5.4 (34).

Rachel Kearns of the Cats collides with Emma O’Driscoll of the Dockers on Saturday. AFL Photos via Getty Images

A heavy collision early in the last quarter put Geelong’s Rachel Kearns out of the game, while Fremantle player Noa McNaughton needed help from two trainers when she also went off in the final term with an ankle injury.

Geelong forward Chantal Mason suffered an ugly cut to her face in a marking contest. Fremantle’s Aoife Healy, Aisling McCarthy and Kiara Bowers, plus Cats player Aishling Moloney all needed injury treatment during the game.

Fremantle started the clash in eighth spot and dropped to 10th. They will host seventh-placed Sydney in the last game of round 12 next Sunday, with the finals starting the following weekend.

The Cats led by 48 points early in the final term, after coach Mick Stinear urged in their three-quarter time huddle to finish the job at “our house”.

It was their fourth home win in a 10-game streak overall that has shot them to second on the ladder. Their only blemish was the 73-point loss in round one to two-time defending premiers North Melbourne, who will most likely again finish the regular season on top of the ladder.

Dynamic midfield duo Georgie Prespakis and Nina Morrison starred for the Cats, while Dockers defender Emma O’Driscoll capped her excellent game with a stunning contested mark in the final quarter.
